For retained raw bytes so corrupt that the pinned decoder cannot form `StoredDigest`, a separately reviewed **cutover inventory** may record `RawCorruptDisposition`; it never asserts an origin, encoding, route or digest. Its codec is A6's `HX-EV-RAW-CORRUPT-1\0 || 02 || 0010` below, whose immutable source identity excludes the decision-time head and ETag; the pre-integration thirteen-field codec 01 is superseded and inadmissible. The provider source, capture and independently authenticated operator decision are read back and cross-checked against exact event key/scope/sequence/raw-byte hash before this record can close **inventory** for that one corrupt item. The disposition is immutable under create-once CAS; changed raw bytes, source identity or decision conflict, while a later valid append that changes the head or ETag does not (A6). It does not make the event readable, authorize a synthetic StoredDigest/V1 origin/route, permit Apply/handler, advance any checkpoint or silently acknowledge any delivery. Replay stops exactly there with typed `RawEnvelopeCorrupt` and last-good nonauthoritative state/checkpoint; subscriber poison acknowledgement still requires the separate AD-31 authenticated capture-before-ack rule. Missing capture, proof or approved decision holds cutover. Every valid retained event still requires full signed manifest, digest sidecar and origin evidence.

Every retained or newly written V1 event has exactly one immutable, event-storage-key-indexed origin record. Its canonical bytes are `HX-EV-V1-ORIGIN-1\0 || 01 || 0007` followed by tags `01` U event storage key, `02` U tenant, `03` U domain, `04` N sequence, `05` B32 raw-event SHA-256, `06` B32 original StoredDigest, `07` B origin branch. Tag `07` is exactly `B(01 || B32 actor-save-certificate hash || B32 PreSaveBundleHash)` for `new-writer`, with both hashes defined by A5, proving that raw event, purpose-06 encoding sidecar, stored-digest sidecar and result were staged and read back in the same actor save. For `retained-offline` it is exactly `B(02 || B32 independently signed migration-manifest digest || B32 reviewer-docket/decision hash || B32 authenticated source-evidence hash || B32 version-2 stored-digest-sidecar hash)`. Any other discriminator or branch length fails. The branch discriminator and fields are immutable under create-once CAS and included in authenticated raw readback. Exactly one branch must verify against the event key, raw bytes, sidecars and StoredDigest before source admission. A new V1 append uses branch `01` and never requires an offline manifest. Historical bytes cannot claim branch `01` without their actor commit certificate; an offline record cannot masquerade as an actor save. Missing, duplicated, swapped or conflicting origin evidence is `LegacyEvidenceConflict` and leaves the event unreadable pending reconciliation without rewriting it. The purpose-06 sidecar remains the exact historical ten-field signed format in §4; this origin record does not alter its claim bytes or the V17 literal fixture.

For new-writer branch `01`, the immutable pre-save intent certificate, `PreSaveBundleHash`, post-save purpose-11 provider receipt, their caps, the zero-event no-op binding and the retention of purpose-11 verification material are A5's codec-02 contract below, with A3's actor-evidence caps and A7's no-op rows. The pre-integration codec-01 certificate, bundle hash and receipt are superseded and inadmissible for new writes. A bundle hash alone, separate saves or provider inability to certify same-save atomicity is `ActorCommitEvidenceHold`, and old offline branch `02` never claims this certificate.

`MigrationAuthorityDigest = SHA256("HX-EV-MIGRATION-AUTHORITY-1\0" || 01 || u32 rowCount || sorted rows)`. Each row is `HX-EV-MIGRATION-AUTHORITY-ROW-1\0 || 01 || 0009` with ordered tags `01` U domain, `02` one-byte purpose (`0d` signer or `0e` independent reviewer), `03` U key ID, `04` B32 SHA-256 of exact SPKI bytes, `05` Q valid-from UTC, `06` Q valid-to UTC, `07` one-byte revocation state (`00` active, `01` revoked), `08` U stable permitted human/service identity, `09` B32 canonical signer/reviewer identity-policy/configuration hash. Sort rows by separately encoded domain, purpose and key-ID bytes in unsigned UTF-8 order; reject duplicate keys, unknown tags, invalid intervals and a signer/reviewer identity or key reused for both roles on one docket. The actual SPKI bytes and exact identity policy are retained alongside the digest and compared to each row before a manifest is admitted. Every reader and publisher that can validate migrated V1 advertises this 32-byte digest **beside** its active per-domain RegistryFingerprint and requires parity before mixed-reader cutover. It is not folded retroactively into the historical V17 RegistryFingerprint or purpose-06 signature. Rotate migration verification keys before signing under the new map, retain old map bytes and valid original intervals for open event/backup/rollback/delivery obligations, and hold source admission/readiness when the advertised digest, retained map or independently authenticated signer/reviewer identity differs.

### A4. Immutable bytes, preparation and migration branches

Import §4's exact `U`, `B`, `B32`, `N`, `I`, `T`, `Q`, `O`, `M`, strict raw JSON renderer, five-byte presence bitmap, derived protection record, options/default expansion and `StoredDigest` formulas. `T` retains original offset minutes; changing only offset changes consumed evidence. Absent/null/empty extension states remain distinct. The original provider bytes are retained verbatim, even when canonical spelling gives an equal digest. Decoder implementation/options/dependency behavior is pinned; a newer decoder cannot redefine an old digest. Provider encoding ID is authenticated original evidence, never the current provider's guessed ID. Caller-created DTO/proof values are inputs to verification and cannot establish authority.

Use §7's exact preparation identity/key and `AppendOperationFingerprint`; for a command `OperationId` is its **admitted execution** `CommandEnvelope.MessageId`, not an event ID or a retry submission ID. For an existing compatibility path without protected admission this is the initial submitted MessageId; that naming rule does not relax AD-5/AD-25 production admission or authorize an unfenced mutation. With an IdempotencyKey, `SubmitCommandHandler` must first obtain authenticated admission, compare the existing protected canonical command identity and obtain `ExecutionMessageId`, `ExecutionCorrelationId`, scope and original admitted input. These define the execution request (the same substitution the current handler makes, with IdempotencyKey removed before actor routing). A retry may submit different MessageId/correlation IDs while matching that protected identity; those transport identities neither change ScopeOpHash nor generate another capsule/pin. Original-input hash means the frozen **original admitted execution request**; never compare its full hash with a retry envelope containing changed transport IDs. Changed semantic payload/scope/other protected identity still conflicts under current admission rules. Recheck current caller authentication, tenant/command authorization and trusted-extension policy before returning any retained result; an old pin grants no access. Compare the canonical original execution request, addressed scope, selected mode/fingerprint and input hash on retry. Fence one `Preparing` owner before generating IDs, timestamp/offset, positions, protected bytes, signatures and bounded domain-result bytes. While still `Preparing`, finish A5 steps 1–5, including all control before/after images, absence evidence and derived certificate/origin bytes. Persist every exact capsule chunk and authenticate readback of its bytes/hash/order and complete manifest **before** CAS-publishing `Prepared`; authenticate that CAS before event-ID reservation, `Ready`, or actor save. No mutation needed by save/recovery may first be constructed after this boundary. Upfront estimate/reservation includes all A5 rows and A7/A8 retirement, complete publication-observation evidence and response capacity; A8 preflight must pass before `Prepared` or append. Missing retained bytes hold; they are never regenerated from current actor state, even when the record would hash identically. Lost preparation acknowledgement holds the same operation; no retry reruns a serializer, protector, clock, allocator or signer to manufacture a comparison result.

| Source | Mandatory evidence before evolved read / activation |
| --- | --- |
| New upgraded V1 | Same-save event, purpose-06 encoding sidecar, version-2 ten-field `HX-EV-STORED-EVIDENCE-1`, outbox, result, member-root and A5 certificate. Exact `HX-EV-V1-ORIGIN-1` branch `01` contains certificate hash and A5 pre-save bundle hash; verify separate post-save purpose-11 receipt. No offline manifest is required. |
| Valid retained V1 | Exact original raw provider bytes and uniquely proven historical encoding/decoder; §4's 26-field `HX-EV-V1-MIGRATION-1` record (64 KiB), dual independent purpose-0d/0e signed carrier (65 KiB), independently read-back reviewer docket, source evidence and version-2 digest sidecar, then purpose-06 encoding sidecar. Origin branch `02` binds manifest/docket/source/digest-sidecar hashes. The signer and reviewer keys/identities differ. |
| Raw-corrupt retained item | A6 source-specific disposition may close that item's cutover inventory only. It is unreadable and has no invented digest, encoding or origin. |
| New V2 | Same-save raw/encoding/digest/outbox/result/member-root/intent plus post-save provider receipt; no V1 origin. V2 still proves the complete save, although the §4 V1 origin codec is inapplicable. |

Retained manifest source kinds remain exactly `versioned-config`, `deployment-log`, `commit-log`, `actor-outbox`, `store-generation`. The independently authenticated interval must enclose the actual event commit or exact commit/generation identity must prove it; JSON appearance proves neither. Retain original source bytes, reviewer receipt, decoder executable/options/closure, signatures, exact trust maps and key intervals/revocation through readable lifetime plus backup, rollback, queue and incident-replay obligations. Missing/changed references or multiple possible encodings yield `LegacyEvidenceConflict` and readiness hold, preserving old bytes. CAS-create/readback only; never rewrite or overwrite conflicting historical evidence. Compare `MigrationAuthorityDigest` separately beside RegistryFingerprint across readers/publishers; do not fold it retroactively into a signed fixture.

### A5. Complete acyclic intent and post-save commit proof

This replaces the pre-integration §4 intended-record list and reconciles it with §7's member-root sidecar. New production intent, bundle and receipt use codec byte `02` under their existing separators; codec `01` examples are not evidence of this new complete-set contract. Purpose-06, V1-origin, append fingerprint, result-record, batch-root and member-root codecs stay unchanged. Every producer and verifier reference uses codec 02 together, including B2's authenticated raw-source admission.

Define `ScopeOpHash = SHA256(U tenant || U domain || U aggregateType || U aggregateId || U OperationId)`, lowercase hex when used in keys. Keys are actor-scoped and store/compare their full components to reject hash collision. The intent key is `actor-intent:` plus ScopeOpHash; member-root key is `batch-member-root:` plus ScopeOpHash. Events and existing actor keys keep their existing keys; encoding/digest/origin records use the exact event key plus `:encoding-evidence`, `:stored-digest-evidence`, `:v1-origin` respectively. Provider receipts are retrieved from a backend-owned committed-operation index by canonical backend identity, actor key, OperationId and committed generation, outside the save they certify.

For codec 02, an intended mutation row is `kind:byte || action:byte || U exactKey || O(B32 expectedBeforeHash) || O(B32 afterHash)`. Actions are `01` put, `02` delete. Absent expected-before means proven absence; a value hashes exact prior bytes. Put requires a value after-hash; delete requires absent after-hash. Explicit null is forbidden in either O. A put of identical bytes still appears if staged. All old-state checks occur under the actor save fence/CAS; a record-hash comparison outside that fence is insufficient. The list is `u32 count || rows`, sorted by unsigned UTF-8 exact-key bytes, with each physical key exactly once. Scope each key to this actor. A failed before-image comparison saves nothing only when the provider proves rejection under the fence and no future commit; it enters the terminal stale-preparation protocol below. It never licenses restaging an old domain result against a new actor version.

| Kind | Exact record category / cardinality |
| --- | --- |
| `01`, `02`, `03`, `04` | Raw event, encoding evidence, stored-digest evidence, outbox routing intent: exactly one of each per appended event, matched by sequence/key. |
| `05`, `06` | One immutable append/no-op result; one member-root sidecar for eventful batches and none for no-op. |
| `07`, `08`, `09` | Aggregate metadata; pipeline/idempotency checkpoint; publication recovery index. Include every put/delete actually made, with exact prior/post bytes. A no-op does not advance stream metadata. |
| `0a`, `0b`, `0c` | Snapshot/witness, trusted effect receipt, pending-count/recovery ownership. Include every actual mutation; no optional component may silently stage outside the list. |
| `0d` | Exactly one A7 immutable no-op checkpoint witness for no-op; absent for eventful save. |
| `7e`, `7f` | Derived intent certificate itself; V1 origin records. Excluded only from intended business rows to break the hash cycle, included in complete actual receipt/readback rows. Exactly one certificate; one origin per V1 event, none for V2/no-op. |

Unknown kinds fail writer readiness. Any future actor state category needs an explicitly reviewed codec/kind revision before use. This list includes control-state deletions, not just events. No-op compatibility terminal checkpoint/index/pending-count mutations are listed when they occur. The actor must seal its staged mutation set before save; comparison to the declared set rejects any extra/missing mutation. A hidden provider-internal storage row is not an application mutation, but the provider must attest atomic visibility of every listed application mutation under one generation.

The exact dependency order is below. Steps 1–5 run under the original fenced `Preparing` owner; “stage” there means prepare private proposed-save bytes, not save or authorize reservation. Alongside the existing hash codecs, the capsule retains every exact non-absent before-image and authenticated absence proof, every exact after-image, all derived certificate/origin bytes and their deterministic keys. Hash-only control rows are insufficient recovery evidence. The actor version/fence used to observe those images is pinned; a later mismatch follows AbortedStale, never reconstruction.

1. Prepare raw event, encoding/digest sidecars, outbox bytes and **domain-result payload bytes**; compute the unchanged AppendOperationFingerprint. In all member leaves `domain/append-result hash` means SHA-256 of those pre-rendered payload bytes (result-record tag `05`), never the hash of the later result **record**.
2. Build this specification's exact MemberLeaf/tree and six-field `HX-EV-BATCH-MEMBER-ROOT-1` from those values. For `n=1` root equals its leaf; for odd levels duplicate last child; 1..1,000 members only. The root sidecar contains fingerprint and payload hash, but no result-record, certificate or commit hash.
3. Form `CoreBundleBytes` as `u32 eventCount`, then for each sequence in ascending order `B raw || B encoding || B digest || B outbox`, then `B memberRootSidecar`. `CoreBundleHash = SHA256(CoreBundleBytes)`. This is the exact complete event/outbox/encoding/digest/member-root bundle for batch-root tag `08` and append-result tag `08`; it deliberately excludes the result record and derived certificate/origins. Build the unchanged eight-field append-result record with that hash and exact original result bytes. The no-op alternative builds A7's result then its witness, with no CoreBundle/member-root.
4. Finish every other business mutation under the actor fence, including snapshots/index/checkpoint/ownership rows. Let `ExactRows` be `u32 count || each (mutationRow || O(B exactAfterBytes))` in the same sorted order; after-bytes are present for put, absent for delete, and must match afterHash. `PreSaveBundleHash = SHA256("HX-EV-ACTOR-PRESAVE-BUNDLE-1\0" || 02 || B ExactRows)`. No origin, certificate, provider ETag or receipt enters this hash.
5. Encode `HX-EV-ACTOR-INTENT-1\0 || 02 || 0008` with unchanged field meanings/types: `01` U actor key, `02` U tenant, `03` U domain, `04` U aggregate type, `05` U aggregate ID, `06` U OperationId, `07` N proposed checked logical version, `08` B exact intended mutation list. Stage it. For each V1 event, stage unchanged origin branch `01` referencing SHA-256 of that certificate and PreSaveBundleHash. These derived records contain no self-hash. Their deterministic keys and bytes must verify before save.
6. Seal the complete staged set (business rows plus certificate/origins). Complete A4 encrypted chunk/manifest readback, then publish/read back `Prepared`; only afterward reserve event IDs and establish `Ready`. Before save, read/compare the retained complete set and pinned before-images under the save fence; lost bytes hold without regeneration. Perform one actor-owned atomic save under the checked expected actor version/fence. For eventful batches, the global reservation must already be `Ready` with every exact ordered ID reference read back. Neither a certificate nor a staged/co-stored receipt proves commitment.
7. After save, obtain the separately issued signed provider receipt `HX-EV-ACTOR-COMMIT-1\0 || 02 || 0009`: `01` U actor key, `02` U OperationId, `03` N actual logical version, `04` U backend identity, `05` B exact provider fence, `06` U resulting ETag, `07` N committed generation, `08` B32 certificate hash, `09` B complete actual mutation list in the v2 row codec. All intended rows must match exactly; the only additional rows are the exact derived `7e`/`7f` set. The receipt never lists itself. Sign through §6 purpose `11` with backend-bound provider authority after the save, never a domain/caller signer.
8. Authenticated provider readback under that committed generation compares **every put's exact bytes**, every delete's proven absence, before-image/CAS evidence, derived rows, actor version, backend, fence and actual ETag. Compute `ActorBundleReadbackHash = SHA256("HX-EV-ACTOR-BUNDLE-1\0" || 02 || B completeExactRows || U committedETag || N logicalVersion)`, with completeExactRows using ExactRows framing including derived rows. Compare the member root and all leaves once. Only then CAS the whole batch root `Ready→Committed` with this hash and immutable result key/hash, and read back that CAS before publication or a committed public outcome. A no-op follows A7 without an event root.

Retain exact certificate, receipt, complete mutation evidence, original purpose-11 SPKI/key interval/revocation/backend binding and verifier implementation/options for every open read, retry, backup, rollback or delivery obligation. Later actor saves may change live metadata/index keys; historical receipt verification uses the authenticated retained committed-generation images, while a fresh source read proves that the addressed immutable event/sidecars still match. It never requires today's actor head/ETag to equal the historical commit ETag. A provider unable to retain or authenticate historical exact images cannot advertise this contract. Its failure is `ActorCommitEvidenceHold`, not permission to accept a digest-only/current-cache substitute.

Lost acknowledgement, timeout or cancellation after save starts follows the same path with a bounded recovery token: clear/ignore staged cache, query the provider operation index, read back the complete generation and reconcile the global root. Full exact match proves committed; an unchanged prior generation **plus authenticated proof that no in-flight save can later commit** proves no commit. Partial, foreign, stale, missing, conflicting or unavailable evidence remains a hold with capsule/reservation retained. Never restage, rerun domain work, release IDs or return a new result while that uncertainty exists. A successful HTTP/save response without provider readback is also insufficient.

#### Proven-no-commit stale preparation

A changed actor version/head or before-image invalidates the prepared domain result as a candidate for a new save. Preserve its original bytes; never replace its logical version, sequences, generated values or signature to fit a newer head. Under the original operation fence, reconcile A5 first. A complete commit wins even if today's actor is newer. Partial/unknown/in-flight evidence stays `ActorCommitEvidenceHold`.

Only authenticated rejection/no-start evidence naming this operation, preparation hash, attempted fence and checked actor version, **plus a durable fence invalidation proving no delayed save can later commit**, permits `Prepared → AbortedStale`. The command admission owner CAS-publishes create-once `append-abort:` plus ScopeOpHash: `HX-EV-APPEND-ABORT-1\0 || 01 || 000a`, tags `01..05` U tenant/domain/aggregate type/aggregate ID/OperationId, `06` B32 preparation identity, `07` B32 exact original capsule manifest hash, `08` N expected actor logical version, `09` B32 authenticated no-future-commit proof hash, `0a` U reason exactly `stale-source`. Record and proof are each at most 64 KiB, reserved before preparation. Read back exact abort, authority, fence invalidation and absence of committed actor/root/pin before CAS-releasing all reserved ID references/root together. Uncertain release holds; never release one member as if the batch were partly aborted.

Retain the abort tombstone, original identity, no-future-commit proof and release receipts through all retry/backup/rollback obligations; reclaim encrypted chunks only after authenticated absence and retention decision as for A7. A repeat of this operation returns the same typed `AppendPreparationStale` precommit conflict; it does not rerun domain work, allocate again, or mint a committed-response pin. A fresh command requires a **new admitted execution identity** (and a new idempotency key where the old key binds the original execution), current source read/admission and a new domain invocation. This explicitly ends the old operation; no transparent same-operation re-admission is permitted. This terminal conflict is independently authorized by the proven abort and current access policy, not by A8's committed-response pin. If preparation never started, release instead requires affirmative durable admission/fence evidence of that state; missing records alone are not proof.

### A6. Raw-corrupt disposition without moving-head conflicts

The raw-corrupt disposition is `HX-EV-RAW-CORRUPT-1\0 || 02 || 0010` (16 fields), replacing the pre-integration thirteen-field codec. Tags `01..0d` retain the pre-integration encodings: U tenant/domain/aggregate type/aggregate ID/event key (`01..05`), N sequence (`06`), B32 exact raw hash (`07`), N observed head (`08`), U observed actor ETag (`09`), B32 exact authenticated observed raw-readback proof hash (`0a`), U AD-31 capture key (`0b`), B32 independently authenticated operator-decision hash (`0c`), Q decision UTC (`0d`). Append `0e` B exact §5 canonical backend descriptor, `0f` U immutable provider store-incarnation ID, `10` B32 SourceIdentityHash. At most 64 KiB, checked before field allocation. A store-incarnation is an authenticated stable generation/restore identity, not a mutable actor ETag or a friendly store name.

`SourceIdentityHash = SHA256("HX-EV-CORRUPT-SOURCE-1\0" || 01 || B backendDescriptor || U storeIncarnation || U tenant || U domain || U aggregateType || U aggregateId || U eventKey || N sequence || B32 rawHash)`. The create-once key is `raw-corrupt-disposition:` plus lowercase SHA-256 of the same input **without final rawHash**. Retain and compare all key components; changed bytes at an existing key cause a conflict instead of creating a second disposition. The operator-approved decision must bind SourceIdentityHash, reason, exact capture key/hash and decision time. AD-31 capture must authenticate the exact original bytes/scope/hash; no caller-provided hash can stand in for that capture.

The original head/ETag/proof are immutable **observations at decision time**, retained and verified as historical proof. On every later use, obtain a fresh authenticated source proof for the same backend incarnation, addressed event key, sequence and exact raw bytes; require current head to cover the sequence and a valid current provider fence. Independently verify the original capture/decision and current source identity. A new valid head/ETag/readback signature caused by appending a later event is accepted when SourceIdentityHash and decision are unchanged. Do not compare fresh proof hash or actor ETag for equality with tags `09`/`0a`. Historical proof validity under its retained interval and fresh current proof validity are separate checks.

Changed raw bytes, key/scope, store incarnation or approved decision are `LegacyEvidenceConflict`; unverifiable/stale fresh proof, missing capture/decision or unreadable historical authority is a readiness hold (`RawSourceUnavailable` where appropriate). A restore/backend move needs an independently approved source migration, not automatic acceptance based on equal JSON. Corruption disposition closes inventory for this one item only: replay stops there with `RawEnvelopeCorrupt`, no invented StoredDigest, no Apply/handler/checkpoint advancement and no silent subscription acknowledgement. AD-31 capture-before-ack remains separately necessary. Valid later events may append under their normal writer gate; they do not make the corrupt prefix readable.

## 5. Registry and compatibility fingerprints

Each deployment computes `RegistryFingerprint = SHA256("HX-EV-REGISTRY-1\0" || 01 || u32 row-count || sorted rows)` for one domain. Row order is one-byte record tag then separately encoded primary-key components compared as unsigned UTF-8 bytes or big-endian numeric version; duplicate primary keys and tags fail. In the table, comma order assigns **field tags `01`, `02`, ... exactly**, each followed by its declared scalar; `H` means B32 SHA-256 of exact implementation assembly-file bytes or canonical options bytes, never a display version. Primary keys precede u16 field count and are not repeated in that count.

| Row tag / primary key encoding | Exact fields in tag order; count |
| --- | --- |
| `44` D: U domain, U canonical type | `U aggregateRouteId`, `I currentVersion`, `U current CLR assembly-qualified type`, `H current type assembly`, `U Apply implementation ID`, `H Apply assembly`, `I state schema version`, `B state schema descriptor`, `U state serializer ID`, `H state serializer assembly`, `H state serializer options`, `H StateSchemaApplyHash`; 12. All D rows of one aggregate route agree on state/Apply fields. |
| `56` V: U domain, U canonical type, I version | `U schema validator ID`, `H validator assembly`, `H validator options`, `U serializer ID`, `H serializer assembly`, `H serializer options`, `U exact format`, `U identity policy ID`, `H identity extractor assembly`, `H identity options`; 10. |
| `41` A: U domain, U exact alias | `U canonical type`, `I source version`, `U source format`, `U source serializer ID`, `H source serializer assembly`, `H source serializer options`, `U alias validator ID`, `H alias validator assembly`, `H alias validator options`, `U identity policy ID`, `H identity extractor assembly`, `H identity options`, `U V1 unknown-member decoder ID`, `H decoder assembly`, `H decoder options`; 15. An alias with no unknown members uses a registered fixed no-op decoder, never an omitted field. |
| `45` E: U domain, U canonical type, I source version | `I target version` (exactly source+1), `U input format`, `U output format`, `U serializer ID`, `H serializer assembly`, `H serializer options`, `U upcaster ID`, `H upcaster assembly`, `H upcaster options`, `U edge identity policy ID`, `H edge identity assembly`, `H edge identity options`; 12. |
| `46` F: U domain, U canonical type, U write alias | `I current version`, `I source version`, `B current schema descriptor`, `B source schema descriptor`, `U input format`, `U output format`, `U downserializer ID`, `H downserializer assembly`, `H downserializer options`, `U identity validator ID`, `H identity validator assembly`, `H identity validator options`, `U semantic validator ID`, `H semantic validator assembly`, `H semantic validator options`; 15. |
| `53` S: U domain, O(U) empty component | `H TrustMapDigest`, `U raw envelope validator ID`, `H validator assembly`, `H validator options`, `U chain executor ID`, `H executor assembly`, `H executor options`, `U JSON serializer ID`, `H serializer assembly`, `H serializer options`, `U bounded raw reader ID`, `H reader assembly`, `H reader options`, `U protection reader ID`, `H protection reader assembly`, `H protection reader options`, `U attestation verifier ID`, `H verifier assembly`, `H verifier options`, `U signer ID`, `H signer assembly`, `H signer options`, `U publisher ID`, `H publisher assembly`, `H publisher options`, `U marker/reservation protocol ID`, `H protocol assembly`, `H protocol options`, `U raw renderer implementation ID`, `H renderer assembly`, `H renderer options`; 31. The appended renderer fields are tags `1d..1f`; existing S tags remain unchanged. |

Every assembly-file H in D/V/A/E/F/S and every handler, registration-adapter, filter, effect-receipt-provider and readback-codec H in the consumer catalog is the hash of the named direct file. A shared sealed per-domain deployment dependency-closure manifest adds one G record for every transitively loadable managed assembly or native library that can affect those implementations, even when another descriptor also names that file directly; deduplicate by exact `(domain, logical load identity, dependency kind)`. The root set includes D/V/A/E/F/S plus every cataloged handler, verified or legacy registration adapter, filter, effect receipt provider and readback codec. The gateway-owned per-domain deployment capability record pins the same sealed manifest bytes and RegistryFingerprint for all serving peers, even when one process does not locally instantiate a cataloged route. Each process verifies exact bytes and closure of every root it executes; for nonlocal rows it compares the complete canonical row bytes to that pinned capability record, and the endpoint that executes each handler proves its local bytes match those same rows. A missing locally executable dependency, absent manifest attestation or mismatched bytes blocks capability instead of producing a narrower RegistryFingerprint. The same sorted G rows enter RegistryFingerprint and the affected route-specific HandlerCompatibilityHash or EventTransformHash subset; a handler-only G row need not enter an unrelated aggregate transform. G has row tag `47`, primary key `U domain || U logical load identity || U dependency kind` (kind exactly `managed` or `native`), u16 count `0003`, tags `01` U resolved version/ABI identity, `02` B32 SHA-256 of exact dependency file bytes, `03` U deterministic loader context ID. Sort G with other registry rows by tag/key bytes. The manifest is generated from the actual resolved load graph and locked at startup; verify every file's bytes and graph edges, reject duplicate logical identities, unresolved/dynamic reflection loads, unmanifested native loads and any newly loaded implementation dependency until a new fingerprint is published. Runtime and framework dependencies that influence validation, serialization, Apply, protection, signing or marker behavior are included. `EventTransformHash` appends only G rows reachable from its applicable D/V/A/E/S-read/protection implementation roots, and its row count includes them; `HandlerCompatibilityHash` appends only G rows reachable from that route/filter/readback roots after the selected filter rows, with a u32 G-row count even when zero. A fixture whose implementations and all relevant dependencies are the one literal `fixture-assembly\n` has no additional G rows and retains the hashes below. Thus peers with different transitive behavior cannot advertise one registry or semantic hash. S has **31** fields as enumerated; optional empty key is encoded `00`, never an ambiguous concatenated tuple. All hash inputs use exact file bytes/configured canonical option bytes; missing files/options block readiness. `TrustMapDigest` is `SHA256("HX-EV-TRUST-1\0" || 01 || u32 count || rows)`. Sort rows by separately encoded `(domain,purpose,key ID)`; each row is tag `4b`, `U domain`, one-byte purpose, `U key ID`, u16 field count `0006`, then tags `01` B32 SPKI SHA-256, `02` Q valid-from, `03` Q valid-to, `04` byte revocation (00 active/01 revoked), `05` U signer algorithm (`ECDSA-P256-SHA256-P1363`), `06` H signer options. Unknown, duplicate or malformed tags/keys fail. Key ID is ASCII lowercase kebab case 1–64; trust lookup is scoped to domain and purpose. Signer/trust changes alter RegistryFingerprint and require verifier-first transition, but do not change read-state semantic hash by themselves.

A domain registry and consumer-handler catalog are each admitted only after checked preallocation accounting: every encoded row is at most **64 KiB**, one domain manifest has at most **65,536 rows** and **64 MiB total encoded bytes**, including names, options, selected G closure, framing and sort workspace. A row's referenced option/dependency bytes must have immutable, bounded content-addressed storage and count toward that manifest's charged closure; unresolved or dynamic dependency graphs fail readiness. Parse, sort and hash through bounded streaming or charged scratch; never materialize an unbounded whole graph. `RegistryLimit` is the typed startup/readiness result for count, byte or row overflow. The same limits apply to route/filter/capability rows before either RegistryFingerprint or HandlerCatalogFingerprint is advertised. The existing fixture-only zero-additional-G-row V17 manifest remains byte-for-byte unchanged.

`StateSchemaApplyHash = SHA256("HX-EV-STATE-APPLY-1\0" || 01 || U aggregateRouteId || I state schema version || B descriptor || U state serializer ID || H serializer assembly || H serializer options || U Apply ID || H Apply assembly)`. `EventTransformHash = SHA256("HX-EV-TRANSFORM-1\0" || 01 || U domain || U aggregateRouteId || u32 row-count || sorted applicable D/V/A/E rows || B32 StateSchemaApplyHash || S-read || protection-adapter record || sorted selected G rows)`, where row-count is **the applicable D/V/A/E count plus two plus selected G count**. The G rows occur exactly once, immediately after the protection-adapter record, sorted by their separately encoded primary key `(domain, logical load identity, dependency kind)` in unsigned byte order; no G bytes are interleaved with D/V/A/E or placed before the fixed state hash. The state hash is a fixed scalar, not a row. A peer or fixture verifier MUST reject a row count that does not equal the number of D/V/A/E, S-read, protection-adapter and G row byte strings actually concatenated. Applicable rows are selected from the immutable manifest-admitted source types/versions reachable on that aggregate route, independent of each peer's observed corpus or retention state; write-only F is excluded unless historical output is an admitted A alias, in which case A/V/E already bind read behavior. `S-read` is tag `73`, codec `01`, u16 count `0012`, fields `01..0f`: S raw validator ID/assembly/options, chain executor ID/assembly/options, JSON serializer ID/assembly/options, bounded reader ID/assembly/options, protection reader ID/assembly/options, each with the same U/H types as S; appended fields `10..12` are raw renderer implementation ID U, renderer assembly H and renderer options H. Existing S-read tags retain their meanings. Protection adapter record is tag `70`, codec `01`, count `0003`, tags `01` U implementation ID, `02` H assembly, `03` H options. No trust, signer, verifier, publisher, marker or handler-only field enters this semantic hash. Changing a read implementation invalidates compatible folded state; key rotation alone does not.

Consumer `HandlerCatalogFingerprint = SHA256("HX-EV-HANDLERS-1\0" || 01 || u32 count || sorted rows)`, separate from the shared domain registry. Route primary key is **`(domain, HandlerRouteId)`**, unique within domain, stable under CLR rename. Route row tag `52`, keys U domain/U route ID, u16 count `0012`, tags `01..12`: U canonical type, U topic, U tenant-scope rule, U handler implementation ID, H handler assembly, H handler config, U effect mode, U effect contract ID, H effect options, I checkpoint state schema version, B checkpoint descriptor, U state serializer ID, H serializer assembly, H serializer options, U readback codec ID, H readback assembly, H readback options, U state store ID. Filter row tag `4c`, key U domain/U filter ID, count `0007`, tags `01..07`: U exact domain predicate, U exact topic predicate, U exact canonical type predicate, U exact tenant-scope rule, U implementation ID, H assembly, H config. Predicates are catalog literals or the one frozen tenant-scope wildcard rule; reject overlapping or ambiguous selectors, never evaluate arbitrary runtime code for hash selection. A verified handler has exactly one additional capability row tag `43`, primary key U domain/U route ID, u16 count `000c`, tags `01..0c`: U route kind (exact `projection` or `subscription`), U projection type (empty for subscription), U canonical current type, I current payload version, U current CLR handler assembly-qualified type (internal only), U DI registration implementation ID, H registration assembly, H registration options, U effect mode (exact `AtomicStore` or `ProviderIdempotency`), U receipt provider ID, H receipt provider assembly, H receipt provider options. A `43` row without its matching `52` route row, a second `43` key, mismatched canonical type/effect mode, missing receipt probe or a current version other than the D descriptor fails startup. The catalog sort includes `43` by tag/key; a route with no `43` row is legacy-only and cannot claim verified current-event capability. `HandlerCompatibilityHash = SHA256("HX-EV-HANDLER-ROUTE-1\0" || 01 || exact route row || u32 selected filter-count || selected filter rows sorted by filter ID || u32 selected G-row count || selected G rows sorted by primary key || selected capability row if present)`. This preserves the existing no-capability-row preimage, including the signed V17 fixture; a verified route appends its one exact self-delimiting `43` row after G. Select only filters whose literal domain/topic/type and tenant-scope rule name that route, and only the capability row with the same domain/route key; unrelated handler/filter changes cannot invalidate its checkpoint. The selected G closure includes the route handler, verified or legacy registration adapter, selected filter implementation, effect receipt provider, state serializer and readback codec dependencies, plus the capability row's registration and receipt provider dependencies. Select these from the identical shared G rows bound by RegistryFingerprint; duplicate rows are never reencoded with another key or hash. Whole catalog fingerprint remains deployment inventory. Route rename needs explicit marker/effect migration; old key interpretation is retained until proven safe.

Production `52` route tag `06` handler-config bytes and tag `11` readback-codec options MUST each bind the same canonical state-backend identity descriptor `(providerKind, backendInstanceOrClusterId, namespace, endpointConfigurationDigest, storeId)`. Encode it as `HX-EV-STATE-BACKEND-1\0 || 01 || U providerKind || U backendInstanceOrClusterId || U namespace || B32 endpointConfigurationDigest || U storeId`, with nonempty identifiers, strict UTF-8 and no trailing bytes; include those exact bytes in the canonical configuration manifests before their H values are calculated. The provider's authenticated readback reports the same five values and the gateway compares them before checkpoint signing or reuse. Since `HandlerCompatibilityHash` binds the `52` row/config and purpose-04 binds that hash plus state-store ID, an equal friendly name or equal state bytes on another backend cannot authorize reuse. A backend move changes the hash and requires authenticated migration or rebuild. The unchanged V17 literal `store` is a declared **test-local** backend in its existing fixture handler config/options and retains the fixture preimage; production configuration cannot use that shorthand and must provide the full descriptor. No checkpoint claim tag or V17 fixture byte changes.

A projection route declares a nonempty, unique set of current `(canonical event type, PayloadVersion, SerializationFormat)` capabilities. Its existing `52` route row remains the **primary** type; the primary version and format are the current V descriptor for that type in the active domain registry. An extra capability is the self-delimiting row tag `58`, primary key `U domain || U HandlerRouteId || U canonical event type || I current payload version || U current format`, followed by u16 field count `0000`; sort extra rows by those separately encoded unsigned key bytes. Every extra type must resolve to exactly one current D/V descriptor with that version/format, differ from the primary triple and every other extra row, and belong to the route's domain. The `43` verified capability row still describes the primary entry; extra rows share its handler/effect/registration contract. Include each `58` in `HandlerCatalogFingerprint`'s sorted row count and append this route's sorted extra rows after its optional `43` row in `HandlerCompatibilityHash`. With zero extras append **no** count, marker or bytes, preserving the exact V17 no-extra-type preimage. `EventRouteCapability` is an additive immutable record with exactly `EventContractType:string`, `PayloadVersion:int` and `SerializationFormat:string`; its three values are validated against the active D/V current descriptor. The existing single-type `AddVerifiedDomainProjectionHandler` registration delegates to an additive overload accepting a nonempty immutable `IReadOnlyList<EventRouteCapability>`; its primary entry is the old argument and the rest are these extra rows. Registration and discovery attest the whole set and reject overlap/ambiguity. For every event on every live, retry, history, reconciliation and shared-rebuild page, validate its verified effective `(type, version, format)` against the selected route set **before** Apply, handler invocation, history fingerprint or checkpoint. One unmatched event yields `HandlerCapabilityMismatch` with no partial handler result or checkpoint advance. A multi-type route never treats its primary type as permission to skip another page event.

A production named-projection key-space declaration is a catalog capability row tag `59`, primary key `U domain || U HandlerRouteId || U keySpaceId`, followed by u16 field count `0005` and ascending tags: `01` U exact logical-key prefix, `02` U ownership mode (only `aggregate` or `shared`), `03` U state store ID, `04` B exact §5 canonical state-backend descriptor, `05` H canonical declaration/configuration options manifest. The prefix is nonempty strict UTF-8; it selects all and only keys beginning with those exact bytes. Equal or prefix-overlapping declarations in the same `(tenant, domain, store ID)` across any route fail startup; declaration changes cannot silently reinterpret an existing key. Include every `59` row in the sorted `HandlerCatalogFingerprint` count and append that route's sorted `59` rows after its optional `43` and any `58` rows in `HandlerCompatibilityHash`, including the selected declaration implementation/configuration and transitive G dependency rows in the hash's selected closure. A route with no declared key-space appends no row/count/marker and preserves the V17 literal preimage. A changed prefix, key-space ID, ownership mode, backend or dependency requires authenticated migration of all retained roots/checkpoints or a complete fenced rebuild before the route is current; a prior checkpoint hash alone never authorizes the new ownership interpretation.

### B8. Read semantics, attestation refresh and rollback

**BH37-10 (§11.5).** The contradictory historical Loop-11 sentence is replaced by this rule: **A write-only F change does not, by itself, invalidate folded state or force semantic replay/rebuild. It changes RegistryFingerprint and therefore invalidates transient old-fingerprint route/prefix/continuation proof. Refresh that evidence through authenticated source admission; restart a paged operation from page 1 when its transient proof is stale.** Operation restart may perform replay work, but it is not proof that unchanged state semantics became incompatible.

The exact §5 distinction is retained: EventTransformHash includes applicable D/V/A/E, StateSchemaApplyHash, S-read/protection and selected read dependency closure; it excludes write-only F, signer/trust/publisher and handler-only fields. An F dependency that is also reachable from a read root is **not write-only**, and changing it changes the read hash. HandlerCompatibilityHash includes selected handler/filter/registration/effect/readback/backend/key-space/mode capability and dependencies; HandlerCatalogFingerprint inventories all routes. StoredDigest/raw/protection evidence never changes merely because any current fingerprint changes.

| Change | Required state and proof action |
| --- | --- |
| F implementation/options or F-only dependencies; identical applicable A/V/E and read/Apply state hashes | Preserve semantically compatible witnessed snapshot/checkpoint after durable source/state verification. Acquire new current route/prefix proof; stale continuation restarts page 1. Do not relabel an old final proof as current or rewrite pinned bytes. |
| Read alias/schema/serializer/upcaster/protection/read dependency, StateSchemaApplyHash, or affected handler/backend/key-space/fold-mode change | Old state cannot become Current by re-signing. Full authenticated replay/rebuild or separately approved migration, with new state/readback and proof; keep old immutable authority for its remaining obligations. |
| Signer/trust rotation only | Verifier-first capability/parity transition and fresh transient proof; no semantic state invalidation by itself. Historic checkpoint/delivery/encoding/provider keys verify only exact retained obligations and original intervals; revocation is not overridden. |
| V1-only or old effective-view/codec/mode endpoint after V2/hopped history or v2 page transcript exists | Fence routing before Apply. `RollbackReaderCapabilityHold` if no capable endpoint; retain work and old/new evidence. Downgrade cannot reinterpret new metadata or omit timeline binding. |

A stale-proof refresh can verify unchanged state through its durable witness/compatible hash and issue fresh transient source evidence without rerunning domain Apply; when that evidence cannot be established, perform authenticated replay or hold. There is no promise of zero source-read cost on registry rotation. Keep A5 historic provider receipts/complete images and A6 original corruption observations separate from fresh head/ETag. Neither historical evidence nor a current signer substitutes for the other. C6 includes all these capability, key retention and rollback requirements in activation; this section grants no activation authority.

### 5.1 Integration rule for row tags

[I-04] Record tags are unique across the registry, catalog and semantic-hash codecs. The registry rows are `44` D, `56` V, `41` A, `45` E, `46` F, `53` S and `47` G, and the trust row is `4b`. The catalog rows are `52` route, `4c` filter, `43` verified capability, `58` extra event-type capability, `59` key-space declaration, `5a` fold mode (B7) and `5b` query route (B7c). The semantic-hash records are `73` S-read and `70` protection adapter. No other tag is admitted, and a new row kind requires an approved amendment of this document. `5a` and `5b` rows follow the same append-only-when-present rule as `43`, `58` and `59`: a route or domain without them contributes no count, marker or bytes, so every historical fixture preimage is unchanged.

## 6. Signed route, prefix, checkpoint and command evidence

Signatures use ECDSA P-256/SHA-256, fixed 64-byte IEEE P1363, exact SPKI trust map and no alternate encoding. Signature input is `"HX-EV-SIG-1\0" || 01 || one-byte purpose || 01+U keyID || 02+B claim`; purpose `01` route, `02` delivery, `03` complete prefix, `04` checkpoint, `05` command continuation, `06` immutable provider-encoding evidence, `07` completed command state, `08` broker membership, `09` consumer lease, `0a` broker publication fence, `0b` external route capability manifest, `0c` provider duplicate-probe transcript. Purposes `08..0b` use the separately configured broker/component authority trust map in §7; purpose `0c` uses the separately pinned provider receipt-attestation authority and is valid only for the exact backend/configuration revision in the V3 probe; purposes `0d` and `0e` use separate offline migration and independent reviewer trust maps over the same §4 MigrationDigest; purpose `0f` is the route/key-space scoped named-maintenance authority under the current domain key and fingerprint; purpose `10` is the trusted provider raw-readback claim and purpose `11` is its actor atomic-commit/readback receipt under a separately configured backend-bound provider trust anchor. Neither provider purpose authorizes a caller-constructed source, event route, delivery or command state. Purposes `12` through `2c` are assigned by B4b and C1–C5, and [I-05] (§6.1) is the complete purpose assignment. Purpose 07 is transient and requires the current active domain key/fingerprint; command-serving domains register its key in `TrustMapDigest`. Claim encoding starts its named separator, codec `01`, u16 field count, then tags `01..N` in table order. Reject missing, extra, duplicate, out-of-order tags. Verify purpose and domain for every claim; route, prefix and continuation require the current active key/fingerprint, while only exact delivery-pin, checkpoint and immutable encoding-sidecar obligations may verify an approved prior fingerprint and original signing interval. Route and complete-prefix claims are transient. They authorize state only while their signature verifies under the **current active domain key and RegistryFingerprint** at verification time; rotation or expiry requires authenticated source replay and new current-key claims, not a historic obligation. Purpose-05 continuation has signed issued/expiry UTC and is similarly invalid under a no-longer-current key/fingerprint, requiring replay from page 1. Purpose-02 delivery pins, purpose-04 checkpoint attestations and purpose-06 encoding sidecars have separate exact durable historic obligations and narrowly scoped expired-key rules; an old sidecar key verifies only its original immutable claim/raw-byte binding, never a new route or prefix. A route claim is capped at **1 MiB encoded** and streamed/charged before allocation, accommodating admitted metadata up to the 512 KiB per-event ceiling; historical larger cases hold readiness for separately approved offline evidence migration, never truncate/poison solely for a new proof cap.

| Claim separator / count | Tags `01..N` and exact scalar types |
| --- | --- |
| `HX-EV-ROUTE-1\0` / 18 | B32 StoredDigest; U tenant; U domain; U aggregate ID; U aggregate type; N sequence; U MessageId; U stored event type name; I stored metadata version; O(U) stored canonical type; O(I) stored payload version; U stored format; U target canonical type; I target version; B32 RegistryFingerprint; B32 effective-payload SHA-256; U effective format; B32 consumed-metadata hash. |
| `HX-EV-DELIVERY-CLAIM-1\0` / 10 | B32 StoredDigest; B32 DeliveryDigest; U tenant; U domain; U aggregate ID; U aggregate type; N sequence; U MessageId; B32 RegistryFingerprint; Q signed issuance UTC. |
| `HX-EV-PREFIX-1\0` / 15 | U tenant; U domain; U aggregate ID; U aggregate type; N start; N end; N admitted head; N target; I count; B32 OrderedDigestListHash; B32 cumulative accumulator; B32 RegistryFingerprint; O(B32 checkpoint anchor hash); O(B32 SnapshotDigest); O(B32 snapshot-prefix accumulator). Tags `0e` and `0f` are appended; existing tags retain their meaning. |
| `HX-EV-CHECKPOINT-1\0` / 18 | U tenant; U domain; U aggregate ID; U aggregate type; U projection route; N completed sequence; B32 accumulator; B32 body hash; B32 StateCheckpointReadbackHash; B32 EventTransformHash; B32 HandlerCompatibilityHash; B32 RegistryFingerprint; U readback ETag for legacy single-state, or the pre-reserved logical state version for production named root; Q signed issuance UTC; U fence coordinator ID; N monotonic fence generation; U state operation ID; U state commit version/ETag (the same pre-reserved logical version for named root). The actual named-root final-pointer ETag is bound only in the provider-issued final-pointer commit receipt after pointer acceptance. |
| `HX-EV-COMMAND-CONT-1\0` / 16 | U tenant; U domain; U aggregate ID; U aggregate type; U stream key; N fixed expected head; N fixed target; N next sequence; B32 RegistryFingerprint; B32 EventTransformHash; B32 cumulative prior-prefix accumulator; U operation ID; Q issued UTC; Q expires UTC; B 16-byte nonce; B32 cumulative effective-event chain. Tag `10` is appended and is mandatory for every newly issued purpose-05 token. |
| `HX-EV-COMMAND-STATE-1\0` / 17 | U tenant; U domain; U aggregate ID; U aggregate type; U stream key; N fixed expected head; N target; B32 RegistryFingerprint; B32 EventTransformHash; B32 StateSchemaApplyHash; B32 final prefix accumulator; B32 SHA-256 of exact final `EventEvolutionProof` container; B32 SHA-256 of canonical final state bytes; O(B32) witnessed SnapshotDigest; B32 effective-event chain hash; O(U) completed replay operation ID; B32 completed page-transcript hash. Tag `11` is appended and binds all prior admitted pages through the durable operation result; for an operation selected under B4b it is the transcript-v2 terminal hash. |

The command-state proof container is `HX-EV-COMMAND-STATE-PROOF-1\0 || 01 || B(exact purpose-07 command-state claim) || U(key ID) || B(exact 64-byte P1363 signature) || B(exact final EventEvolutionProof container)` with a 2 MiB total cap and no trailing bytes. Its effective-event chain starts `SHA256("HX-EV-COMMAND-EFFECTIVE-1\0" || 01 || U tenant || U domain || U aggregate ID || U aggregate type || N target)` and advances in sequence order as `SHA256("HX-EV-COMMAND-EFFECTIVE-STEP-1\0" || prior B32 || N sequence || B32 StoredDigest || U effective type || I effective version || U effective format || B32 SHA-256(effective payload))`; a witnessed snapshot seed starts after its covered sequence, while full replay starts at 1. An empty chain uses the genesis. The router checks purpose-07 signature/current key, addressed command route and immutable actor head/target, final prefix signature/accumulator and canonical final-state bytes digest. For a one-page request it recomputes the effective chain and page transcript directly from every `verifiedEffectiveEvents` entry and purpose-01 route. For a completed multi-page operation it retrieves the immutable completed ledger/result, verifies every persisted page transition and proof hash under the same operation ID, checks the terminal stored accumulator, effective chain and page transcript against purpose-07 tags `0b`, `0f` and `11`, and checks final page entries directly. A final-page DTO alone never asserts prior pages. A page or continuation token alone is never a completed command state proof. On long streams, `POST /replay-state/pages` produces a completed, privately retained final state and final proof under `operationId`; the command claim binds their hashes and operation ID. The router retrieves that finalized state from the durable operation result, checks completion and hashes, and passes only verified typed state to the processor. A missing or expired result restarts authenticated replay at page 1. On a bounded old request lacking proof, the gateway performs authenticated actor-source lookup and constructs this carrier/proof before invocation; unavailable or conflicting source fails `CommandStateUnproven`. The lookup is keyed by exact scope, stream key, expected head and target; it uses bounded raw actor pages/readback and signs only after a complete prefix reaches target. The domain router can repeat that lookup over its mutually authenticated trusted gateway channel but never accepts free client state. Final state bytes use the registered canonical state serializer and §8 state budget. Empty head=target=0 requires the signed empty prefix and canonical empty-state hash.

`ConsumedMetadataHash = SHA256("HX-EV-CONSUMED-1\0" || 01 || N globalPosition || T timestamp || U correlationId || O(U) causationId || O(U) userId || O(U) DomainServiceVersion || U EventTypeName || U SerializationFormat || I MetadataVersion || O(U) canonical type || O(I) payload version || B32 StoredDigest)`. Route receiver compares **every** consumed DTO scope/target/stored/effective field and this hash to signed claim and authenticated source, and recomputes effective payload hash. A changed/missing attestation triggers source lookup, never direct Apply. Both metadata and payload retain the original timestamp offset; equal instants with different offsets have different evidence.

`OrderedDigestListHash = SHA256("HX-EV-PREFIX-LIST-1\0" || 01 || u32 count || each (N sequence || B32 StoredDigest))`. Check contiguous sequence, count, start/end/head/target and exact per-event route claim order before Apply. `EventEvolutionProof` contains an ordered bounded route claim/signature/key-ID entry **for each event**, one prefix claim/signature/key ID and optional checkpoint claim/signature/key ID, with no unmatched/duplicate entries. Up to 256 events, each route claim at most 1 MiB, page proof at most **64 MiB** charged before allocation; command page proof has stricter **2 MiB** and must use smaller page count when claims are large. Single-event proof is a one-entry list. Empty prefix is start 1/end 0/head 0/target 0/count 0, list hash over count zero, signed scope/fingerprint and no anchor; nonempty head with empty prefix fails except the two exact witnessed zero-tail forms below and, for transcript-v2 operations, B3's empty-target prefix (start 1/end 0/target 0/count 0 under an authenticated head above zero, with no anchors or routes).

The exact `EventEvolutionProof` container is `HX-EV-PROOF-1\0 || 01 || u32 route-count || route entries || one prefix entry || one-byte checkpoint discriminator || optional checkpoint entry`. Each entry is `B(exact signed claim bytes) || U(key ID) || B(exact 64-byte P1363 signature)` with no extra tags. Route entries are in strictly increasing contiguous sequence order and route-count equals the event count in the associated page; zero routes are valid only for signed empty-stream, B3 empty-target, witnessed snapshot zero-tail or checkpoint-anchored **projection** zero-tail forms. The prefix entry is mandatory and unique. The discriminator is `00` for no checkpoint and `01` followed by exactly one checkpoint entry; all other values fail. Decode length/count and aggregate 64 MiB proof limit (2 MiB for command pages) **before** allocating claim or entry buffers, then reject trailing bytes, duplicate sequence, unmatched route, wrong purpose/key, invalid signature, scope/head/fingerprint disagreement and a prefix count/order mismatch. Snapshot tags remain only in the prefix claim; they are not checkpoint entries. `/replay-state/pages`, command replay and aggregate reconstruction reject checkpoint discriminator `01` and prefix checkpoint anchor tag `0d`; only projection delivery/completion admits those forms after verifying its projection route and durable state. `CheckpointAnchorHash = SHA256("HX-EV-CHECKPOINT-ANCHOR-1\0" || 01 || B(exact checkpoint claim bytes) || U(key ID) || B(exact 64-byte signature))`. Prefix tag `0d`, when present, must equal this hash of the container's verified checkpoint entry. That entry must name the same scope and projection route, its completed sequence must be exactly page start minus one **only when completed sequence is below `long.MaxValue`**; the terminal count-zero sentinel below compares equal instead. Its accumulator, immutable state-version pointer/readback and active trust/fingerprint must verify before tail Apply. An absent anchor on a projection tail forces full rebuild from sequence 1; an invalid anchor never authorizes partial state. Before a projection page is signed or dispatched, the gateway measures its exact route entries, prefix/anchor carrier, stored DTOs and copied effective-view buffers against both the 64 MiB proof cap and the §8 combined 128 MiB live-scratch cap. If a candidate of at most 256 contiguous events does not fit, it reduces the event count, recomputes the ordered digest list, accumulator, end/count and **new signed complete-prefix claim** for that smaller contiguous range, and retries admission from the same checkpoint without Apply or state write. It continues deterministically down to one event; a single event whose exact signed proof still cannot fit returns `ProofLimit` with source/size evidence and holds route readiness, never retries forever or silently skips it. After a smaller page commits and its checkpoint/readback proves the new end, the next page starts at exactly end+1 under a fresh source-head/target/route-membership check. If source head or route capability changes during shrinking, discard candidate proofs and restart authenticated selection under the new fixed head. Command pages keep their separate 2 MiB outer proof rule. For ordinary stream, Admin, trace, authorized backup and every other authenticated page reader, the gateway likewise premeasures exact proof, readable bytes and simultaneously live scratch before signing or materializing any page of at most 256 contiguous events. A candidate above the 64 MiB proof or 128 MiB live-scratch cap is reduced to a smaller contiguous range; the gateway recomputes and re-signs its route entries, ordered list, prefix range/count/head/accumulator and any applicable anchor under the same fixed source target. It resumes only after the reduced page has been accepted and the next page begins at its end+1, with no skipped event or partial downloadable export. One event whose exact proof cannot fit returns typed `ProofLimit` and holds the reader with source/size evidence; it never loops on the same oversized page. Command pages retain the stricter outer rule. No existing signed fixture claim changes.

The appendable checkpoint accumulator begins `SHA256("HX-EV-CHECKPOINT-CHAIN-1\0" || 01 || U tenant || U domain || U aggregate ID || U aggregate type)` and advances for each contiguous event as `SHA256("HX-EV-CHECKPOINT-STEP-1\0" || previous B32 || N sequence || B32 StoredDigest)`. A page extends the signed previous accumulator; the final complete-prefix claim carries and binds the final value. A token alone is never completion proof. A witnessed snapshot at sequence k requires actor-owned readback of exact folded bytes, SnapshotDigest and cumulative accumulator through k; the signed prefix binds both SnapshotDigest and that accumulator. For k below `long.MaxValue`, its first tail page starts exactly k+1; k at `long.MaxValue` has no tail. Prefix tags `0e` and `0f` are both absent without a witnessed snapshot or both present and verified with one; mixed presence fails. A snapshot zero-tail proof for head=target=k>0 and k below `long.MaxValue` has start k+1/end k/count 0, absent checkpoint anchor, both snapshot tags present and bound to witnessed SnapshotDigest/accumulator, and no Apply. A projection metadata-only completion at checkpoint=head=k>0 and k below `long.MaxValue` has exactly start k+1/end k/count 0, present checkpoint anchor tag `0d` and checkpoint container entry for the same scope/route/sequence k, absent snapshot tags `0e`/`0f`, matching checkpoint accumulator and fenced state readback, and no event read, Apply, handler call, state write or checkpoint advance. **Terminal zero-tail sentinel:** when k=head=target=`long.MaxValue`, either anchored form instead has start=end=`long.MaxValue`, count 0 and zero route entries. Its appropriate snapshot or checkpoint anchor is mandatory, its accumulator/readback must match k, and the equality of start/end is valid only under this exact count-zero terminal rule. It represents no next sequence; the sentinel itself admits no route entry, duplicate event at k, checked increment or continuation to k+1. Separately, a normal one-event page may have start=end=head=target=`long.MaxValue`, count 1, prior accumulator through `long.MaxValue-1` and exactly one verified route at `long.MaxValue`; Apply that event once and complete without next-sequence arithmetic or another token. These forms are distinct from empty-stream start 1/end 0/head 0 with no checkpoint or snapshot tags and from B3's empty-target prefix. Any other zero-route nonempty-head form fails. Missing or incompatible anchor forces authenticated replay from 1. A projection tail starts only at signed checkpoint+1 when the checkpoint is below `long.MaxValue`; absent/invalid anchor forces full rebuild from sequence 1. `StateCheckpointReadbackHash = SHA256("HX-EV-STATE-READBACK-1\0" || 01 || U tenant || U domain || U state store ID || U durable state key || U route || N source sequence || U operation ID || U state version/ETag || U serializer ID || H serializer options || B bounded canonical state bytes)`. Require handler state source sequence **equal** completed sequence and matching operation/version before signing.

Checkpoint body is unsigned and acyclic: `HX-EV-CHECKPOINT-BODY-1\0`, codec `01`, count `000b`, tags `01..0b` tenant U, domain U, aggregate ID U, aggregate type U, route U, state bytes B, serializer ID U, completed sequence N, accumulator B32, source head N, expected CAS token O(U). It excludes readback hash, signature and resulting ETag. For the legacy single-state/V17 mode, hash body, CAS, read exact body/ETag and actual durable handler state, then sign purpose 04. For a production named row-set root, reserve the operation-scoped logical state version under the coordinator fence, compute the root/body/readback hash and sign purpose 04 **before** the one final root/checkpoint pointer CAS; claim tags `0d` and `12` both carry that reserved logical version. The prepared readback certificate binds only the prepared-record ETag; the actual final-pointer ETag enters only the separately authenticated provider-issued receipt after CAS acceptance, never a precommit claim or hash. If stores differ, use a linearizable `IProjectionStateCheckpointFence` coordinator for `(tenant, domain, aggregate ID, aggregate type, projection route)`. It owns one durable per-scope generation record under a coordinator ID. Its required provider operation is `TryWriteWithFence(scope, expectedGeneration, operationId, versionedStateOrCheckpoint)`: under a linearizable transaction/CAS, the participating state or checkpoint store compares the coordinator's **persisted current generation** with `expectedGeneration` and rejects a stale token before writing any state or checkpoint bytes. A coordinator generation advance serializes with these compare-and-write operations; an already issued token never authorizes a write after the advance. Each store persists operation ID, generation and immutable version together with the write and exposes their fenced readback. The coordinator must furnish a shared serializable fence that covers both stores' compare-and-write operations; independently sampled generations or readback after an unfenced write do not qualify. Persist state/effect under one stable operation/version, read it under that fence, CAS checkpoint referencing it, reread both before releasing the fence, and bind coordinator ID, generation, state operation/version and checkpoint ETag in the signed purpose-04 claim. If either backend cannot implement the compare-and-write guarantee, `CheckpointFenceUnavailable` holds readiness and the previous checkpoint/state pointer stays authoritative. Concurrent advances serialize on this fence; a mismatched row, stale generation or provider unable to enforce the shared fence returns `CheckpointFenceUnavailable` and leaves the prior checkpoint authoritative. CAS and independent readbacks alone do not qualify. State bytes/readback ceiling is 64 MiB, streaming hash buffer at most 1 MiB plus metadata; `CheckpointStateLimit` leaves last good checkpoint. Historic checkpoint obligations are immutable records keyed by scope/route/sequence/body hash/state readback hash/signature/key ID with tag `0e` signed issuance UTC matching obligation time and purpose-04 key interval, prior fingerprint and pending rebuild/rollback obligations, separate from delivery-pin obligations. Expired key use is only for the exact still-open historic obligation, original signing interval and durable readbacks; revocation requires explicit incident disposition. Trust-only transition verifies old obligation, current semantic/handler hashes, state/readback and accumulator, then signs current-fingerprint attestation **before** tail Apply at an actor boundary.

The handler state write above is an **immutable version**, never an in-place replacement of the key read by the old checkpoint. Its durable key is `projection-state-version:` plus lowercase SHA-256 of `U tenant || U domain || U aggregate ID || U aggregate type || U HandlerRouteId || N completed source sequence || U operation ID || N fence generation` under the §4 scalar codec; create-once CAS rejects a different value at that key. The checkpoint's durable record atomically carries a `HX-EV-CHECKPOINT-STATE-POINTER-1\0 || 01 || 0006` sidecar with tags `01..06`: U immutable state-version key, U state store ID, U state operation ID, U state version/ETag, N fence generation, B32 checkpoint body hash. This pointer is committed with the checkpoint CAS and its exact state key/version is read back under the same fence; the signed purpose-04 claim tags `0f..12`, the body hash and `StateCheckpointReadbackHash` bind it without changing the existing signed claim/body codecs or V17 fixture bytes. Until checkpoint body **and pointer** CAS/readback prove one committed transition, the old checkpoint still points to its old immutable state version. On ambiguous CAS, retain both versions and the fence generation, reconcile checkpoint/pointer/state by operation ID, and never report a new `Current` from a state write alone. In a single transactional store the equivalent is one serializable transaction that creates the immutable state version and changes the checkpoint body/pointer together, followed by readback; no in-place overwrite is allowed there either. Garbage collection of an old state version requires durable proof that no current checkpoint, retry, rebuild or rollback obligation references it. The approved V17 claim bytes remain a codec fixture; production acceptance also requires the corresponding immutable state-version key and pointer readback.

The V17 historical/test-local named-batch codec uses `BatchStateReadbackHash = SHA256("HX-EV-BATCH-READBACK-1\0" || 01 || u32 row-count || sorted rows)`. Each unique row is `U stateStoreId || U durableStateKey || U operationKind || N sourceSequence || U operationId || one-byte resultState || U resultingETagOrVersion || B32 canonicalReadbackBytesDigest`; sort by the separately encoded state-store ID and durable key, then operation kind/sequence/ID, reject duplicate keys or rows and unknown operation kinds. `resultState=01` is a present write (`operationKind=upsert`) whose resulting ETag/version and exact canonical readback digest match durable state. `resultState=00` is a successful delete (`operationKind=delete`): the same write fence supplies an authenticated absent-state readback and durable delete operation receipt/version in `resultingETagOrVersion`; the B32 digest is SHA-256 of the exact canonical delete receipt bytes, and the receipt binds key, operation ID, source sequence and fence. Absence alone, a missing receipt, a missing write row, or a present deleted row fails. After every `ReadModelBatchOperation` effect, read back **every** durable row under one write fence and compare operation ID, source sequence, version and canonical bytes or delete receipt. A missing/mismatched row prevents checkpoint advance. A delete receipt is the provider-authenticated, durable bytes `HX-EV-DELETE-RECEIPT-1\0 || 01 || 0007`, tags `01..07`: U state store ID, U durable state key, U operation ID, N source sequence, U write-fence ID, U resulting delete version/ETag, B exact provider delete-ack bytes. The same fence authenticates an absent-state readback for that key; the receipt is not constructed from absence alone. `canonicalReadbackBytesDigest` for a delete is SHA-256 of this complete receipt, and `resultingETagOrVersion` equals tag `06`. Missing durable ack, incomparable fence or provider inability to prove absence holds the checkpoint without advancement. The present-write V17 fixture uses discriminator `01`; its checkpoint signature binds that batch hash and the shared-fence fields in §11.

Named-projection writes use immutable shadow rows, never an in-place key visible to an ordinary reader. A startup-frozen catalog assigns each `(tenant, domain, HandlerRouteId, declared logical key-space)` **one** ownership mode: `aggregate` (one addressed stream) or `shared` (many streams), using the §5 key-space capability rows; overlapping declarations fail readiness. Each source stream retains its own authenticated contiguous sequence checkpoint and prefix accumulator. A shared route/key-space has one durable linearizable generation coordinator and commit-order log. Under its CAS fence the coordinator reserves the next checked **global commit ordinal** for one prepared operation, binds that candidate ordinal to immutable operation ID, original authenticated source-proof hash, precommit transition-intent hash and previous root hash, and commits the ordinal log entry **atomically with** the new route-global root and source checkpoint visibility. A failed uncommitted candidate consumes no ordinal; an ambiguous result is read back by operation ID before any replacement candidate. The ordinal is exactly previous ordinal plus one (genesis zero); gaps, reused ordinals, changed operation bytes, conflicting source progress or an unavailable coordinator hold. An exact retry of the same operation reuses its assigned ordinal/result after readback, including ambiguous CAS. A late source event whose per-stream sequence or aggregate ID sorts before an already committed source gets the next ordinal; it cannot change prior visible history. Authenticated replay follows this durable ordinal log, not arrival-time sorting or a retrospectively sorted `(sequence, aggregate)` tuple. The root binds the ordinal and source proof through its progress intent and operation witness, while every contributing stream remains independently sequence-contiguous. A per-aggregate pointer never publishes a shared key; queries select the route-global committed root and certificate. Aggregate-owned keys use the same root/progress codec with one source and need no cross-stream ordinal. Provider inability to supply the fence, ordinal CAS and exact readback blocks route readiness.

For each candidate operation, under that fence read the **currently committed logical** value, logical ETag/version and expiry from the old root, then apply the existing public `ReadModelBatchOperation` policy. `ExpectedETag` with an empty ETag means create-only and requires proven logical absence; a nonempty ETag must match the present visible logical ETag. `IdempotentAbsent` is **delete-only**: a present logical key is deleted under the fence, and an already absent key is a proved idempotent no-op. It never rejects a valid present-key delete merely because absence is false. Unconditional writes remain serialized by the fence. A fresh absent shadow physical key is not proof of logical absence. The operation witness records observed and resulting logical versions/ETags, exact intended canonical bytes, `ReadModelBatchOperation.ValueTypeName`, policy, TTL and the assigned global ordinal/source-proof intent for shared ownership. Exact retry compares OperationId and all those intended fields; an intervening committed logical version conflicts unless the original operation/result is read back as already committed. `BatchStateReadbackHash` is the changed-row/delete witness, distinct from full membership. V17's signed batch witness remains a historical/test-local codec vector. The production logical-operation witness is `HX-EV-BATCH-LOGICAL-1\0 || 01 || I operationCount ||` entries in original batch ordinal order. Each entry is `HX-EV-BATCH-LOGICAL-ENTRY-1\0 || 01 || 000d`, ascending tags: `01` I ordinal, `02` U logical key, `03` U OperationId (for a `ReadModelBatchOperation`, exactly its enclosing `ReadModelBatchScope.BatchId`, never a nonexistent per-operation member), `04` U kind (`upsert`/`delete`), `05` U policy (`Unconditional`/`ExpectedETag`/`IdempotentAbsent`), `06` O(U) caller expected ETag (empty means create-only), `07` O(U) observed committed logical ETag (absent means proved logical absence), `08` N observed logical version (zero for proved absence), `09` O(U) resulting logical ETag (absent for tombstone/no-op), `0a` N resulting logical version, `0b` B32 SHA-256 of exact intended canonical value bytes (empty bytes for delete), `0c` O(N) positive TTL ticks, `0d` U exact `ValueTypeName` (nonempty for upsert, empty for delete). Ordinals start at zero and are contiguous. A present-key `IdempotentAbsent` creates the durable delete receipt/absence readback; an already absent no-op retains its version and carries a fenced absence witness without inventing a delete receipt. The shared commit ordinal and original authenticated source-proof hash are bound by the §6 source-transition intent included in ProgressHash; a batch cannot substitute an operation from a different source/ordinal. The production `NamedBatchScopeBytes` are exactly `U ReadModelBatchScope.StoreName || U TenantId || U Domain || U AggregateId || U ProjectionType || U BatchId || U HandlerRouteId || U keySpaceId || U ownershipMode` in that order. All operations in one batch carry the same BatchId; an exact retry compares the complete scope tuple, BatchId, ordinal, source-transition intent and logical operations before reuse. Production `BatchStateReadbackHash = SHA256("HX-EV-BATCH-READBACK-2\0" || 02 || B(NamedBatchScopeBytes) || B32 SHA-256("HX-EV-BATCH-READBACK-1\0" || 01 || u32 row-count || sorted changed-row/delete rows) || B(exact logical-operation witness))`.
