The complete scope tuple and BatchId therefore enter this batch fingerprint and the root through tag `0b`; the root also carries tenant/domain/route/key-space/ownership and its tag `07` OperationId equals the same BatchId. A mismatch in any field is a conflicting batch/root, never an exact retry; V17's signed V1 hash and literal bytes remain historical framing evidence only.

The production complete row-set is a persistent immutable **keyed sparse Merkle tree**, with the existing root record's tag `09` binding its root and tag `08` its checked member count. Its key tuple is the exact separately encoded §4 `U tenant || U domain || U HandlerRouteId || U keySpaceId || U logicalKey`; path bits are the 256 bits of SHA-256 over that tuple, most-significant bit of byte zero first. The leaf at depth 256 is `HX-EV-NAMED-LEAF-2\0 || 02 || 000b`, ascending tags `01..05` the five U key components, `06` U immutable physical row key, `07` U physical row version/ETag, `08` one-byte state (`00` proved delete/tombstone, `01` present), `09` B32 SHA-256 of exact authenticated row content/readback bytes or exact durable delete receipt, `0a` O(N) positive logical TTL ticks and `0b` N original visibility generation. Its hash is `SHA256("HX-EV-NAMED-LEAF-HASH-2\0" || 02 || B(exact leaf record))`. At depth 256 the empty hash is `E256 = SHA256("HX-EV-NAMED-EMPTY-2\0" || 02 || u16(256))` with count zero; a leaf has count one. At each depth `d=255..0`, `NodeHash = SHA256("HX-EV-NAMED-NODE-2\0" || 02 || u16(d) || I leftCount || B32 leftHash || I rightCount || B32 rightHash)` with checked parent count equal to leftCount+rightCount. `Ed` is that formula with both child counts zero and both child hashes E(d+1). The root of a zero-member set is E0 with count zero. Present and proved tombstone leaves both count as one retained member until certified compaction. The exact row proof is `HX-EV-NAMED-ROW-PATH-2\0 || 02 || B(exact key tuple) || one-byte terminalKind || terminal || u16(256) || siblings`: terminalKind `00` has no terminal bytes and denotes E256/count zero; `01` is followed by `B(exact leaf record)` with count one. Each sibling is `I checked count || B32 hash` in ascending depth `0..255`; no default sibling is omitted. A membership proof uses `01`, including a tombstone, and an absence proof uses `00`. There are no extra entries or trailing bytes. Recompute bottom-up using the key bits, require both reconstructed root hash and count to equal root tags `09` and `08` under the authenticated certificate, and read/hash the selected physical row or delete receipt before returning value or absence. A different exact leaf key on the same 256-bit path is a hash collision and fails closed; it never silently replaces a member. A changed key recomputes only its verified 256-level logical path by immutable path copying under the route fence; unchanged subtrees and their counts are reused from the previously certified root. Physical storage is a deterministic content-addressed compressed sparse trie: materialize leaves and two-child branch records, and encode each maximal single-child run as `HX-EV-NAMED-SPAN-2\0 || 02 || u16 startDepth || u16 endDepth || I descendantCount || B32 descendantHash || B(ordered path bits)`; the decoder expands every skipped logical level with its fixed Ed empty sibling and the declared key bits before comparing the root. The bit string has exactly `endDepth-startDepth` bits, packed most-significant-bit first into the minimal byte count with unused low bits zero; a span with startDepth >= endDepth or a branch hidden inside a span is invalid. Spans are maximal, nonempty and uniquely normalized; their exact content hash and referenced child bytes are authenticated. This compression preserves the full 256-level proof codec while allowing the 1 GiB retained-index bound to be met for a million small leaves; an oversized encoded index still fails `NamedIndexLimit`. Complete membership/absence comes from the path and certified root, never a linear row scan or adjacent-member inference. The older sorted-leaf/V17 literal is historical framing evidence only and cannot certify a production named root.

The logical source-progress set is keyed by `(aggregate type, aggregate ID)` and holds each contributing source's checked sequence (the proposed sequence only for the addressed transition, otherwise its committed sequence), **previous committed** source-checkpoint hash, prefix accumulator, last operation ID and `O(B32)` precommit transition-intent hash. The currently building checkpoint hash is never an input to its own candidate progress/root hash. For production, encode each source entry as `HX-EV-NAMED-PROGRESS-ENTRY-2\0 || 02 || 0007` with ascending tags: `01` U aggregate type, `02` U aggregate ID, `03` N sequence, `04` B32 previous committed checkpoint hash, `05` B32 accumulator, `06` U operation ID and `07` O(B32) transition-intent hash. A new source with no prior checkpoint uses exactly 32 zero bytes only at sequence zero; unchanged entries have absent intent and retain the currently committed checkpoint. The addressed source has exactly one present intent. That intent remains `HX-EV-NAMED-SOURCE-INTENT-1\0 || 01 || 0008`, tags `01` U aggregate type, `02` U aggregate ID, `03` N proposed source sequence, `04` B32 proposed accumulator, `05` B32 original authenticated actor/source proof hash, `06` U operation ID, `07` N coordinator-assigned global commit ordinal (zero for aggregate-owned mode), `08` B32 previous committed checkpoint hash. Path key is SHA-256 of exact §4 `U aggregateType || U aggregateId`, with the same most-significant-bit-first 256-level path and collision fail-closed rule as the row tree. Progress leaves use `SHA256("HX-EV-NAMED-PROGRESS-LEAF-2\0" || 02 || B(exact entry))` with count one. Empty and node hashes use distinct `HX-EV-NAMED-PROGRESS-EMPTY-2\0` and `HX-EV-NAMED-PROGRESS-NODE-2\0` separators, the same depth and checked child-count codecs as the row tree, with zero-count empty leaves. `ProgressHash = SHA256("HX-EV-NAMED-PROGRESS-ROOT-2\0" || 02 || I checkedSourceCount || B32 sparseProgressRoot)`; this commits both complete source count and sparse tree root in tag `0a` of the named root. The exact source proof is `HX-EV-NAMED-PROGRESS-PATH-2\0 || 02 || B(exact U aggregateType || U aggregateId tuple) || one-byte terminalKind || terminal || u16(256) || siblings`, with terminalKind `00` for the empty terminal and no bytes, or `01` followed by `B(exact progress entry)`; each of the 256 ascending-depth `0..255` siblings is `I checked count || B32 hash`. No default sibling is omitted and no extra bytes are allowed. Its reconstructed checked count and hash must equal the certified ProgressHash, and each source update reads/verifies the previous certified path, changes only that path and retains all unchanged subtrees. Progress branches and maximal single-child runs use the same authenticated compressed storage rule with distinct `HX-EV-NAMED-PROGRESS-SPAN-2\0` separator; proof verification always expands the full 256 logical levels. No complete million-entry vector or O(total sources) SHA-256 is reconstructed per event. Missing prior source evidence, an altered transition intent or a count/root mismatch holds before publication. From the prior signed checkpoint and original source proof, build candidate rows, intent, ProgressHash and root **first**. The new source checkpoint then signs that candidate root/intent; the final fenced pointer CAS publishes the prepared root and checkpoint only together with their authenticated certificate linking hashes, source intent, ordinal and previous checkpoint. Readback verifies the certificate and new signature against the already constructed root without any forward hash reference. A query verifies only selected source leaves/index paths and the coordinator certificate, never the entire vector. Missing prior checkpoint, altered intent, cyclic forward reference, changed operation or absent certified sparse-progress path/proof prevents root commit/readiness.

The authoritative checkpoint **state bytes** for a named batch are the exact canonical root/pointer record `HX-EV-NAMED-ROWSET-ROOT-1\0 || 01 || 000d` with ascending tags: `01` U tenant, `02` U domain, `03` U HandlerRouteId, `04` U keySpaceId, `05` U ownership mode (`aggregate` or `shared`), `06` N generation (equal to the assigned global commit ordinal for shared ownership), `07` U OperationId (exact enclosing `ReadModelBatchScope.BatchId` for a named batch), `08` I complete row count, `09` B32 Merkle root hash, `0a` B32 ProgressHash, `0b` B32 BatchStateReadbackHash, `0c` Q provider-certified atomic pointer visibility UTC, `0d` B exact canonical `HX-EV-STATE-BACKEND-1\0` descriptor bytes from §5. The fence provider reserves tag `0c` as its certified prospective pointer-visibility UTC **inside the same held linearizable commit operation before the candidate root is hashed and checkpoint signed**. The final root/checkpoint CAS must certify and use that exact reserved UTC as its visibility time or abort without publishing either record; a caller clock, unfenced pre-CAS estimate or post-sign substitution cannot supply it. A provider unable to reserve and atomically certify that time and root holds route readiness. Its reserved serializer ID is exactly `hexalith.eventstore.named-rowset-root.v1`; its canonical §4 LF options manifest is exactly `{"codec":"hx-ev-named-rowset-root-1","version":1}\n`, expanded with no optional fields and hashed by the §4 OptionsHash rule. No handler-defined object occupies named-batch state bytes. The named checkpoint state readback hash uses the exact §6 `HX-EV-STATE-READBACK-1\0` formula with this root record as `B bounded canonical state bytes`, the reserved serializer ID/options hash, route/key-space root durable state key, source sequence, operation ID and a **deterministic operation-scoped logical state version reserved under the coordinator fence before signing** in the `U state version/ETag` position. This is a logical version, never the provider ETag first returned after CAS. The provider compares that reserved version while staging root and signed checkpoint as invisible prepared records, reports the exact prepared readback and actual provider ETag under the fence, and certifies that the final pointer CAS can publish precisely those bytes and that logical version together with the postcommit certificate. A provider unable to reserve and compare it holds route readiness. The changed-row `BatchStateReadbackHash` remains tag `0b`, a separate operation witness. Stage and read back every changed shadow row/delete receipt, affected sparse-tree paths, previous addressed source checkpoint and source transition intent first; authenticate untouched subtrees against the previous certified roots without rereading every member. Construct the candidate root from those prior records; only afterward sign the addressed source checkpoint over that exact root and intent. Root and newly signed addressed source checkpoint are staged as **prepared and invisible** under the operation fence; other source checkpoints in the progress vector remain unchanged. The coordinator reads back both prepared byte strings, their reserved logical version and **prepared-record ETag**, and authenticates the separate prepared readback certificate below. It then performs **one** final fenced pointer CAS that selects their exact hashes and root generation, atomically makes the checkpoint transition visible, and causes the provider to issue the separate final-pointer commit receipt below. The actual final-pointer ETag is known only after this CAS accepts and never enters a prepared hash or signature. No reader selects a prepared root or checkpoint before that CAS. Neither root nor progress leaf contains the newly signed checkpoint hash, so construction is acyclic. A separate store stages the source checkpoint invisibly under the same fence until root commit and exposes it only through the committed root. Read back the exact root, selected sparse progress-path validation, source checkpoint, prepared certificate, final-pointer provider receipt and state hash before `Current`. Before the final visibility CAS, the authenticated **prepared readback certificate** is `HX-EV-NAMED-PREPARED-1\0 || 01 || 000a`, with ordered tags `01` U tenant, `02` U domain, `03` U HandlerRouteId, `04` U keySpaceId, `05` U OperationId, `06` B32 exact prepared root-record hash, `07` B32 exact prepared signed checkpoint-carrier hash, `08` U reserved logical state version, `09` U **prepared-record ETag**, `0a` B exact authenticated prepared-provider readback/fence evidence. It contains no final-pointer ETag, final visibility generation or post-CAS timestamp. The final pointer CAS verifies those prepared hashes/version/ETag and creates a provider-issued **final-pointer commit receipt**, `HX-EV-NAMED-POINTER-COMMIT-1\0 || 01 || 000c`, ordered tags `01` U tenant, `02` U domain, `03` U HandlerRouteId, `04` U keySpaceId, `05` U OperationId, `06` B32 prepared-certificate hash, `07` B32 selected root-record hash, `08` B32 selected signed checkpoint-carrier hash, `09` U reserved logical state version, `0a` U **actual final-pointer ETag**, `0b` N actual visibility generation and `0c` Q actual provider-certified visibility UTC. Its authenticated provider binding to the atomic pointer CAS is verified through the configured backend trust/fence and independently read back before `Current` or query; receipt tag `0b` must equal selected root tag `06`, and receipt tag `0c` must equal the provider-reserved root tag `0c` or the CAS is rejected as uncommitted. The receipt is not included in its own pointer hash. A missing, changed or unprovable final-pointer receipt holds the previous certified root or the candidate for same-OperationId reconciliation. If a crash occurs after preparation but before final pointer CAS, readers keep the previous certified pointer. Recovery reads exact prepared root/checkpoint bytes, prepared ETag, logical version and prepared certificate under the original fence, then retries that **same** pointer CAS without inventing a final ETag or time. A lost final CAS acknowledgement reads back pointer and provider receipt before reporting visibility. Missing or changed evidence holds without publication; a lost CAS acknowledgement is reconciled by exact pointer/provider-receipt readback before retry. A provider exposing prepared root bytes as current before certificate/pointer publication fails readiness. The legacy single-state/V17 claim and hash codec stay unchanged. Partial rows or uncertain CAS keep the old root and last-good state. A same-store serializable transaction may stage rows plus checkpoint and publish their certified pointer atomically with the exact prepared readback certificate and provider-issued final-pointer receipt; independent stores require the shared coordinator/fence and retain all old generations until obligations close. V17's fixed signed checkpoint is a historical batch-hash framing vector and is not rewritten; production named-batch root mode uses this reserved state codec.

Named row and progress indexes are separately capacity-bound **before** root publication: each separately encoded logical key is at most 512 UTF-8 bytes, each complete leaf/progress entry at most 4 KiB, each retained complete index at most 1 GiB encoded, each row/source count at most 1,000,000 and all live construction scratch at most 128 MiB. Checked byte counters charge keys, records, framing and Merkle nodes before each allocation. For each event, at most **4,096 changed logical keys** are admitted. Read and verify the prior committed row and source roots, then copy only the affected 256-node paths into authenticated encrypted bounded storage, sharing untouched immutable nodes. Charge all changed keys, 256 path nodes per changed key, encoded bytes, proof buffers and 128 MiB live scratch before construction; stage every chunk under one OperationId, verify readback, then publish one root and certificate. An oversized change is `NamedIndexLimit` before any visible pointer. Corpus/readiness preflight proves required routes fit this bound or requires a separately approved migration. Initial migration may stream a bounded complete index once; ordinary event updates never scan all rows or sources. `NamedIndexLimit` rejects an overlarge candidate before root publication while retaining the previous committed root. A tombstone and its exact delete/version evidence remain while any rollback, retry, backup, checkpoint or older-root obligation refers to them. Once all such obligations close with durable proof, a fenced compaction root at a new global ordinal may omit the tombstone, retaining immutable archived delete/version evidence for ABA-safe later creates; absence is then proved by the authenticated empty sparse path against the compacted root. Compaction advances no source sequence, signs no fabricated source event, and requires exact root/certificate readback. If safe pruning cannot maintain all bounds, route readiness holds rather than dropping evidence or silently rejecting valid history.

The additive public `INamedProjectionVersionedReadModelStore` query seam has `GetAsync<TValue>(string storeName, string logicalKey, NamedProjectionReadScope scope, CancellationToken cancellationToken): Task<ReadModelEntry<TValue>>` and `GetManyAsync<TValue>(string storeName, IReadOnlyList<string> logicalKeys, NamedProjectionReadScope scope, CancellationToken cancellationToken): Task<IReadOnlyList<ReadModelBulkEntry<TValue>>>`, with the old `TValue : class` constraint. `NamedProjectionReadScope` is immutable descriptive route input and names tenant, domain, HandlerRouteId, declared key-space, ownership mode, optional addressed aggregate for aggregate ownership and state-backend ID; the separately verified capability below grants access, and caller JSON alone cannot grant it. Under the shared fence the router reads the **last committed route-global root for shared keys** or the aggregate root for aggregate-owned keys, verifies its checkpoint/state hash, backend, progress root, operation and catalog declaration plus the authenticated coordinator commit certificate that the changed source path and unchanged certified subtrees yield the complete ProgressHash at root CAS, then releases the coordinator lock. It reads only requested logical keys through authenticated leaf membership/absence index paths and checked physical row/delete readbacks, not a full row-set scan. Before returning **any** route-aware value, it reacquires the coordinator fence and rechecks both the exact root pointer/generation **and authoritative coordinator UTC against every selected leaf expiry**. Inside a dispatcher-installed versioned query session, B7d's pinned-root rule replaces this per-call selection and retry. Otherwise, if the root changed it retries at most three times; if UTC reached an expiry even with an unchanged root, it triggers or observes maintenance and returns `ReadModelExpiryPending` with no expired bytes until a tombstone root is certified. A fourth root change returns `CheckpointFenceUnavailable` with no partial values. Cancellation releases proof buffers, rows and locks and returns no mixed generation. The route-aware `GetManyAsync` proves all keys against one root, preserves request order and rejects duplicate keys.

Pre-admission caps are **1,000,000 complete rows per root**, **256 requested keys**, **8 MiB total encoded query proof**, **64 MiB total result bytes**, and **128 MiB combined simultaneously live proof/row/result/scratch bytes**. Charge conservative encoded sizes and allocator capacity before each allocation or lock hold; a request that cannot fit returns typed `ReadModelQueryLimit` with no partial result or held fence. The query proof includes the exact root record, selected leaf/absence paths and selected source-progress paths, each under its own index hash; all hash/readback comparisons precede deserialization. Corpus/readiness preflight holds a route whose key count, retained row sizes or source-vector/index proof cannot satisfy these limits; it never raises a cap silently.

`DaprReadModelStore` implements the route-aware seam additively. A startup-frozen catalog discriminator recognizes every versioned logical key and shadow generation before **all** public legacy reads and writes: `GetAsync`, `GetManyAsync`, `SaveAsync`, `TrySaveAsync`, time-to-live writes, delete/erase, batch, bulk and staging entry points. A legacy read either goes through a registered authenticated scoped query adapter or returns `ReadModelRouteContextRequired` before touching a versioned key; a legacy write to that key returns the typed context-required failure and cannot create a shadow row. Only the authorized route-aware fenced writer/query seam may touch versioned generations. During 6.6 migration, `SharedProjectionEpochCoordinator.ReadGenerationAsync`, `BuildBatch` and every physical-generation read/write use an additive authorized route-aware store adapter carrying the same authenticated route/key-space scope and fence. Existing physical rows are readable only with authenticated legacy generation/marker evidence; new writes enter the new root protocol. A direct old `IReadModelStore` call from the coordinator is neither an unguarded bypass nor a blocked production path: readiness requires that migrated adapter and a test proving the generic legacy guard rejects the same physical key without its authority. Non-versioned keys retain existing APIs and coordinated-batch marker behavior. Admin projection views use the route-aware seam; missing/ambiguous root is `ProjectionStateUnproven`, never a free shadow read.

`TimeToLive` starts at tag `0c` atomic root visibility UTC, as the public batch contract specifies. The leaf binds its TTL duration and original write visibility generation; checked addition to that generation's provider-certified CAS UTC yields expiry, checked against authoritative coordinator UTC. An unchanged leaf retains its original generation and expiry across later root commits. The coordinator retains an authenticated `(generation, visibility UTC, root hash, operation ID)` ledger for every still-referenced generation; a missing or changed old time holds the query rather than resetting TTL. Shadow and prior physical rows, delete receipts, index nodes and source proofs have independently renewed storage retention while any committed pointer, retry, rollback or backup obligation references them. Renewal uses separate lease/metadata keys or a provider operation proved to preserve the exact physical row bytes, version and ETag bound by its Merkle leaf. If renewal mutates any bound field, the coordinator copies the row into a new immutable version and certifies a new root under the fence before old retention lapses. An unrenewable referenced row holds readiness; no maintenance silently invalidates an already certified root. TTL expiry is a **route/key-space scoped maintenance transition** with no source event, arbitrarily selected contributing aggregate, fabricated source checkpoint, source-sequence advance or accumulator change. Its immutable OperationId is `SHA256("HX-EV-NAMED-TTL-OP-1\0" || 01 || B32 old root hash || U logical key || N original visibility generation || Q checked expiry UTC)` rendered as lowercase hex. Under the route/key-space fence it creates one proved tombstone leaf and root at the next checked global commit ordinal; **ProgressHash and every contributing source's signed checkpoint, sequence and accumulator remain unchanged**. An aggregate-owned key may use the same scoped maintenance claim and unchanged-progress rule. The maintenance intent is `HX-EV-NAMED-TTL-INTENT-2\0 || 02 || 0008`, tags `01` B32 old root hash, `02` U logical key, `03` N original visibility generation, `04` Q checked expiry UTC, `05` U OperationId, `06` N assigned global ordinal, `07` B32 unchanged ProgressHash, `08` B32 exact authenticated tombstone leaf/readback hash. Maintenance root tag `0b` is `SHA256("HX-EV-NAMED-MAINT-READBACK-1\0" || 01 || B(exact maintenance intent))`, so it is constructible before the root hash; the claim then signs that completed new root hash. No root, intent, claim or checkpoint hash refers forward to itself. A distinct **purpose `0f`** signed `HX-EV-NAMED-MAINTENANCE-1\0 || 01 || 000d` claim has tags `01` U tenant, `02` U domain, `03` U HandlerRouteId, `04` U keySpaceId, `05` B exact canonical backend descriptor, `06` B32 old root hash, `07` U logical key, `08` Q expiry UTC, `09` B32 new tombstone-root hash, `0a` N global commit ordinal, `0b` B32 unchanged ProgressHash, `0c` U exact maintenance OperationId, `0d` B32 SHA-256 of the exact maintenance intent. It uses the current active domain signing key and never verifies as an event-progress purpose-04 checkpoint. The coordinator atomically publishes the new root and this maintenance claim, then reads back an authenticated commit certificate binding both hashes, ordinal, backend, operation ID, exact logical version and provider ETag before queries select it. Exact retries reuse the pinned operation ID, ordinal, root and claim; ambiguous CAS reconciles by OperationId before another attempt.

At each committed root, a durable scheduler registers only changed/new finite-leaf expiry jobs or a successor explicitly rebased under that root, retaining unchanged jobs by reference with their original generation, expiry UTC and maintenance OperationId. Before executing a job, it reads the current certified root under the route/key-space fence and authenticates that leaf. If the exact logical leaf is absent, replaced, or has a different original visibility generation or expiry, it durably marks the old job superseded and never tombstones the replacement. If the same expiring leaf persists under a newer root, it derives a successor maintenance OperationId by the §6 formula using that current root and unchanged key/generation/expiry, CAS-links the old job to the successor and drives the successor against the current root. An ambiguous old attempt is reconciled under its original OperationId before rebasing. Concurrent expiry jobs for one key serialize under the fence; a scheduler or query trigger drives the linked successor or returns typed `ReadModelExpiryPending`, never spins on a stale root. It retries after crash and reconciles ambiguous CAS before another transition. Every route-aware query compares the leaf expiry to authenticated coordinator UTC. At `now >= expiry`, it triggers or observes that scheduled transition and returns typed `ReadModelExpiryPending`/`ProjectionStateUnproven` until a committed tombstone root and signed maintenance certificate prove absence. It never returns expired bytes or infers absence from clock time alone. Scheduler outage or late first query therefore holds the value as unproven until repair; a still-live value is returned only while authenticated UTC is strictly before expiry. Physical row expiry never substitutes for this transition. Missing, altered or early-retired evidence holds readiness.

An **event-progress** checkpoint's `StateCheckpointReadbackHash` is the exact precommit logical-version root-state readback hash for a production named batch, and the existing single-state hash for a single-state operation. A scoped purpose-`0f` TTL transition instead binds its root and unchanged ProgressHash through its distinct maintenance claim and final-pointer provider receipt; fenced compaction binds those values through its own authenticated root certificate. Neither invents a source checkpoint. `BatchStateReadbackHash` is separately bound inside the named root. The historical V17 batch-hash checkpoint vector retains its original codec bytes and is not a production root-state substitute. Every signed production checkpoint binds its selected state bytes/hash under the shared fence, never an unfenced copy of intended writes.

The optional folded-snapshot witness is an additive actor-owned side record, never a rewrite of the approved Story 6.1 v1 envelope. `SnapshotDigest = SHA256("HX-EV-SNAPSHOT-1\0" || 01 || U tenant || U domain || U aggregate ID || U aggregate type || N covered sequence || I snapshot envelope version || U snapshot state serializer ID || B canonical verified readable folded-state bytes || B32 StateSchemaApplyHash || B32 EventTransformHash || B32 derived protection record hash || B32 cumulative prefix accumulator through covered sequence)`. The protection record includes state, metadata version, scheme, key alias, content hint and `O(M)` flags under §4; snapshot state obeys the approved Story 6.1 bound and is streamed/checked before witness hashing. The proof carries those exact folded bytes, digest and accumulator or authenticated actor retrieval of all three. The signed prefix and receiver recomputation tie `DomainServiceCurrentState.SnapshotState` to the verified bytes; a free typed/JSON `CurrentState` is never command authority. Gateway obtains signed source/snapshot proof for it or rejects it, and the domain router rejects unproven state before calling even the old processor. `DomainServiceCurrentState.SnapshotState` is deserialized **from the verified bytes** under fingerprinted serializer; receiver recomputes witness and never trusts a free object to assert it. Actor stages snapshot and side record in one batch, saves once and reads both back; absent, partial, stale or incompatible witness safely bypasses to full replay. If Story 6.2 runtime is absent, no witness is read/written and full replay is used. Changed state/Apply, transform or relevant handler compatibility causes replay/rebuild; verifier-only key rotation does not.

The persisted witness at `AggregateIdentity.SnapshotKey + ":evolution-witness"` has exact binary schema `HX-EV-SNAPSHOT-WITNESS-1\0 || 01 || 0011`, followed by tags `01..11` in order: U tenant, U domain, U aggregate ID, U aggregate type, U snapshot key, N covered sequence, I approved v1 envelope version, U state serializer ID, B32 SHA-256 of canonical verified readable folded-state bytes, B32 SHA-256 of the complete exact original v1 snapshot storage/envelope/ciphertext bytes, B32 SnapshotDigest, B32 StateSchemaApplyHash, B32 EventTransformHash, B32 protection-record hash, B32 cumulative prefix accumulator, U actor batch operation ID, N actor logical version chosen before save with checked increment. The actor pre-renders the exact provider snapshot storage bytes with a bounded deterministic serializer before staging, and both snapshot hashes bind those separately preserved approved v1 bytes and key; no field changes that envelope. Stage snapshot plus side record under one actor batch operation and predeclared logical version, then read back their exact bytes, key, sequence, equal operation/logical version and provider ETag before treating either as authority; the post-save ETag is readback evidence outside the prewrite side record, so no digest is circular. A partial or mismatched pair is a safe full-replay bypass. The existing v1 snapshot may be re-folded only after full authenticated replay and one actor-owned paired save/readback. Domain receivers obtain snapshot authority through `IAuthenticatedSnapshotSource.ReadAsync(tenant, domain, aggregateType, aggregateId, snapshotKey, coveredSequence, CancellationToken)` over the mutually authenticated gateway channel. The actor-owned response contains exact original v1 snapshot-storage bytes, exact side-record bytes, verified readable folded-state bytes obtained through the existing typed snapshot unprotection/readability outcome, batch operation ID, predeclared logical version and provider ETag, all under one linearizable provider read fence. The gateway verifies provider key/scope/ETag and exact bytes under the actor identity before returning them; request-carried `snapshotWitness`/`snapshotState` are only bounded hints. The receiver independently hashes original storage bytes and folded bytes, decodes the side record, compares its two byte hashes, batch ID, logical version, key, sequence, serializer, protection, StateSchemaApplyHash, EventTransformHash and accumulator to the source response and signed prefix, then deserializes only authenticated, verified readable folded bytes. The lookup has a 128 MiB raw-storage and 64 MiB folded-byte cap, streams before materialization, and never returns a free typed state. Unavailable, partial, mismatched or unfenced readback bypasses the snapshot and forces authenticated replay from sequence 1; it cannot authorize tail Apply.

Protected approved-v1 snapshots have **two distinct byte domains**. First authenticate the exact original actor storage/envelope/ciphertext bytes, key, ETag, batch/version and protection metadata under the 128 MiB raw cap, with bounded provider readback before materialization. Then invoke the existing typed snapshot unprotection/readability outcome using the registered provider, key and occurrence context, bounding the readable result at 64 MiB before materialization. Only a successful readable outcome supplies the canonical folded-state bytes for tag `09`, `SnapshotDigest`, deserialization and signed state proof; ciphertext is hashed only by tag `0a` and the actor storage witness. Recheck the derived protection record and original storage hash independently. `ProtectedUnreadable`, `ProviderOpaque`, missing key/provider, ambiguous unprotection or a cap failure preserves the stored snapshot and safely bypasses to authenticated replay from sequence 1 under existing retention/erasure policy, without deleting the snapshot, treating ciphertext as state or falling back to guessed plaintext. A verified `Unprotected`/legacy no-op outcome still passes these separate storage and readable-byte checks.

The additive cumulative-prefix side record at `AggregateIdentity.MetadataKey + ":evolution-prefix"` is `HX-EV-PREFIX-STATE-1\0 || 01 || 0008` with tags `01..08`: U tenant, U domain, U aggregate ID, U aggregate type, N covered sequence, B32 accumulator, U actor batch operation ID, N actor logical version chosen before save with checked increment. Its genesis is the §6 scope genesis. After a fully authenticated seed, each actor append computes the §6 step once per newly staged contiguous event, saves the final accumulator with the event batch under the same operation, and reads both back under the same predeclared logical version and provider ETag before publishing it. A snapshot copies the verified accumulator at its covered sequence. For old streams with no side record, authenticated full replay from sequence 1 establishes a seed and stages it with the next actor-owned save or paired refold; no missing-history shortcut is allowed. A missing, conflicting or ambiguous update forces full replay and prevents a tail-cost claim. Each normal append advances from the last readback value with O(1) work per event, without rereading the entire stream at each fold.

Paged command-state request/response carries addressed scope, fixed expected head/target, page start/count/max bytes, ordered EventEvolutionProof, continuation token and final signed complete-prefix proof. Each page has at most 256 events, 64 MiB readable bytes and 2 MiB proof. Before admitting a **final** page, compute the exact encoded size of its final `EventEvolutionProof` plus purpose-07 claim, key ID, 64-byte signature, command-state-proof framing and Base64 carrier, and reserve the entire result within the outer 2 MiB `commandStateProof` cap. If the page is too large, shrink and re-sign it **before** admission or return `ProofLimit` with no Apply or authoritative completion; a signed admitted final page is never silently over cap. This proof budget is distinct from the 128 MiB actual encoded response cap. Continuation uses purpose 05 claim above plus key ID/signature codec; one stable operation ID, head, target, fingerprints, stored accumulator, effective chain and nonce span pages. For each admitted page, the receiver starts with the signed prior chain, verifies every route/effective payload and applies the §6 effective-step hash in sequence order. Its signed next token tag `10` equals that resulting chain; a next request whose token chain differs from the durable prior ledger chain is `CommandStateUnproven` before Apply. The durable operation ledger persists both accumulators and a page transcript. The transcript-v1 genesis, retained only for operations that began before transcript v2 was selected, is `SHA256("HX-EV-COMMAND-PAGES-1\0" || 01 || U operation ID || U tenant || U domain || U aggregate ID || U aggregate type || N fixed head || N target)`, and each completed v1 page advances as `SHA256("HX-EV-COMMAND-PAGE-STEP-1\0" || prior B32 || N page start || I page count || B32 SHA-256(exact EventEvolutionProof container) || B32 resulting stored accumulator || B32 resulting effective chain)`. Persist the page start/count, exact proof hash, prior/resulting values and transcript under the ledger CAS/readback; no transition may skip or repeat a sequence. Purpose-07 tag `11` signs the terminal transcript from that ledger. A new operation selects the B4 production transcript v2 through B4b, and its zero-event completion commits exactly one count-zero final transition (B4a); only a pre-existing v1 operation completes a zero-page empty or witnessed-snapshot request from the v1 genesis and its signed anchor. The gateway stores a durable bounded spent-token ledger keyed by token digest and operation. It holds at most 65,536 entries and 64 MiB encoded bytes, retains entries at least 24 hours and issues tokens valid for 15 minutes. Capacity is reserved as described below before Apply, and full capacity returns `ContinuationCapacityHold` without authoritative progress. The old full-array adapter fills one array from successive verified pages only within §8 limits, with no extra full-stream upcast array.

The operation ledger stores the complete request fingerprint, exact original signed-request-blob key/hash, consumed-token digest, pinned response-blob key/hash, owner instance/generation/lease, next token and committed transition under CAS. An exact retry of a pinned incomplete page returns its byte-identical response without another Apply only while matching live domain scratch remains available for continuation. If scratch is lost after a receiver crash, the old operation is invalidated; the gateway returns `ReplayRestartRequired` and begins new authenticated replay from page 1. A pinned **final** response is different: its complete final state/result/proof are durable under the same ledger transition, so an exact retry returns the pinned blob without volatile scratch or Apply while the blob, **current** proof key/fingerprint, complete final prefix and 24-hour durable pin obligation remain valid. Its exact retry lookup by operation ID, request fingerprint and consumed-token digest precedes the 15-minute token-expiry check; expiry bars new Apply or continuation, not return of an already committed final response within its retained obligation. An invalid/stale final proof or changed active key/fingerprint requires source-authenticated page-1 restart even when a blob exists. Incomplete pinned pages still require a live scratch match; expired token, missing blob or lost scratch invalidates continuation and restarts from page 1. Altered requests fail even when a blob exists. A previously consumed token cannot run Apply again under its old operation. Cancellation before a proven absent pin discards private scratch; cancellation after a committed pin reports its committed truth; ambiguous outcomes use the reconciliation protocol below.

The existing `AggregateReconstructionRequest` positional constructor and bounded `POST /replay-state` whole-array route remain source/wire compatible. Add `POST /replay-state/pages` with records `PagedAggregateReconstructionRequest` and `PagedAggregateReconstructionResponse`; property names below are exact lower-camel JSON names under the pinned Web serializer, no unknown or duplicate members, and `byte[]` is canonical padded RFC 4648 Base64. Request fields are: `tenantId:string`, `domain:string`, `aggregateType:string`, `aggregateId:string`, `expectedHead:long`, `targetSequence:long`, `pageStart:long`, `pageCount:int` (0..256), `maxPageBytes:int` (1..67,108,864), `events:ReplayEventEnvelope[]` (only this verified page, with count equal to `pageCount`), `eventEvolutionProof:byte[]` (the §6 binary container, at most 2 MiB), `snapshotWitness:byte[]?` (exact §6 side-record bytes), `snapshotState:byte[]?` (exact original folded-state bytes), `continuationToken:byte[]?`, `operationId:string`, `includeTimeline:bool`, `requestId:string?`, and, for a transcript-v2 operation, the required `replayTranscriptSelection:byte[]?` of B4b. The two snapshot fields are both absent without prefix snapshot tags `0e`/`0f` and both present together only on the first page after an actor-authenticated witness readback; the signed prefix binds their SnapshotDigest and accumulator. The receiver obtains §6 `IAuthenticatedSnapshotSource.ReadAsync` actor evidence and checks side-record scope/key/covered sequence, original v1 storage-byte hash, folded-state byte hash, state/transform/protection hashes, actor batch/version and provider ETag against its source readback and signed prefix before deserializing the looked-up folded bytes into `DomainServiceCurrentState.SnapshotState`; request-carried bytes alone never prove these values. A missing, mixed, failed or unreadable snapshot witness causes the receiver to reject and discard the post-snapshot page **before Apply**. It asks the gateway for a fresh actor-authenticated page-1 request and newly signed proof with no snapshot authority, then starts a new replay operation; it never treats a tail page as complete history or locally changes its start to 1. The same rule applies after a protection outcome or readback failure, preserving the stored snapshot. The first page has null continuation and start 1 or witnessed snapshot sequence+1 when that sequence is below `long.MaxValue`; later pages have one current signed token. `targetSequence <= expectedHead`, all values are checked before allocation and the page range cannot exceed target/head. `/replay-state/pages` admits a zero-event request **only** for the signed empty-stream, B3 empty-target or witnessed snapshot zero-tail form, including §6's terminal max-sequence sentinel; it rejects a checkpoint anchor, checkpoint proof entry or projection metadata-only form even if its signature is valid. A count-zero terminal request has `pageStart=expectedHead=targetSequence=long.MaxValue`, no continuation and no event, and it cannot issue a next token. No `target+1` arithmetic is attempted at that value.

Response fields are `operationId:string`, `returnedPageStart:long`, `returnedPageEnd:long`, `returnedPageCount:int`, `nextContinuationToken:byte[]?`, `isComplete:bool`, `finalResult:AggregateReconstructionResult?`, `finalProof:byte[]?`. For an incomplete accepted page, the next token is non-null and both final fields are null; for complete success, the next token is null, `finalResult.StateJson` is the final state and `finalProof` is the exact signed complete-prefix container reaching target. A typed failure/cancellation has no authoritative final state or completion proof. The response's range/count must match the accepted request page, including start=target+1/end=target/count=0 for an ordinary witnessed zero tail, or start=end=target=`long.MaxValue`/count=0 for the terminal sentinel. A page ending at `long.MaxValue` is final and has no next token. Add nullable `PagedContext` properties to `AggregateReconstructionRequest` without changing its positional constructor; the new endpoint maps request scope, target, one-page `Events`, `IncludeTimeline`, `RequestId` and verified proof/continuation context into the existing `IAsyncAggregateReplay.ReplayAsync(AggregateReconstructionRequest, CancellationToken)` signature. On this route `Events` never means complete history; old processors and the synchronous adapter reject non-null `PagedContext`. Gateway verifies `finalProof` against original actor head, target and accumulated pages, then durably pins the exact final result/proof/response before exposing `finalResult`. The new endpoint and DTOs are additive; old `/replay-state` remains subject to §8 full-array bounds.

`PagedRequestFingerprint = SHA256("HX-EV-PAGED-REQUEST-1\0" || 01 || taggedRequestRecord)`, where the quoted separator ends in **one NUL byte** (`00`), never the two literal characters backslash and zero. `taggedRequestRecord` begins u16 field count `0011` (17) and then ordered one-byte tags with these exact §4 encodings: `01` U tenantId, `02` U domain, `03` U aggregateType, `04` U aggregateId, `05` N expectedHead, `06` N targetSequence, `07` N pageStart, `08` I pageCount, `09` I maxPageBytes, `0a` u32 bounded event count followed by one B for each canonical **stored** `ReplayEventEnvelope` value in page order, `0b` B exact EventEvolutionProof bytes, `0c` O(B) snapshotWitness, `0d` O(B) snapshotState, `0e` O(B) continuationToken, `0f` U operationId, `10` one byte includeTimeline (`00` false, `01` true), `11` O(U) requestId. The event count equals pageCount and is at most 256; every B/O length and the complete record are checked before allocation. The stored event value uses the §4 recursive canonical JSON renderer over the exact lower-camel stored DTO names (`sequenceNumber`, `eventTypeName`, `payload`, `serializationFormat`, `metadataVersion`, `messageId`, `correlationId`, `causationId`, and present additive `storedEventContractType`, `storedPayloadVersion`, `storedSerializationFormat`, `storedEventTypeName`, `storedDigest`, `registryFingerprint`), with byte arrays as canonical padded Base64. Its raw parsed member-presence map distinguishes absent from explicit null and includes only stored provenance, never an effective payload/view or caller-declared adaptation. Unknown, duplicate or wrong-case V2 member names fail. Preserve the original stored evidence and page order; a typed-object reserialization cannot erase presence or substitute bytes for this fingerprint. For a transcript-v2 page, P tag `04` binds B4b's `SelectedRequestHash`, and this 17-field fingerprint remains the field-validation record. The endpoint computes it before lookup and compares every retry's exact fingerprint, source evidence, **original signed proof bytes**, token and operation to the CAS-pinned request blob and ledger; changed bytes or meaning cannot receive a pinned response.

For page 1, null `continuationToken` has digest `SHA256("HX-EV-ABSENT-CONT-1\0" || 01 || 00)`; a **present empty** token is rejected at raw-presence validation before fingerprint or lease lookup. Every later token is nonempty signed exact bytes, and its digest is SHA-256 of those exact bytes, including signature. ReplayOwnerLease, ledger, pinned request/response blob keys and exact retry checks use this same null-versus-present rule; no empty-byte array aliases absence. The `/replay-state/pages` request parser rejects, by raw member presence before the stored-only PagedRequestFingerprint, any caller supplied `effectivePayload`, `effectiveEventContractType`, `effectivePayloadVersion`, `effectiveSerializationFormat`, `isAdapted`, `verifiedEffectiveEvent`, `verifiedEffectiveEvents` or any other effective/adaptation/verified-view member at any event or request level. Unknown members, including wrong-case variants, fail before lookup. Only the authenticated private reader derives effective views; a changed or unexpected member cannot retrieve a pinned response.

`AggregateReconstructionRequest` gains an additive nullable **public sealed immutable** `PagedContext` record containing public immutable `IReadOnlyList<VerifiedEffectiveEventView>` verified page views, copied exact `byte[]` EventEvolutionProof bytes, four addressed scope `string` fields, `long` expected head/target/page start/page end, `int` page count, `string` operation ID, opaque bounded `byte[]` scratch-handle token, copied exact signed `byte[]` continuation token, two copied 32-byte stored/effective accumulators and `bool` completion flag. The endpoint builds it only after actor source/proof validation. Its public constructor or factory lets an external `IAsyncAggregateReplay` implementer receive the verified page/proof, immutable scope/range and prior accumulators, plus an opaque bounded `byte[]` scratch-handle token. Constructors and getters defensively copy the token; only the gateway/domain ledger can authenticate its bytes and associate them with live private scratch. Constructors snapshot the view list and its byte fields, proof and accumulator arrays; a later caller mutation cannot change the admitted page. The gateway/domain operation ledger authenticates the token and its owner/generation and rechecks all proof/view hashes at the call boundary; no public member exposes an internal CLR type, raw mutable scratch or unverified state. The context grants the one async call a borrowed opaque handle under the operation/page fence **and a public `IPagedReplayStateSession StateSession`**. This session is supplied in process, never JSON-bound, and has `ReadPriorAsync(byte[] handle, CancellationToken): ValueTask<ReadOnlyMemory<byte>>` and `WriteSuccessorAsync(byte[] priorHandle, ReadOnlyMemory<byte> canonicalState, string serializerId, CancellationToken): ValueTask<byte[]>`. `ReadPriorAsync` authenticates the handle's scope, operation, owner instance, scratch generation and current page lease and returns a defensively copied, charged canonical prior state; the external async replay implementation can deserialize and Apply its verified page. `WriteSuccessorAsync` follows B5: before returning a task or suspending, it authenticates the handle, validates the serializer, reserves the B6 capacity and copies the canonical bytes once into a private owner, then validates and hashes that copy and CAS-creates **one** private successor from it under that same owner/generation/page lease. The session also exposes B4's `AppendTimelineEntry`. It returns only a defensively copied opaque successor handle, never a mutable reference to stored state. Both calls propagate cancellation and reject another operation, stale handle, second successor, prior-state mutation or publication of intermediate state. `PagedProgress` names exactly this successor handle; the ledger validates proof/range, resulting state hash and CAS readback, commits it once, invalidates the prior handle and clears its full old capacity. Ambiguous successor writes reconcile by operation ID and handle generation before retry, without another Apply; a failed or cancelled transition preserves the prior committed private state until no obligation refers to it. The old handle is invalidated and its full capacity cleared on a committed transition; on failure, cancellation or restart the ledger retains or clears it according to the reconciliation state, never exposes it to a caller or a second operation. Only the async `IAsyncAggregateReplay` implementation may consume `PagedContext`; every old/synchronous adapter rejects a non-null value before Apply. `AggregateReconstructionResult` gains an additive nullable **public sealed immutable** `PagedProgress` record, with a public constructor or factory, containing an opaque bounded defensively copied `byte[]` resulting scratch-handle token, resulting stored/effective accumulators, exact processed start/end/count and final-state flag. These public immutable fields have only public types and are transport-neutral; the gateway alone can commit or invalidate a handle under the operation ledger. The async implementation returns this progress after a verified page without publishing intermediate state or timeline as authority. The endpoint matches its range/chains to the signed proof and durable ledger, maps it to `PagedAggregateReconstructionResponse`, and exposes `FinalResult` only after final proof and durable pin verification. A missing, mismatched or cancelled progress returns no authoritative completion.

The signed purpose-05 token already binds operation ID and nonce. A durable `ReplayOwnerLease` keyed by `(tenant, domain, aggregate type, aggregate ID, operation ID, exact token digest)` has `HX-EV-REPLAY-OWNER-1\0 || 01 || 000e` and ordered tags `01` U tenant, `02` U domain, `03` U aggregate type, `04` U aggregate ID, `05` U operation ID, `06` B32 exact token digest, `07` U stable domain-service instance ID, `08` U authenticated endpoint ID, `09` N private scratch generation, `0a` B32 current RegistryFingerprint, `0b` B32 EventTransformHash, `0c` Q issued UTC, `0d` Q expiry UTC no earlier than token expiry, `0e` N monotonic CAS generation. Its actor/gateway-owned linearizable readback, not a caller field, is authority. The gateway selects that exact live instance for every later page; the receiver compares owner ID and scratch generation under the operation fence **before Apply**, and renews the lease/next generation before issuing the next token. Authentication of the endpoint and lease readback prevents a load balancer from routing a continuation to a different instance. If instance, lease or scratch is lost, invalidate the operation and restart authenticated replay at page 1; a deployment without enforceable affinity cannot advertise paged replay readiness. A durably committed final response is still returned from its pin without instance or scratch, subject to the current proof and retained obligation checks above.

Before any page Apply, CAS-pin an encrypted, authenticated **exact original request blob** keyed by `(tenant, scope, operation ID, page start, consumed-token digest)` containing the canonical 17-field request record, exact original signed `EventEvolutionProof`/continuation bytes, exact request-mode proof carrier bytes and their SHA-256/fingerprint. Preserve signature byte identity; a newly signed semantically equivalent claim is a different request, never an exact retry. The request blob uses the same scope authorization, 24-hour minimum retention, obligation-based CAS deletion and 128 MiB per-blob maximum as response pins, and is charged to both B6 storage levels (the operation's 1 GiB per-operation quota and the deployment replay-storage ceiling); reserve its capacity before Apply and return `ContinuationCapacityHold` if unavailable. Ambiguous pin creation is reconciled by exact blob readback before Apply. On retry, retrieve and compare the caller's fingerprint **and exact signed bytes** with this pinned blob before checking a previously committed response; return pinned bytes without re-signing or re-Applying. Missing/corrupt original proof bytes holds or restarts from authenticated page 1, never fabricates equivalent signatures. A pinned final response remains retrievable through this durable request blob even after owner scratch is gone.

The **gateway also pins before sending** the exact fully encoded, signed `/replay-state/pages` request bytes and exact proof carrier under that same `(tenant, scope, OperationId, pageStart, consumed-token digest)` identity. It reserves the checked request-blob quota, writes the authenticated encrypted blob, and reads back the byte-for-byte payload/hash, signature, scope and retention obligation **before** transport send; receiver-side pinning before Apply remains a separate check. A lost response or gateway restart first reads this outbound pin and resends its bytes unchanged, including the same signatures and JSON/Base64 spelling. An ambiguous outbound pin creation reconciles by operation/page and exact hash without sending a new encoding. If the pin cannot be recovered or authenticated, the gateway returns `ReplayRestartRequired`, invalidates that operation and begins a fresh page-1 operation with a new identity; it never re-signs the old operation or asks the receiver to accept semantically equivalent bytes as an exact retry. Caller cancellation after the send starts retains the pin and follows the same recovery path.

The 65,536-entry/64 MiB durable continuation ledger is a metadata index, not the response-byte store. Keep exact encoded retry responses in a separate durable CAS blob store keyed by operation ID, page start and consumed-token digest, with a **128 MiB actual encoded per-response** hard bound, charged with the request blobs to both B6 storage levels, expiry no earlier than the ledger's 24-hour retention. Each blob is keyed by tenant, addressed scope and operation/page/token digest, encrypted at rest with authenticated readback, and readable only by the gateway/domain principal authorized for that exact operation; cross-tenant lookup and payload logging are forbidden. After every retry, rollback and proof obligation closes (never earlier than ledger retention), CAS-delete the encrypted blob and revoke its operation access/key, then read back absence. A failed deletion or revocation holds quota/capacity for reconciliation rather than silently leaking the state copy. Startup recovery performs the same bounded cleanup; cancellation does not bypass it. The cap includes the complete Web JSON response: final state, optional timeline, proof, Base64 expansion, JSON escaping, metadata and token. The separately allowed 64 MiB raw state and 64 MiB timeline do **not** imply their combined encoded response fits. Before invoking Apply, atomically reserve a conservative checked upper bound for the requested page response and ledger transition. A final page reserves enough for its maximum admitted encoded state/timeline/proof or returns `FinalResponseLimit` before Apply; an ordinary page that cannot fit may be shrunk and re-signed **before** admission or returns `ContinuationCapacityHold`. A signed admitted page is immutable, so no post-admission shrink is allowed. If optional timeline causes `FinalResponseLimit`, a fresh authenticated **state-only** replay with `includeTimeline=false` may be started from page 1 under a new operation; no failed oversized response claims completion. State-only output remains subject to the same actual encoded cap.

Compute the page and any final state/proof in private charged scratch **after** reservation. Serialize the exact `PagedAggregateReconstructionResponse` once under the pinned Web JSON/Base64 codec and check actual length against its reservation and the 128 MiB cap. If it exceeds the cap, return `FinalResponseLimit` for a final page or `ContinuationCapacityHold` for an incomplete page, without authoritative transition. Commit by one linearizable operation: create the immutable exact response blob and, for a final page, immutable final result/proof under the same operation ID; CAS the ledger pointer to their exact hashes, request fingerprint, consumed-token digest and next-token/completion state. A backend with a serializable multi-key transaction may commit all three together. Otherwise the blob/final objects are prepared immutable first and **only** the ledger-pointer CAS is the authoritative transition; they are invisible until that pointer commits. Read back blob, ledger pointer and final result/proof under the same durable operation identity before returning response bytes or exposing/consuming a next token. The prior token remains authoritative until the pointer's commit is proven.

After **any** blob create, final-result create, ledger CAS or readback error, including a lost acknowledgement, retain reserved quota, operation ID, token and private scratch; classify the outcome as `ReplayCommitAmbiguous`. Under the same linearizable operation fence, read back **all three** objects and exact blob bytes/hash, token transition, request fingerprint and final proof/result; for an incomplete page the final-result object must be proven absent. If the pointer, blob and required final-result presence/absence exactly match the proposed commit, return the pinned bytes and committed truth without another Apply. If the old pointer and token remain unchanged and the backend proves no committed transition or in-flight CAS can later appear, release quota, discard prepared orphans and scratch, and permit a new source-authenticated page-1 replay. Any mixed, missing, stale or inconclusive evidence holds for reconciliation with quota and operation identity retained; it never releases capacity, retries Apply under the uncertain token or reports completion. A crash before commit uses the same readback classification on recovery. A crash after proven commit returns the exact pinned blob on identical retry. Incomplete committed pages require matching live scratch for **continued** Apply, otherwise `ReplayRestartRequired`; a final committed pin needs no scratch. Final retry precedes token-expiry rejection while its 24-hour obligation, current proof key/fingerprint and complete prefix remain valid; expiration still forbids new Apply or continuation. A missing/invalid final blob/proof restarts from authenticated page 1. Test a capacity failure after computation, lost CAS acknowledgement, mixed readback, lost incomplete response and lost final response after token expiry.

`NamedProjectionReadScope` is descriptive routing input, **never authorization**. The trusted query router issues one unforgeable store-verified `NamedProjectionReadCapability` after authenticating the principal and current catalog/access policy. Add nullable init-only `byte[]? ReadCapability` (`readCapability`) to the public `NamedProjectionReadScope`, preserving its constructor; the router sets a private copy of exactly 32 CSPRNG bytes, while the store looks up only SHA-256 of that token in a tenant-scoped durable CAS/readback capability index. The bound record contains authenticated principal identity, tenant, domain, HandlerRouteId, key-space, backend identity, ownership mode, optional aggregate, allowed exact logical keys or constrained prefix, allowed read operation (`Get` or `GetMany`), authoritative expiry UTC no later than five minutes after issuance, nonce and catalog/authorization revision. Raw token bytes are never logged or stored, and a caller-created scope without a live matching index record conveys no authority. On every route-aware `GetAsync` and `GetManyAsync`, `DaprReadModelStore` verifies the capability index and tenant scope under the trusted store, checks the authenticated current principal from request context and catalog/authorization revision, requires the requested store, route, keys and operation to be within its grant, and checks expiry against authoritative time **before** root or row lookup. A public constructor, copied capability for another principal, stale/revoked revision, wrong route/key or expired grant yields typed `ReadModelAccessDenied` with no existence signal, read-model bytes or partial bulk result. Root/row proof and final fence/UTC checks remain mandatory after this access check. The legacy store/key-only API cannot be used to inspect protected versioned key spaces.

An exact-key grant never broadens to a prefix when the inline 1 KiB capability record cannot hold its keys. For 1..256 requested exact logical keys, store a separate tenant-scoped immutable authenticated `HX-EV-QUERY-KEYSET-1\0 || 01 || u16 count || sorted unique U key` blob of at most 256 KiB; each key is at most 512 UTF-8 bytes under the named-index rule. The inline record stores only the blob's immutable key, B32 exact blob hash and u16 count, still within 1 KiB. Issuance reserves record **and** blob quota, stages both under one CAS transaction or a recoverable token-hash operation, reads back exact bytes and publishes the token only after both are proven durable. Every requested key is checked against the authenticated exact set before any row/root read; a changed, missing or extra key denies without existence leakage. Expiry/revocation CAS cleanup of token and blob is atomic or reconciled by token hash, blob hash and record versions; ambiguous deletion retains both quota charges until authenticated readback. A prefix grant is legal only when the caller explicitly requested that prefix and policy authorized it, never as a substitute for an exact set.

The exact-key blob has its **own** tenant-scoped active quota: at most **100,000 live key-set blobs** and **1 GiB encoded blob bytes including storage/index overhead** per tenant, separate from the capability-record limit of 100,000 live records and 128 MiB encoded index. Issuance reserves both charges under one token-hash operation before either record or blob is made active; saturation of either returns `ReadModelAccessUnavailable` before token issue or row lookup. A token and blob are retired together by authenticated expiry/revocation, CAS deletion and readback; ambiguous deletion retains **both** charges until exact record version and blob hash/absence reconcile. An orphaned blob cannot be counted free, an inline token cannot name a missing blob, and a caller never receives a partial grant.

Add `AggregateReconstructionStatus.InProgress = 3` after the existing `Succeeded = 0`, `Partial = 1` and `Failed = 2` values, and add nullable init-only `PagedProgress` to `AggregateReconstructionResult` without changing its existing eight-field positional constructor or deconstruction. For an incomplete accepted `/replay-state/pages` call, that result is exactly `Status=InProgress`, `StateJson=null`, `LastAppliedSequenceNumber` equal to the **verified completed page end only**, `FailedSequenceNumber=null`, `FailedEventType=null`, `ErrorCategory=None`, `Message=null`, `Timeline=null`, and a non-null verified `PagedProgress` bound to the ledger CAS/readback. It is neither `Succeeded` nor `Partial` and conveys no authoritative final state. The pages endpoint maps this status to `isComplete=false`, null `finalResult` and `finalProof`, and exactly one pinned non-null next token; it never publishes the intermediate result as a final result. Only a signed, completed whole prefix reaching the fixed target may return `Succeeded` with authoritative `StateJson`, `FinalResult`, no next token and a verified final proof. The old `/replay-state` route rejects `InProgress` before serializing its old response, so an old consumer cannot mistake a page for a complete reconstruction. A failed or cancelled page carries no `PagedProgress` that authorizes continuation and preserves last-good state.

For production named-projection mutations add `IVersionedNamedProjectionBatchWriter.TryCommitAsync(VerifiedNamedProjectionBatch request, CancellationToken cancellationToken): Task<ReadModelBatchResult>`. `VerifiedNamedProjectionBatch` is an immutable, defensively copied request with exact addressed `StoreName`, `TenantId`, `Domain`, `HandlerRouteId`, declared `KeySpaceId` and prefix, `OwnershipMode` (`aggregate` or `shared`), optional `AggregateType`/`AggregateId` (required for aggregate ownership and absent for shared ownership), authenticated event source proof and current effective-view digest, stable `OperationId` and enclosing `ReadModelBatchScope.BatchId`, expected certified root hash/generation, coordinator ID/fence generation, and ordered `ReadModelBatchOperation` values including kind, `ValueTypeName`, policy, expected logical ETag, TTL and bounded canonical value bytes. The trusted dispatcher creates a `VerifiedNamedProjectionBatch` only from a validated route/page and a store-verified write capability bound to the current catalog, source proof, root and fence; a caller-created instance is transport data, not authority. The writer reauthenticates that capability, catalog route/key-space/backend, source and operation identity, current root and shared fence before staging. It applies concurrency to the committed logical value, stages immutable shadow rows, computes exact batch/readback and complete-row-set proofs, then publishes only a certified root/checkpoint pointer under §6. It returns `ReadModelBatchResult` only after readback, with conflict, retryable and indeterminate outcomes distinct. Both `IVerifiedDomainProjectionHandler` and migrated `SharedProjectionEpochCoordinator` use this one seam. The existing six-field `ReadModelBatchScope(StoreName,TenantId,Domain,AggregateId,ProjectionType,BatchId)` remains unchanged: map its store/tenant/domain, stable BatchId and projection type explicitly into the new request, verify that its aggregate ID equals the source for aggregate ownership, and for shared ownership treat its aggregate ID only as original source-delivery provenance rather than the shared key owner. Its old opaque marker hash never substitutes for HandlerRouteId, key-space, root or fence authority. Generic `IReadModelBatchStore.ExecuteAsync` remains source-compatible for ordinary keys but is denied write access to protected versioned generations without this authenticated adapter.

Finite-leaf expiry scheduling is incremental: at a certified root transition register a job only for a new/changed finite leaf, or for a successor explicitly rebased under the current root; unchanged jobs retain their original visibility generation and expiry by reference and are never re-enqueued for every root. At most one active job exists per finite logical leaf. A superseded job is CAS tombstoned and compacted only after its successor/root obligation is read back; ambiguous deletion is reconciled by original job ID before releasing capacity. Cap each encoded job at 1 KiB, active jobs at 1,000,000, and the active scheduler index at 1 GiB per route/key-space. Reserve checked capacity before root publication; saturation is a typed capacity hold with prior certified root still authoritative. The §6 stale-root rebase, exact maintenance OperationId and fail-closed query expiry checks remain mandatory. The shared global-ordinal log has at most 1 GiB hot bytes. Seal contiguous content-addressed segments of at most 64 MiB into a tenant-scoped authenticated archive; hot plus retained archive counts toward B6's 64 GiB retained named-state ceiling, which spans every route, key space, operation and generation in the stable deployment/backend scope. Each archival transition commits exact segment start/end ordinals, content hash, predecessor/successor anchor and current root under the same fence, then reads it back. Replay proves a gapless ordinal chain, every source proof/root hash and every archive link before Apply. Segments referenced by replay, backup, rollback, retry or source-history obligations remain; compact only after a durable certified checkpoint/retention decision proves no reference. Reaching either quota holds the next transition before its ordinal/root commit; authoritative history is never dropped to make room.

The §6 `NamedProjectionReadCapability` index is tenant-scoped and quota reserved **before** token issuance: at most 100,000 live records and 128 MiB encoded index bytes per tenant, with each record at most 1 KiB and lifetime at most five minutes. The issuer charges exact encoded record and index overhead using checked arithmetic under the capability-store CAS fence. `ReadModelAccessUnavailable` on saturation grants no token and no fallback read. Expired records are CAS-deleted only after authenticated expiry and exact record-version readback; an ambiguous delete is reconciled by token hash and version before releasing quota, and a changed/revoked record is never recycled as an active grant. This quota is independent of the 256-key, 8 MiB proof, 64 MiB result and 128 MiB scratch query limits.

### B3. Complete prefixes, snapshots and public compatibility

This refines §§3, 6, 8–9. Fix scope, admitted head and inclusive target at operation admission (`0 ≤ target ≤ head ≤ long.MaxValue`). Authenticate actual source under that operation. New later appends do not extend its target; a changed/invalid fixed-head proof restarts page 1 without reusing partial state. Never silently clamp a requested beyond-head target into success. Existing `Replay_UpToSequenceBeyondLastEvent_ReturnsLastValidState` documents legacy behavior only: a legacy gateway must resolve and disclose the actual target before verified admission; it cannot assert a signed prefix through unavailable events.

Before Apply, require a contiguous ordered page, exact per-event route proofs and signed prefix count/start/end/head/target/accumulator; reject gaps, duplicates, reordered authenticated entries, truncation and mixed scope. Pages are at most 256 events/64 MiB readable and 64 MiB proof; command replay uses 2 MiB proof including its final wrapped/Base64 command-state carrier. Reduce and re-sign an unadmitted page until the entire live phase fits B6. Never shrink, re-sign or alter a pinned page under its existing operation. Each committed next page starts at prior end+1; final success requires end=target and complete transcript/state proof, not merely exhaustion of the supplied array.

The §6 count-zero forms remain exact: empty stream start=1/end=head=target=0; witnessed snapshot or projection checkpoint at k<head's integer limit uses start=k+1/end=k/head=target=k; at `long.MaxValue` use start=end=head=target=k, count=0 with the appropriate anchor and no increment/next token. A count-one terminal event at k is distinct and applies once. Aggregate replay rejects projection checkpoint anchors. A checkpoint cannot substitute for a snapshot or complete history. To preserve replay-at-zero for an existing stream, selected v2 additionally admits an **empty-target prefix** with start=1/end=target=count=0 and the authenticated actual head>0, no anchors or routes, and scoped genesis accumulators. This is the only exception, applied in §6, to its prohibition of every other count-zero nonempty-head form; it proves the requested empty prefix, never that the stored stream is empty. Old v1 parsers must not receive the added form.

Snapshot reuse requires the exact approved v1 storage bytes and paired `:evolution-witness`, matching source scope/key/sequence, batch operation/logical version, authenticated provider readback, folded-byte/storage-byte hashes, serializer, protection, `StateSchemaApplyHash`, `EventTransformHash` and covered accumulator. Authenticate storage/ciphertext independently from readable folded bytes. Deserialize only proven folded bytes. Missing/stale/free snapshots, protected unreadability, changed bytes or mismatched pair discard the **entire** candidate tail before Apply and request fresh page 1 without snapshot authority. A snapshot whose covered sequence equals a nonzero requested target **below the actual admitted head** is ineligible for the zero-tail shortcut: for snapshot=target=7/head=9, discard its entire candidate tail before Apply and perform full authenticated replay from 1 through the original target 7 under actual head 9. Do not lower the admitted head, extend the target, or invent a count-zero prefix. A snapshot whose covered sequence **exceeds** the requested target (for example snapshot 9, target 7, head 9) is likewise ineligible: folded state cannot be unwound, so discard it before Apply and perform the same full authenticated replay from 1 through the original target under the actual head. This fallback uses existing nonempty prefix codecs; stored snapshot/witness bytes remain intact. Preserve stored snapshot bytes. Cancellation propagates and infrastructure failure cannot fabricate an empty stream. Full authenticated replay may still fail on unreadable event history; fallback never skips it. Without approved folded runtime and its witness path, use full replay and claim no snapshot tail-cost optimization.

For `includeTimeline=true`, **always start at sequence 1 without a snapshot**: current public timeline means one post-event state for every event through target. A folded snapshot cannot reconstruct earlier entries. Target zero returns a completed empty timeline using the exact empty-stream or empty-target form above; `false` returns null. B4 keeps all timeline state private until final completion. B7's projection checkpoint optimization is independent of this aggregate timeline rule.

Keep existing public constructors/deconstruction, required `ReplayEventEnvelope.MetadataVersion`, `long? GlobalPosition`, stored `Payload`/`EventTypeName`/format meanings and old endpoints. New async replay is §3's `IAsyncAggregateReplay` with token-aware `ReplayAsync(request, token)` and explicit aggregate-route selection; it is discoverable independently of keyed command processors. Hopped sources require it, and projections require verified handlers. Existing sync replay/rehydrator adapters are bounded, zero-hop only, reject `PagedContext`, and check cancellation immediately before/after invocation and between events where the adapter owns the loop. They cannot promise interruption within synchronous Apply. A nonzero-hop source never reaches stored-envelope Apply. Command processors receive only purpose-07 proven complete state, with all committed pages verified via the durable ledger, or `CommandStateUnproven` before invocation.

Keep legacy `Partial` results as diagnostics only where that contract already exists; never present them as a successful state/checkpoint/query or use them as command input. Paged `InProgress` has null final state/result/proof/timeline, `ErrorCategory=None`, a verified page-end sequence and opaque progress/token only. Last-good diagnostics must be retained **before** Apply (B5); the current catch-and-serialize mutated object is not sufficient. No intermediate timeline is publicly successful, even when signed.

### B4. Authenticated private timeline and atomic page transition

**BH37-3 (§11.5).** §6 promises final-only public results and exact pinned requests and responses; this private protocol also binds the cumulative timeline to the successor. It neither introduces public chunked timelines nor permits intermediate `Succeeded`/`Partial` responses. These records supplement the §6 route/prefix proof; they do not independently authorize events.

Use §4 primitives: `U`/`B` are u32 big-endian byte length then strict UTF-8/exact bytes; `N` is signed-i64 big-endian restricted to `0..2^63-1`, `I` is signed-i32 big-endian restricted to `0..2^31-1`, `H` is exactly 32 bytes. The separators below end in one NUL. Ordered tagged records have the stated u16 count and one-byte tags `01..count`; reject duplicate/missing/unknown/out-of-order fields, invalid lengths and trailing bytes before allocation. Canonical state uses the registered state serializer; no current serializer may regenerate a pinned retry.

Reject negatives and values above those signed maxima **on encoding and immediately on decoding every I/N**, before arithmetic, allocation, range interpretation or use. This includes nested S head/target, E sequence/version, P pageStart/count/timeline counts/bytes/generation, selector versions/revisions/ticks, manifest lengths/indices and prior-state sequence/generation. Positive payload versions still require `1..1024` after scalar decoding; page counts still require `0..256`. `u32` length/count framing remains unsigned `0..2^32-1` followed by its smaller enclosing content cap; it is not I, and a high-bit u32 length does not become a negative scalar. Q uses checked nonnegative N ticks. LB-08 exercises both encode and decode boundaries, including nested scope, without changing any previously valid literal codec bytes.

| Codec | Exact preimage/fields |
| --- | --- |
| Operation scope S | `U tenant || U domain || U aggregateType || U aggregateId || U OperationId || N head || N target || H RegistryFingerprint || H EventTransformHash || H StateSchemaApplyHash || byte includeTimeline`. The mode byte is exactly 00/01. |
| Timeline genesis T0 | `SHA256("HX-EV-REPLAY-TIMELINE-1\0" || 01 || B S)`. State-only mode retains this hash/count=0/bytes=0 with no entries; mode/scope substitution changes it. |
