Redelivery reauthenticates source/configuration, recomputes the complete set, and compares every route record, shared pin and manifest bytes; changed source, route set or pin is `LegacyHandoffConflict` and never creates a second effect. The old JSON broker delivery without a D7 retained-custody handoff is acknowledged only under C4's logical-completion rule: after the shared binary send has durable broker acceptance, the side record, manifest, every route record and the pin/send intent read back, **and every addressed route has a durable terminal decision**. A crash before that point leaves it unacknowledged; a later redelivery reuses the full set and the existing route receipts. The outbox sends the one exact pinned binary delivery until durable broker acceptance; every logical route independently uses its marker and effect receipt, so one completed route cannot suppress another. A source lookup, batch readback or broker failure keeps the old JSON unacknowledged. Legacy JSON cannot assert `isAdapted` or bypass reservation/effect checks. The new `application/vnd.hexalith.eventstore.v2+octet-stream` route decodes the exact body and `hyevattestation`, builds `VerifiedDeliveryContext`, and verifies body, transport, signature and effective route before DTO binding/handler selection. JSON and binary binders never reinterpret each other's bytes. Reconcile old broker unacked counts, full handoff batches, outbox states and target acceptance before removing JSON ingress.

The durable legacy handoff manifest is C4's exact 23-tag `HX-EV-LEGACY-HANDOFF-1\0 || 01 || 0017` schema; the pre-integration tag assignment is superseded. Its tag `10` is exactly `SHA256("HX-EV-LEGACY-DECODED-1\0" || 01 || U tenant || U domain || U aggregate type || U aggregate ID || U event key || N sequence || U MessageId || B32 StoredDigest || B(§4 canonical decoded original stored-event JSON value) || B(exact decoded readable payload bytes) || B(exact derived protection-record bytes) || B(exact original CloudEvent core/ordered-header identity bytes whose hash is tag `0f`))`; the canonical renderer retains all known/unknown legacy members and null/absent distinctions, so raw whitespace is not an identity input. The complete handoff manifest is capped at 2 MiB and its route set at the authenticated 4,096-member physical-subscription bound before nested allocation; the send-intent B is capped at 1 MiB. The side record is tenant-scoped authenticated encrypted bounded storage keyed by that OperationId; it contains the exact original JSON body (at most the admitted 128 MiB raw-carrier bound) and core/header bytes, is capped as a complete encrypted side record at 193 MiB (C4, [I-26]), and is read back byte-for-byte before handoff commit or old-message acknowledgement. Before constructing the binary pin, parse those original bytes with the frozen legacy codec and compare **every** stored event field, readable payload and protection state with authenticated actor source and the newly rendered binary body under the frozen binary codec. Different whitespace can produce equivalent decoded content only after exact original broker pin/body bytes and decoded fields authenticate; changed content, scope, route set, side-record bytes or configuration revision is `LegacyHandoffConflict`. The manifest, original-body side record, all route records and send intent share one committed handoff pointer; partial readback cannot acknowledge the original JSON delivery. Handoff/side-record retention lasts through broker retry, rollback, route-effect and late-delivery obligations.

A queued original JSON delivery may perform **one explicit JSON-to-binary pin migration** only when authenticated actor source, original broker component/topic/physical-subscription/configuration-revision evidence and old publication/outbox record prove the same MessageId, scope, StoredDigest, original JSON identity and **complete addressed logical route set**, and independently prove no prior binary pin or send. Under the global MessageId CAS, install one durable migration obligation and the exact new attested binary pin plus the batch-wide handoff manifest and **every** route record above. This is a one-time transition from proved JSON publication, not a second global pin. Read back obligation, shared pin/send intent, manifest and every route record before any send; the old JSON delivery is acknowledged only under C4's rule. A repeated JSON delivery resolves to those same bytes and complete set. Ambiguous prior binary send, missing historical route-set/configuration proof, incomplete batch or conflicting pin holds `LegacyHandoffConflict`/reconciliation without acknowledgement or effect. Current publisher configuration and broker attempt ID cannot supply missing historical route identity.

Binary readiness uses three exact version-1 claims, independently of the immutable event delivery pin. Each starts with its ASCII separator ending NUL, codec `01`, a big-endian u16 field count and ascending one-byte tags under §4; unknown, missing, repeated, out-of-order or trailing fields fail. `RegistryFingerprint` is the raw 32-byte current **domain-scoped** value, not its hex text. One claim names exactly one domain; a multi-domain subscription supplies one independent entry and lease per domain. All U strings use strict UTF-8 and the existing domain, route and key grammars where applicable.

| Claim | Exact separator/count and tagged fields in order |
| --- | --- |
| MembershipClaim | `HX-EV-MEMBERSHIP-1\0`, `0008`: `01` U domain, `02` U authenticated component, `03` U topic, `04` N positive monotonic revision, `05` B32 RegistryFingerprint, `06` B member set, `07` Q issued UTC, `08` Q expires UTC. |
| ConsumerConfiguration | `HX-EV-CONSUMER-CONFIG-1\0`, `000e`: `01` U consumer identity, `02` U domain, `03` U component, `04` U topic, `05` U stable broker subscription ID, `06` U stable HandlerRouteId (a stable external route ID for external members), `07` U canonical event-type selector, `08` U tenant-scope rule, `09` B32 binary-carrier capability hash, `0a` U duplicate-safety mode, `0b` U dedup/receipt-provider ID, `0c` B32 provider-backed duplicate-probe receipt digest, `0d` U exact provider backend identity, `0e` N configuration revision equal to MembershipClaim revision. |
| ConsumerLeaseClaim | `HX-EV-CONSUMER-LEASE-1\0`, `000f`: `01` U consumer identity, `02` U domain, `03` U component, `04` U topic, `05` N revision, `06` B32 SHA-256 of exact MembershipClaim, `07` B32 configuration hash from its member row, `08` B32 RegistryFingerprint, `09` B32 binary-carrier capability hash, `0a` U duplicate-safety mode (`DurableDedup` or `ProviderIdempotency`), `0b` U provider ID, `0c` B32 duplicate-probe receipt digest, `0d` U provider backend identity, `0e` Q issued UTC, `0f` Q expires UTC. |

| PublicationFenceClaim | `HX-EV-PUBLICATION-FENCE-1\0`, `0009`: `01` U domain, `02` U component, `03` U topic, `04` N revision, `05` B32 SHA-256 of exact MembershipClaim, `06` B32 RegistryFingerprint, `07` U publisher operation ID, `08` Q expires UTC, `09` B exactly 16-byte broker nonce. |

The `ConsumerLeaseClaim` row above is the historical `000f` lease codec and remains byte-for-byte unchanged, including V23 fixture literals. Its tag `07` hashes an exact ConsumerConfiguration row. For production effect-mode admission use `HX-EV-CONSUMER-CONFIG-2\0 || 02 || 000f`, preserving tags `01..0a` with their declared types/meaning, then `0b` U effect mode (`AtomicStore` or `ProviderIdempotency`), `0c` U dedup/receipt-provider ID, `0d` B32 provider-backed V3 duplicate-probe receipt digest, `0e` U exact provider backend identity and `0f` N active configuration revision. Its hash occupies the same lease tag-`07` slot; a V23 legacy configuration row remains historical fixture evidence, not production effect-mode readiness. Broker/subscriber follow the lease hash to this authenticated V2 row and verify effect mode at **row tag `0b`**; compare V2 row tags `0a`/`0c`/`0d`/`0e` to lease tags `0a`/`0b`/`0c`/`0d` respectively, and compare V2 row tag `0f` to the active lease/membership revision and current catalog before send or effect. No lease field is invented or its historical count changed.

The member set is u32 count followed by each `U consumerIdentity || B32 configurationHash`, sorted by unsigned UTF-8 consumer identity; duplicate identities fail.
For a physical subscription with multiple handlers, the broker enumerates one stable logical consumer identity per `(physical subscription ID, HandlerRouteId)`, encoded `U physical subscription ID || U HandlerRouteId` and rendered as canonical lowercase hex in ConsumerConfiguration tag `01` and the membership set. Every logical member has its own configuration row and route-specific lease, though the physical subscription receives one pinned message. Tag `07` is the canonical type for one type or exact `*` for an attested nonempty multi-type set. **Production tag `09` for both single-type and multi-type routes** is `SHA256("HX-EV-BINARY-CAP-2\0" || 01 || B32 base binary-carrier capability hash || B32 current HandlerCompatibilityHash || B32 EffectProviderConfigurationHash || B(exact route-capability evidence))`. `EffectProviderConfigurationHash = SHA256("HX-EV-EFFECT-CONFIG-1\0" || 01 || U effect mode || U receipt-provider ID || U backend ID || B32 canonical provider-options hash)`. Internal route evidence is `B(exact 52 primary row) || O(B(exact 43 verified row)) || u32 extra-row count || each B(exact 58 row) sorted as §5`; a single-type route uses zero extras and still binds its handler/filter/state compatibility and effect provider. External evidence is the exact signed carrier below. Changing any route, handler, filter, state or effect configuration advances membership revision and invalidates old leases. The broker checks all logical members behind a physical subscription under one revision before the one pinned send. The unchanged V23 single-member fixture and older multi-type formula are historical codec examples only; its literal `consumer` identity is insufficient for production.

`ExternalRouteCapabilityManifest = "HX-EV-EXTERNAL-ROUTE-1\0" || 01 || 000d` has ordered tags `01` U domain, `02` U physical subscription ID, `03` U stable external HandlerRouteId, `04` B route set, `05` B32 filter/config digest, `06` B32 handler implementation digest, `07` U effect mode, `08` U receipt-provider ID, `09` U provider backend ID, `0a` B32 EffectProviderConfigurationHash, `0b` B32 HandlerCompatibilityHash, `0c` B32 ExternalDependencyClosureHash, `0d` B exact external dependency-closure record bytes. Route set B contains u32 positive count and sorted unique `(U canonical type, I current version, U format)` rows. The closure record is `HX-EV-EXTERNAL-CLOSURE-1\0 || 01 || u32 positive row count || sorted G-format §5 dependency rows || u32 positive root count || sorted root records || u32 edge count || sorted edge records`, capped at 1 MiB. A root record is `U role || U logical load identity || U dependency kind || B32 expanded-options/configuration hash`, with role exactly `handler`, `validator`, `filter`, `serializer`, `registration`, `effect-provider` or `receipt-provider`; every executable role used by the route has a root. An edge record is `U parent logical load identity || U parent kind || U child logical load identity || U child kind`, sorted by those four separately encoded keys. Every root and edge endpoint resolves to exactly one G row, every reachable managed/native load has a row, and no row is unreferenced by a root or transitive edge. G rows bind exact file bytes/ABI/loader-context hashes; roots bind exact options/configuration. Duplicate roots/edges, cycles not present in the actual loader graph, missing edges or a different loaded graph fail. A named root with no dependency still has its own G row and root record. `ExternalDependencyClosureHash = SHA256(exact complete closure record bytes)`; tag `0c` must equal this hash of tag `0d`, and both are covered by the purpose-`0b` signature. Its exact §6 carrier is signed for purpose `0b` by a predeclared broker-trusted external capability authority; consumer self-signing is insufficient. Manifest tag `0b` MUST equal `SHA256("HX-EV-EXTERNAL-HANDLER-1\0" || 01 || U domain || U external HandlerRouteId || B exact route set || B32 filter/config digest || B32 handler implementation digest || B32 EffectProviderConfigurationHash || B32 ExternalDependencyClosureHash)`; the broker recomputes it. Before lease issue and at active membership revision, the broker authority authenticates the endpoint's sealed loader graph and exact file/config hashes against every row, rejects duplicate/missing/dynamic loads and requires a new signed manifest/revision after any change. A self-reported closure without independent broker-authority verification is insufficient. The broker verifies signature, scope, route set, compatibility hash, closure and version-3 provider probe before using those exact carrier bytes in production tag-`09`. External multi-type uses `*` only with this manifest; unknown types are never admitted by wildcard.

Production duplicate-safety readiness requires **probe receipt version 3**, exact bytes `HX-EV-DEDUP-PROBE-3\0 || 03 || 0015`, then ordered tags `01..15`: `01` U tenant, `02` U domain, `03` U aggregate type, `04` U aggregate ID, `05` U test MessageId, `06` B32 test DeliveryDigest, `07` U HandlerRouteId A, `08` U distinct HandlerRouteId B, `09` U effect mode, `0a` U provider backend identity, `0b` N configuration revision, `0c` I A attempts (3: injected attempt, retry, duplicate), `0d` I B attempts (2: first and duplicate), `0e` U crash point (exact `effect-before-receipt-commit`), `0f` I A committed-effect count after injected crash (0 or 1), `10` I A durable-receipt count then (equal to `0f`), `11` I final A committed-effect count (1), `12` I final B committed-effect count (1), `13` B32 final A receipt digest, `14` B32 final B receipt digest, `15` B32 authenticated provider query/commit transcript digest. Both routes receive the same scoped MessageId and DeliveryDigest on the same physical subscription; only HandlerRouteId differs in their eight-field C3 effect keys ([I-32]). Inject a crash between intended effect and receipt commit on A, restart, query its durable effect/receipt, retry A, deliver B and duplicate both. If A committed before crash, tags `0f`/`10` are both 1; otherwise both are 0 and retry commits once. Final route-specific effect and receipt counts are exactly one each, never MessageId-only dedup. The authenticated transcript binds both keys, crash boundary, pre/post queries, commits and duplicate attempts; broker independently queries and checks both route receipts. Its digest in tag `15` is SHA-256 of the exact provider-signed `HX-EV-DEDUP-TRANSCRIPT-3\0 || 03 || U provider backend identity || N configuration revision || u32 6 || rows` carrier, capped at 8 KiB before signing or decoding. The six ordered rows are A injected attempt, A durable query after restart, A retry, B first attempt, A duplicate and B duplicate. Each row is `B(exact eight-field HX-EV-EFFECT-KEY-2 bytes) || I attempt ordinal || one-byte operation` (`01` call or `02` read-only query) `|| one-byte observed commit` (`00` absent or `01` committed) `|| I cumulative committed-effect count || I cumulative durable-receipt count || U provider commit version/ETag` (empty only when absent) `|| O(B32 receipt digest)`. The provider signs the complete transcript through the exact §6 signed carrier with purpose `0c` and a separately trusted receipt-attestation key; tag `15` hashes that complete carrier including its key ID and signature. The broker verifies the signature, exact backend/configuration revision, both receipt queries and all six rows; a caller-supplied transcript is not evidence. For a committed row, its `U provider commit version/ETag` is the canonical ASCII decimal of effect-commit receipt tag `05` (no sign or leading zeros) followed by `:` and the exact nonempty commit receipt tag `06` ETag; split only at the first colon. Its present receipt digest is C3's `ReceiptDigest` over the complete precommit effect record, and tags `13`/`14` equal the final A/B row digests respectively. The broker/provider reads back that complete record with its commit and readback receipts and compares its eight-field key, mode, backend, result digest and actual commit fields; an unknown record field, version disagreement or digest without its record fails readiness. Production ConsumerConfiguration V2 tag `0d` and the unchanged ConsumerLeaseClaim tag `0c` bind SHA-256 of these exact V3 bytes under the current revision/backend; the historical V23 ConsumerConfiguration V1 tag `0c` remains fixture-only. Missing route, same-route pair, another route's receipt or unauthenticated transcript holds readiness. V23 V1 and earlier V2 framing are historical examples, insufficient for production. Route B in this V3 probe is an isolated provider-local test route on the **same effect mode, backend identity, provider options and configuration revision** as route A; it has a distinct HandlerRouteId and exact eight-field effect key, and cannot execute a live business effect. The provider provisions and tears down B under its authenticated test namespace while retaining the signed receipt/transcript. A live route's readiness requires a separate V3 probe for **each** effect mode/backend/configuration revision it uses; the probe for backend `store-a` never certifies another backend or option set. The broker compares each live route's effect configuration hash to that probe's authenticated backend/revision and requires both route-specific durable receipts; no test-route receipt is accepted as a live event effect receipt.
`configurationHash = SHA256(exact ConsumerConfiguration bytes)`. Broker authority verifies active rows, domain/fingerprint/revision, current HandlerCompatibilityHash and effect configuration, the V3 crash/two-route transcript and two independent durable receipts before signing membership/leases. The historical ConsumerLeaseClaim `000f` codec is unchanged and does not directly repeat an effect-mode field. At admission, follow its tag `07` exact ConsumerConfiguration hash to the authenticated active configuration row, verify that row's tag `0b` effect mode, provider/backend/probe, current membership revision, tag `09` carrier capability and lease signature/expiry. A changed mode with unchanged lease bytes changes the configuration hash and fails before publish or acknowledgement. A changed registry, handler, filter, state codec or effect provider/configuration advances membership revision and invalidates old leases. The capability hash binds exact binary/structured CloudEvents codecs, content type, attestation extension, routing-header verifier and route/effect evidence above. A configured provider name, V23 probe-V1 or single-route V2 receipt cannot substitute. Probe evidence remains durable and support-safe.

Each signed carrier is exactly `B(claim bytes) || U(purpose-specific key ID) || B(exact 64-byte IEEE P1363 signature)` with no trailing bytes, using §6 `HX-EV-SIG-1\0` framing and purposes `08` membership, `09` consumer lease, `0a` publication fence. The broker/component authority signs membership and fence; it signs leases or delegates them to an authenticated predeclared per-domain/component/topic authority. Authority keys and purposes are pinned separately from event route/delivery trust, with exact SPKI, validity and revocation checks. Neither event key nor consumer self-signing authorizes these claims. Reject noncanonical member order, nonpositive or reused revision, issued-after-expiry, expired claim, wrong purpose/key, mismatched domain/fingerprint/configuration, or a fence expiry later than either membership expiry or the **earliest active member lease expiry**.

The authoritative broker persists membership revision, exact signed member set/configuration hashes, matching leases and publication fences under one linearizable serialization boundary. `TryPublishAtRevision`, with C2's exact tenant-scoped signature, request and predicted accepted images and parent binding, atomically checks trusted broker UTC, membership and every active matching lease's issued/expiry interval, domain/fingerprint/configuration/probe hashes, fence expiry and nonce, exact active revision/member set and operation ID **at acceptance**; a membership activation or lease expiry before acceptance rejects without bytes. A joined/changed consumer cannot become active until its new probe and lease pass. A broker lacking this compare-and-accept primitive holds binary publishing with `ConsumerMembershipFenceUnavailable`. One global MessageId pin and one operation ID per shared component/topic serve all subscribers; no per-subscriber binary resend is created. Publisher obtains and prechecks fresh claims on every send, but its precheck never substitutes for broker acceptance-time checks.

`ExactCanonicalPinDigest = SHA256("HX-EV-BROKER-PIN-1\0" || 01 || B(exact decoded delivery body) || B(exact decoded hyevattestation))`; the body already contains the signed §7 CloudEvent core and routing-header fields (tags `1c..25`), so no unsigned transport-only broker header enters this digest. A global pin stores those canonical bytes and the deterministic renderer version for each permitted transport mode. It also retains exact original outbound bytes for same-mode retries. Binary mode uses the raw body and canonical padded Base64 extension; structured mode uses exact canonical padded Base64 `data_base64` and Binary extension. A broker mode conversion is accepted only if strict decoding gives the same pinned body, attestation, signed core attributes and routing metadata **and** exact canonical rendering for the received mode. Unknown attributes, noncanonical Base64 or changed decoded content/destination are `DeliveryPinConflict`; arbitrary byte equality between two different modes is not required. A same-mode retry must use its retained exact outbound bytes. No delivery/marker identity depends on unsigned transport-only headers.

The deterministic **structured** renderer emits one UTF-8 JSON CloudEvent object with keys sorted by unsigned UTF-8 name bytes, no insignificant whitespace and the §4 options-text string escaping rule. Required keys are `specversion`, `id`, `source`, `type`, `datacontenttype`, `data_base64` and `hyevattestation`; optional `subject` and `time` appear only when signed as present. `data_base64` and `hyevattestation` use canonical padded RFC 4648 Base64 of the exact pinned binary body/attestation. No `data` member or unknown attribute is allowed. Event `datacontenttype` is the signed `application/vnd.hexalith.eventstore.v2+octet-stream`; outer HTTP content type is `application/cloudevents+json`. The deterministic **binary** renderer uses the exact pinned raw body as HTTP/DAPR data, event content type as outer content type, and exact lowercase `ce-specversion`, `ce-id`, `ce-source`, `ce-type`, optional `ce-subject`, optional `ce-time`, and `ce-hyevattestation` with canonical padded Base64. Both renderers use the same canonical signed `time` text when present: seven fractional digits, original signed T offset, `Z` for zero offset and `+HH:MM`/`-HH:MM` otherwise. Application routing headers/metadata are the exact six signed lower-case `hx-*` keys already defined above, sorted as M; they remain outside the structured JSON CloudEvent object. Publisher pins the renderer version, exact canonical event object/body and application header map, plus actual outbound mode bytes. Ingress rejects duplicate/unknown event attributes, alternate Base64, changed signed fields, changed routing metadata or noncanonical received-mode rendering before comparing the decoded canonical pin. Hop-by-hop transport headers remain unsigned and cannot affect route or identity.

Broker idempotency, attempt registration, result observations and `GetPublicationReceipt` are C2's exact tenant-scoped per-attempt contract: an identical retry after an accepted send returns the same durable acceptance with no second publication, and changed bytes under one operation key always conflict. An ambiguous send or acknowledgement **first queries the exact attempt's complete observation chain**; an Accepted result is recorded without another send, a proved class-01 Rejected result permits a renewed fence and nonce for the same member send and pin, and an Unknown result or unavailable lookup holds with no new nonce or send. Durable receipt retention covers all event pin, retry, rollback and handoff obligations; expiry cannot turn an unresolved send into a fresh operation. §11.3 gives admitted signed broker claim vectors, distinct from event trust.

Publisher cutover is scoped to each affected domain/component/topic. Enumerate every internal and external active consumer from the authoritative membership claim and verify its exact signed lease, provider-backed duplicate probe and current RegistryFingerprint before any V2 binary send; unknown/unready members hold. A join, leave, configuration or fingerprint change increments the revision and invalidates existing fences/leases as described above. The publisher keeps one global pinned send per shared topic and retains old JSON ingress until queued legacy traffic, handoff outboxes and broker acceptance have drained with durable evidence. Binary decoding alone is never a cutover proof.

For an existing `CommandEnvelope`, preparation `OperationId` is **exactly the admitted execution command `MessageId`** (A4), validated for the addressed scope before the first prepare CAS and carried unchanged through gateway, actor retry and result lookup. Event MessageIds allocated later are separate. A non-command batch append caller supplies an additive required stable client OperationId; missing, changed or freshly generated-on-retry values fail before volatile generation. The same rule covers a zero-event no-op. An immutable client/gateway `OperationId` and the **canonical original command or batch input** define append preparation identity before any timestamp, MessageId, global position, protected payload, sidecar signature or result is generated. `AppendPreparationIdentity = SHA256("HX-EV-APPEND-PREP-1\0" || 01 || U OperationId || U tenant || U domain || U aggregateType || U aggregateId || B(canonical original request value under the §4 strict JSON renderer))`. The raw request and parsed presence map are bounded, authenticated and frozen before hashing; volatile generated fields are absent from this identity. The global linearizable preparation CAS key is `append-preparation:` plus lowercase hex `SHA256("HX-EV-APPEND-PREP-KEY-1\0" || 01 || U tenant || U domain || U aggregateType || U aggregateId || U OperationId)`. The record retains and compares that exact five-part tuple as well as `AppendPreparationIdentity`, so a hash collision fails closed. It creates `Preparing(tuple, identity, inputHash, ownerFence)` before generation. Equal command MessageIds in different **tenants** use different preparation keys; within one tenant, reuse of an execution MessageId in another scope is `CommandIdentityConflict` at admission (A8), and a changed original input in one scope conflicts. This namespace is separate from the global event-MessageId uniqueness index. Only its fenced owner may generate once and CAS an immutable `Prepared` capsule containing identity, original input hash, the selected writer mode/approved fingerprint, all generated IDs/timestamps/allocated positions, exact prepared raw/protected bytes and original protection record, original StoredDigest/decoder identity, encoding/digest sidecars, outbox intent, original bounded result bytes and full AppendOperationFingerprint. Preparation is **durable before** any MessageId reservation or actor save. An exact retry first reads and authenticates that capsule, compares the original input/identity and reuses every pinned value and byte; it never reruns a clock, ID allocator, protector, serializer or signer to compare against Committed. Different original input under one operation ID is `AppendPreparationConflict`. A missing, incomplete or ambiguous capsule is `AppendPreparationHold` before actor save until its CAS and no-save state are reconciled; a proven never-started preparation may be released under durable no-commit proof. Neither timeout nor caller cancellation guesses that proof. Generated global positions are allocated under the same fence and held by the capsule; retries neither skip nor reallocate them. The actor reads back capsule identity/fingerprint with the committed bundle.

Before generating any volatile append value or allocating a `Prepared` capsule, calculate a checked conservative aggregate **encoded** batch bound from the original input, declared count, per-provider maximum raw/protected output, sidecars, outbox intents, operation result, identifiers, signatures, field lengths and framing. A provider without a verified output bound cannot serve append readiness. The exact encoded capsule is then measured as it is streamed, still before reservation/actor save; any bound violation is `AppendPreparationLimit` with no partial capsule or regenerated values. One durable preparation capsule is at most **512 MiB** per operation, and all simultaneously live capsule plus request/response reservations share the existing **1 GiB** operation quota. Build and read the immutable capsule as authenticated encrypted bounded chunks, each with checked exact length and SHA-256 and a whole-capsule hash/root and ordinal/count; reserve bytes before each chunk, use at most **128 MiB live scratch**, and never materialize the full capsule in memory. Readback verifies every chunk, order, exact whole bytes/hash, preparation identity and owner fence before any MessageId reservation or actor save. A lost, altered or ambiguous chunk holds `AppendPreparationHold` and retry under the same operation ID without regenerating IDs, time, protected bytes or signatures. No partial capsule is durable append authority.

A `Prepared` capsule remains retained while its reservation/save is Pending, Ready or ambiguous, or any in-flight retry still needs its original volatile bytes. Only after Committed actor/root/result/full-bundle readback and durable closure of retry, rollback and publication obligations may a fenced CAS publish `HX-EV-APPEND-COMPLETION-1\0 || 01 || 000f`: `01` B32 preparation identity, `02` B32 original-input hash, `03` U exact OperationId, `04..07` U tenant/domain/aggregate type/aggregate ID, `08` B32 AppendOperationFingerprint, `09` B32 committed batch-root hash, `0a` B32 committed member-root hash, `0b` B32 actor intent-certificate hash, `0c` U original result key, `0d` B32 exact result hash, `0e` I event count and `0f` U authenticated retention-decision ID. The record and supporting actor/provider evidence are immutable and independently read back before capsule chunk reclamation. Reclaim encrypted chunks only with authenticated absence/readback; ambiguous deletion retains quota until reconciled. An exact late retry authenticates this compact record, original-input identity, committed root/member proofs, actor certificate, sidecars and result; it returns the pinned result without regenerating ID, time, signature or payload. Missing required evidence is `AppendPreparationHold`, never a fresh append. Pre-reserve capacity for both retained capsules and compact records under the operation quota; saturation returns `AppendPreparationHold` **before** a new save, with no unbounded or unsafe fallback.

One global strongly consistent `IEventMessageReservationStore` spans tenants, routes and instances. Key is `event-id-reservation:` plus lowercase SHA-256 of exact UTF-8 MessageId, with original MessageId stored to detect a hash collision; each per-ID index points to one authenticated batch root. Domain readiness proves the same backend identity, namespace and atomic ETag/CAS semantics across instances with persisted cross-instance probe. Prepare exact stored raw bytes/digest, reject duplicate MessageIds within the proposed actor batch, and reserve durable capacity for the complete index before save. A root first enters `Pending`; CAS-create every per-ID entry in deterministic order under that root's backend/fence and read back the exact ordered IDs, root fingerprint and each index pointer. **Actor save is forbidden until one CAS changes the root to `Ready` after that full readback.** A crash during partial Pending indexing resumes only by the same OperationId and exact durable Prepared capsule when actor-save absence is proven, or releases the whole root plus all entries under durable no-commit proof. Missing, ambiguous or conflicting capsule/index/save evidence holds the entire root; a different append cannot reuse any of its IDs. Only `Ready` may enter actor save/readback. After exact actor-owned bundle/result readback, one linearizable root CAS to `Committed` grants publication, subscriber and retry authority for every ID simultaneously. Per-ID status is always derived from the root, never committed independently. A failed reservation or proven no-save cleanup releases all entries under the same fence; timeout or cancellation alone is no-commit proof. Historical collision, capacity and retention rules below remain in force.

Batch reservation is one atomic decision after a recoverable indexing phase. Before per-ID index creation, CAS-create one durable root `HX-EV-APPEND-BATCH-1\0 || 02 || 000c` with ordered tags `01` U OperationId, `02..05` U tenant/domain/aggregate type/aggregate ID, `06` B32 AppendOperationFingerprint, `07` u32 ordered ID count followed by each U MessageId, `08` B32 proposed event/outbox/sidecar bundle hash (result-record tag `08`), `09` one-byte status (`00` Pending, `01` Ready, `02` Committed, `03` Released), `0a` O(B32) actual actor bundle readback hash, `0b` O(U) result-record key and `0c` O(B32) result-record hash. Root key is `append-batch:` plus the same scoped preparation-key digest; it retains and compares the exact five-part tuple from the preparation record and is CAS-fenced against a second root for that tuple. A distinct scope with the same OperationId has a distinct root key; every per-ID reference retains its own exact globally unique event MessageId. Each per-ID record contains exact MessageId, root key, root fingerprint, ordinal, scope and owner fence; readback must recover **exactly** the ordered root list, with no missing, extra or foreign entry, before Pending→Ready. A per-ID reference alone conveys no commit. Tags `0a..0c` are absent through Ready and populated only in the single Ready→Committed CAS after exact actor event/outbox/sidecar/result readback. `ActorBundleReadbackHash` is A5's codec-02 hash over the complete exact rows, committed ETag and logical version ([I-07]); tag `08` is A5's `CoreBundleHash`. At actor commit or ambiguous-save reconciliation, recompute that full hash once and require the same committed root for every batch member. Afterward publication, subscriber and duplicate checks verify the addressed member through the bounded member-root inclusion proof and authenticated committed root, without rereading the full bundle on each delivery. A crash before commit reconciles all IDs together; Pending partial indexing with any actor-save evidence is ambiguous and holds rather than completing Ready. Released is a tombstone under durable no-commit evidence, retaining the operation/ID conflict record for its obligation. Root and references share one strongly consistent backend/fence; no separate per-ID Committed transitions or partial-batch visibility exist.

At actor commit, stage an immutable outbox **routing intent** and the bounded pre-rendered operation-result side record in the same actor-owned operation as the event, purpose-06 encoding sidecar and stored-digest sidecar. The exact bounded intent record is `HX-EV-OUTBOX-INTENT-1\0 || 01 || 0012` with ascending tags: `01` U event key, `02` U tenant, `03` U domain, `04` U aggregate type, `05` U aggregate ID, `06` U MessageId, `07` B32 StoredDigest, `08` U operation ID, `09` U exact publisher source URI, `0a` U pubsub component, `0b` U topic, `0c` M canonical routing-header name/value map, `0d` U routing policy version, `0e` B32 destination-configuration digest, `0f` O(U) CloudEvent subject, `10` O(T) CloudEvent time preserving original offset, `11` B nested record `HX-EV-OUTBOX-CORE-1\0 || 01 || U content type || U stored event type name || U source-derivation ID || B exact source/type derivation inputs`, and `12` B exact immutable configuration bytes or `HX-EV-OUTBOX-CONFIG-REF-1\0 || 01 || B32 content hash || U immutable address`. Tag `12` is exactly one `B` whose length includes its first payload byte: `00 || exact immutable configuration bytes` or `01 || complete HX-EV-OUTBOX-CONFIG-REF-1 record bytes`. There is no discriminator outside the B length and no second nested B around the variant. Hashing, pinning and readback use those exact tag-12 B bytes; resolve either form to exact configuration bytes whose SHA-256 equals tag `0e`. Absent and present optional subject/time values are distinct. The entire intent is at most 1 MiB encoded and is charged before allocation; an overlimit or unresolved configuration reference holds append before reservation. All configuration bytes and derived core attributes are fixed before actor save; the content-addressed reference and its exact resolved bytes remain retained for every pin/retry obligation. Save and read back exact intent, event, both sidecars **and operation-result record** bytes under the same operation/ETag before marking the global reservation Committed or allowing first publication. The publisher derives the first delivery pin solely from this readback intent and authenticated original event, never from mutable current routing configuration. A retry compares source URI, destination, header values/policy and configuration digest to the pin; changes are conflict. An old outbox without authenticated intended-route evidence holds for separately approved offline evidence migration; guessed destinations and current defaults are forbidden.

`AppendOperationFingerprint = SHA256("HX-EV-APPEND-OP-1\0" || 01 || B32 AppendPreparationIdentity || U operation ID || U tenant || U domain || U aggregate type || U aggregate ID || u32 ordered batch count || for each event in original batch order: U MessageId || U event key || N sequence || B exact prepared raw storage bytes || B32 StoredDigest || U selected historic provider encoding ID || B exact immutable outbox routing-intent bytes; then B32 SHA-256(exact pre-rendered actor result bytes))`. All lengths/counts use §4 checked bounds. The intent bytes include commit-selected CloudEvent subject/time presence and values, content type, exact type/source derivation inputs, source URI, component/topic, headers/policy and immutable destination configuration bytes/digest and are deterministically prepared before reservation. The fingerprint is computed once from the exact values atomically committed in the `Prepared` capsule and stored in that capsule before reservation; a retry compares original input with its preparation identity and then uses the pinned fingerprint. Volatile sidecar signature/issuance bytes are **not** recomputed for a retry. The global Committed **batch root** stores the fingerprint and result-record key/hash; the exact original actor result bytes live in the immutable actor-owned operation-result side record. The event, outbox, purpose-06 encoding sidecar, stored-digest sidecar and result record are read back under one actor fence and compared before the reservation becomes Committed. A repeated append with an already `Committed` MessageId may return the original actor result only after comparing this exact **entire proposed batch and operation** fingerprint against the committed record and reading back all corresponding immutable events/outboxes/sidecars **and original result record** under the actor fence. Same ID with a different batch, order, route or any evidence is `MessageIdConflict`; missing, partial or uncertain readback holds reconciliation without staging or returning a new result. This rule applies even if one event's scope and StoredDigest happen to match.
The pre-rendered domain/append result is encoded once by the selected bounded V1/V2 writer **before** MessageId reservation and actor save; its exact byte size obeys the mode's §8 total result cap. Stage an immutable side record at `aggregate-operation-result:` plus lowercase SHA-256 of `U tenant || U domain || U aggregate ID || U operation ID`, with `HX-EV-APPEND-RESULT-1\0 || 01 || 0008` and ordered tags: `01` U operation ID, `02` B32 full AppendOperationFingerprint, `03` U actor state key, `04` N predeclared actor logical version, `05` B exact original bounded result bytes, `06` B32 SHA-256 of tag-`05` bytes, `07` I event batch count, `08` B32 A5 `CoreBundleHash` of the complete event/outbox/encoding/stored-digest/member-root bundle staged in the same actor batch. After deriving all event sequences and original result bytes, and before global reservation, the actor predeclares its checked logical version, stages result, event, both sidecars and routing intent together, saves once, and reads back their exact bytes, operation/version and ETag under the actor fence. The result record is never first invented at the later global `Committed` transition. If save commits but acknowledgement is lost, `Ready` reconciliation finds this record and the full bundle, compares result hash/fingerprint/operation and readback, then completes the reservation and returns **the original recorded result bytes**. Missing, partial, mismatched or uncertain evidence holds Ready for bounded reconciliation with no restaging or newly computed result; proven no-commit releases it under the existing rule. A repeated Committed append follows the same full-batch/readback comparison and returns that recorded result, never a new serialization.

A zero-event `DomainResult.IsNoOp` follows the same original command MessageId/OperationId and immutable preparation identity but uses a separate **actor-owned no-event completion CAS**, not a zero-member event batch root. Pre-render the exact existing public no-op result shape and payload with the selected bounded writer before the CAS. The durable `HX-EV-NOOP-RESULT-1\0 || 01 || 0009` side record has ascending tags: `01` U OperationId, `02` B32 AppendPreparationIdentity, `03` B32 canonical original input hash, `04` U selected writer mode, `05` O(B32) selected registry fingerprint (absent for authenticated old V1), `06` B exact pre-rendered result bytes, `07` B32 SHA-256 of tag `06`, `08` U actor command-idempotency checkpoint key and `09` U checked actor logical version. The actor commits this record atomically with a no-op completion witness at that checkpoint under the same operation fence, then reads back exact identity, input hash, mode/fingerprint, result bytes/hash and version before returning. No per-event MessageId index/root, event stream append, outbox intent or publication is created. An exact retry resolves this side record and returns its pinned bytes without re-running domain work or serialization; changed original input under the same command MessageId is `AppendPreparationConflict`. An ambiguous no-op save is `AppendPreparationHold` until actor readback proves committed or never-started; caller cancellation follows the same actor commit witness as an event append and never invents a new result. The no-op record and checkpoint survive for the command idempotency/retry obligation.

A no-op `Prepared` capsule obeys the same retention and quota rule as an event batch, but its compact completion is **not** a zero-member batch-root claim. After authenticated readback of the committed no-op result/checkpoint witness, same-save actor intent certificate, post-save provider commit receipt and closure of retry/rollback obligations, CAS-publish `HX-EV-NOOP-COMPLETION-1\0 || 01 || 000f` with ordered §4 tags: `01` B32 preparation identity, `02` B32 original-input hash, `03` U OperationId, `04..07` U tenant/domain/aggregate type/aggregate ID, `08` U selected writer mode, `09` O(B32) selected RegistryFingerprint, `0a` U no-op result storage key, `0b` B32 exact no-op result-record hash, `0c` B32 authenticated no-op checkpoint-witness hash, `0d` B32 actor intent-certificate hash, `0e` B32 purpose-11 provider commit-receipt hash and `0f` U authenticated retention-decision ID. The complete compact no-op record is capped at 4 KiB before allocation. It has no event count, StoredDigest, member root, batch root or fabricated event ID. Read back the compact record and all named witnesses before deleting encrypted capsule chunks; ambiguous deletion retains quota. An exact late retry compares original input and this compact record, authenticates the still-retained no-op result/checkpoint/intent/receipt evidence, and returns the pinned original no-op result without generating IDs, clocks, signatures or payload again. Missing required evidence yields `AppendPreparationHold` and never reexecutes the no-op CAS.

Before each append, the store reserves durable capacity for the preparation capsule, batch root, all per-ID references and reconciliation headroom under its configured scalable quota; inability to guarantee that capacity returns `ReservationCapacityHold` before save. A capacity failure never falls back to tenant-local uniqueness. Pending entries have bounded reconciliation, but Committed entries are not evicted merely because the store is full.

Per-route marker key includes scoped MessageId, canonical type, physical subscription ID and stable HandlerRouteId, while immutable duplicate identity compares scope, sequence, StoredDigest and DeliveryDigest; RegistryFingerprint is audit/readiness metadata, not duplicate identity. Same MessageId may reach several cataloged routes only for identical event evidence. A changed body, destination, header or reused ID is conflict, never duplicate. Migrate legacy Completed/Dispatched marker under CAS only with independent scoped actor evidence **and** route-specific receipt/outbox/catalog proof; Completed remains terminal, Dispatched only finalizes. Old InProgress may retry only under proven effect idempotency. Unique-ID inventory alone is insufficient. Ambiguity holds for reconciliation.

There is exactly **one durable global publication pin keyed by the exact MessageId**, CAS-created only after comparing scope, StoredDigest, DeliveryDigest and all pinned decoded body/attestation/core/header bytes and the exact outbound bytes for the same transport mode. A changed digest cannot create a second pin even if a secondary index includes that digest. The separate durable historic delivery-pin obligation is keyed by scoped MessageId and DeliveryDigest and stores purpose 02, scope, StoredDigest, exact body and extension bytes, signature/key ID, signed issuance UTC from claim tag `0a` and approved fingerprint, source head, pending queue/quarantine/rollback needs and drain status. Recovery may derive the first pin from durable original event/readability only when actor commit/outbox witness proves no prior send; otherwise it holds for operator reconciliation. The exact global MessageId publication pin and its body/attestation bytes remain durable until every queue, broker retry, quarantine replay, rollback target and old-key verification obligation for that event has closed with durable evidence; beyond that they stay available for every possible late duplicate, and a CAS tombstone may replace them only under C1's rule: after authenticated closure proves no future same-MessageId comparison can arise, or when the tombstone names one authenticated immutable full-byte comparison source retained for the whole enforceable redelivery horizon. A hash-only tombstone never deduplicates. A late delivery is compared byte for byte with the pin or that source and the original actor source before route-receipt deduplication; changed bytes conflict, and missing bytes, trust or evidence hold without a new send, effect or false acknowledgement. The global Committed ID index and immutable event digest remain for lifetime uniqueness. D6 atomically reserves the complete admitted batch and original per-tenant/deployment charges before append; the separate pin install authenticates exact reservation-bound attachment/readback before send or A8 revision zero. Waiting existing committed work remains `PublicationPinCapacityHold` under D6 without partial grants or an uncharged pin. A retired key may verify only its exact still-open pin obligation after proving signature validity in the key's original interval and exact byte/scope equality. On a queued approved pin after registry rotation, first validate the historic purpose-02 signature, prior RegistryFingerprint, signed issuance time/key interval and **exact durable pin obligation**; do not compare that prior fingerprint to the active route fingerprint. Independently authenticate the immutable actor source under current trust, compute a fresh purpose-01 route and verified effective view under the **current** key/fingerprint, compare StoredDigest, MessageId, scope and sequence across old pin, actor source and new route, and compare the received exact delivery body/attestation/transport bytes to the old pin before handler selection. The current view retains the authenticated source digest and original delivery digest as provenance; a newly computed effective payload need not equal the old pinned readable payload. Missing old obligation, unavailable source or missing current route holds without effect or acknowledgement. Historic purpose-02 acceptance never authorizes old effective bytes to bypass current evolution. Revocation or compromise follows an explicit incident decision; age alone never grants generic old-key acceptance or drops an open pin. Before activating a new signer, every affected verifier advertises the new trust map/fingerprint and old obligations remain readable.

The existing public `EventStoreDomainEventContext` remains an **unsealed** positional record with its exact six-argument constructor `(TenantId, AggregateId, MessageId, SequenceNumber, Timestamp, CorrelationId)`, generated six-field deconstruction, nullable `long? GlobalPosition`, and optional init properties `Domain`, `CausationId`, `UserId`. No member is redeclared, sealed, made required, or changed in type or accessibility; old source and compiled callers retain their API. Add a separate immutable `VerifiedEventStoreDomainEventContext` wrapper for the two new effect callables. Its public `LegacyContext: EventStoreDomainEventContext` is a detached copy with those original fields, and its verified-only members are addressed `AggregateType`, non-null verified global position, `DeliveryDigest`, `HandlerRouteId`, stored metadata/type/version/format/digest, effective type/version/format/payload digest, current `RegistryFingerprint`, and exact purpose-01/02 claim/key/signature values. Binary members are immutable copies; public mutable transport arrays never back signed authority. The router constructs the wrapper only after source, consumed-metadata, current-view and both signed claims validate, compares every wrapper and legacy member to those claims and actor readback, and binds scope, MessageId and DeliveryDigest to `EventEffectKey`. Production admission requires a verified global position when the signed claim requires one; this does not narrow the old nullable member. A mismatch is `HandlerCapabilityMismatch` before effect or marker. Both new callable interfaces receive the verified wrapper; an old-handler adapter receives its `LegacyContext` and preserves its six-argument metadata semantics.

The additive effect contract uses C3's immutable eight-field `EventEffectKey(tenant, domain, aggregateType, aggregateId, MessageId, DeliveryDigest, physicalSubscriptionId, HandlerRouteId)` and a provider-backed durable `EventEffectReceipt`, which is C3's precommit effect record plus its commit and readback receipts. Add independent `ITransactionalEventStoreDomainEventHandler<TEvent>.HandleAndCommitAsync(TEvent eventPayload, VerifiedEventStoreDomainEventContext context, EventEffectKey key, IEventEffectTransaction transaction, CancellationToken cancellationToken): ValueTask<EventEffectReceipt>` and `IEventEffectReceiptReader.GetReceiptAsync(EventEffectKey key, CancellationToken cancellationToken): ValueTask<EventEffectReceipt?>`. The router builds `VerifiedEventStoreDomainEventContext` only after source, route and delivery proof validation and compares every context field to the signed consumed metadata and authenticated actor source. It first queries the receipt, then obtains a provider transaction bound to the exact key under a unique constraint/linearizable CAS, invokes the new handler **only within that context**, and accepts success only after effect and receipt commit in one serializable transaction and authenticated readback. `IEventEffectTransaction` exposes a provider-enlisted `IEventEffectWriteSession EffectWrites` and `CommitEffectAndReceiptAsync(EventEffectReceipt proposedReceipt, CancellationToken cancellationToken): ValueTask<EventEffectReceipt>`; that call atomically commits every enlisted effect mutation and the unique-key receipt, and authenticated readback must match the returned receipt. A second commit or a write after commit fails. Any handler path that can perform an effect outside this session cannot claim `AtomicStore`. A crash before commit yields neither effect nor receipt; a crash after commit yields both; an ambiguous commit is resolved by receipt/effect readback before another invocation. `ProviderIdempotency` uses `IProviderIdempotentEventStoreDomainEventHandler<TEvent>.HandleIdempotentlyAsync(TEvent eventPayload, VerifiedEventStoreDomainEventContext context, EventEffectKey key, IEventIdempotentEffectProvider provider, CancellationToken cancellationToken): ValueTask<EventEffectReceipt>` and the same read-only receipt lookup. The provider enforces the exact key on its effect call and returns/queries the same result and receipt across crash/retry; an adapter cannot emulate this by writing a receipt after an arbitrary side effect. The router selects the cataloged transactional or provider-idempotent implementation ahead of the unchanged `IEventStoreDomainEventHandler<TEvent>` `Task` API, with duplicate route registration rejected. Consumer lease mode `DurableDedup` denotes the proved `AtomicStore` transaction-and-receipt contract; `ProviderIdempotency` denotes the external exact-key contract. Existing handlers stay source-compatible and production-ready only through a verified adapter satisfying one of those callable contracts. Production route activation requires the §7 version-3 crash/two-route probe and authenticated durable receipt for every route; a configured provider name or a later marker write is insufficient. `HandlerCapabilityHold` occurs before handler invocation, acknowledgement or completed marker when a route lacks a proven contract. Production activation freezes and audits the transitive DI/service graph and implementation dependencies of each effect-capable route. `AtomicStore` may reach effect sinks only through its `IEventEffectWriteSession`; `ProviderIdempotency` may reach them only through the exact-key provider. A service locator, dynamically resolved or injected alternate effect sink, or effect write outside those channels fails registration/readiness. Per-route crash and concurrency probes plus code/configuration review verify this restriction; a fixture alone cannot prove arbitrary handler code pure. A crash after effect but before `Dispatched` queries the receipt and finalizes the same key without rerunning effect. Valid addressed event with no current-type handler is `HandlerCapabilityMismatch` and retries; `PredeclaredRouteFilter` may acknowledge only authenticated out-of-scope delivery under its frozen predicate. AD-31 quarantine is evidence capture, never permission to advance a checkpoint past bad history.

`EventEffectReceipt` is a bounded canonical provider record set, not a free DTO: C3's precommit effect record `HX-EV-EFFECT-RECORD-2`, its atomic `HX-EV-EFFECT-COMMIT-1` receipt and its `HX-EV-EFFECT-READBACK-1` receipt, each at most 16 KiB, with `ReceiptDigest` over the exact precommit record and `EffectReceiptHash` over all three plus the readback authentication carrier. The pre-integration 4 KiB `HX-EV-EFFECT-RECEIPT-1` record, which carried the commit version and ETag inside the digested record, is superseded. A reader limited to 4 KiB records may read historical records but is fenced from every route that can produce a C3 record (C6), and no record is truncated to fit the old cap. V3 probe transcript tags `13`/`14`, broker and provider readback and route deduplication compare the complete records and `ReceiptDigest`; a changed mode, key, backend, commit version or ETag is a conflict, not an already completed effect. Existing V17/V20/V22/V23 signed fixture literals remain historical and unchanged.

The 6.6 binary cutover includes `Operations/Capture/DeadLetterEnvelopeParser` and `Operations/Endpoints/DeadLetterOperationsEndpointExtensions`. The parser recognizes the exact §7 authenticated Binary CloudEvent body **and headers** and structured `data_base64` mapping, in addition to legacy structured JSON `data`. Before assigning replay-safe scope or MessageId it verifies the attestation, pinned body/core/header identity and transport-to-canonical decoding; it retains exact transport bytes, headers and hashes. Malformed or unauthenticated bytes may receive a support-safe unidentified hash for evidence capture but can never be replayed as an identified event. The capture endpoint streams a bounded admitted body up to C4's 128 MiB raw-body cap, with its exact bounded headers, into tenant-scoped authenticated encrypted durable blob storage, recording exact bytes/hash/headers in an actor CAS index with readback; a broker/publisher durable reference is equivalent only when it proves the identical pinned bytes and finite retention obligation. HTTP 200/ack occurs **only after** exact durable capture and readback. The former 1 MiB default cannot acknowledge an uncaptured valid binary delivery. Capacity, provider or readback failure is retryable non-2xx and holds binary readiness unless a broker dead-letter path independently proves retention beyond its finite retry budget; finite retries alone are insufficient. Above-cap bytes are classified with safe hash evidence and never claimed captured, while publication/subscription bounds prevent treating them as valid deliveries. AD-31 durable capture still precedes poison acknowledgement; no-handler valid addressed events retain their §9 retry/hold rule.

Binary ingress resolves the **complete addressed logical HandlerRouteId set** from the authenticated pinned physical-subscription membership revision and the verified current event route set, even though the broker delivers one body. Before any physical acknowledgement, CAS-stage/read back one immutable `HX-EV-BINARY-HANDOFF-1\0` delivery/route-set manifest keyed by the exact global MessageId, physical subscription ID, membership revision and DeliveryDigest; it binds the sorted unique route IDs, canonical pin/body/attestation hashes, source scope and one stable delivery OperationId. Each addressed route has its own durable effect key and Completed/Filtered receipt under that operation. The handoff's committed pointer is the sole authority that all required route entries exist; partial/ambiguous staging is reconciled by OperationId and leaves the physical message unacknowledged. Invoke only routes lacking an authenticated terminal receipt, at most once per exact effect key. A predeclared authenticated filter may terminalize only its proven out-of-scope route. Acknowledge the physical delivery only when **every** addressed route has a durable C3 terminal decision (`Completed`, permitted `Filtered`, or capture-backed `Quarantined` for proven permanent poison) and the complete manifest, decisions and receipts read back. Any missing handler, retryable, failed, ambiguous, changed route set or changed bytes leaves the physical message unacknowledged, resumes only incomplete routes and never converts another route's receipt into global completion. An empty addressed set is not success for a valid addressed event unless the signed predeclared physical route filter proves it out of scope. This binary rule is independent of, and consistent with, the batch-wide legacy JSON handoff above.

The immutable actor-save result in §7 is the **domain/append result**, not the later public command or publication outcome. Pre-render and stage that exact bounded domain result (including rejection) with the original event/outbox/sidecar bundle; the zero-event no-op uses its separate actor-owned no-event result record (A7). Actor commit and an exact append retry return only the pinned domain result bytes at the append layer. Public outcome revisions, the immutable first POST response pin and terminal `PublishFailed` are defined only by A8 and C5 below; `PublishFailed` or pending publication after save never overwrites the committed append result or alters its fingerprint. A lost public-response acknowledgement is resolved by readback; cancellation before actor save requires proven no commit, while cancellation after save preserves append truth and leaves publication and outcome reconciliation on a bounded recovery token. A zero-event no-op has no publication receipt and pins its public shape from its actor completion witness without an outbox send.

At actor commit/reconciliation, authenticate and hash the **entire** prepared event/outbox/encoding/stored-digest/result bundle once under the actor fence. Add a versioned committed per-member Merkle commitment as an actor-owned sidecar within the exact bundle whose hash is batch-root tag `08` and whose readback hash is A5's codec-02 `ActorBundleReadbackHash`. The separately defined AppendOperationFingerprint remains the original complete-batch input comparison and does not change its historical codec. For ordered batch index `i` of count `n`, define `MemberLeaf_i = SHA256("HX-EV-BATCH-MEMBER-1\0" || 01 || I i || I n || U MessageId || U exact event key || B32 raw event hash || B32 StoredDigest || B32 outbox-intent hash || B32 encoding-sidecar hash || B32 stored-digest-sidecar hash || B32 domain/append-result hash)`. Build a left-to-right binary tree with `Parent = SHA256("HX-EV-BATCH-NODE-1\0" || 01 || B32 left || B32 right)`; duplicate the last hash at an odd level, record `n`, leaf order and final B32 root in the authenticated member-root sidecar bound through batch-root tag `08` and `ActorBundleReadbackHash`. The actor's one full-bundle readback verifies every leaf before the global root becomes Committed. A per-member proof contains version `01`, checked `i`, `n`, exact leaf fields, and one ordered sibling B32 per level with left/right derived from index; its depth is exactly `ceil(log2 n)` (zero for one member), at most 10 for the admitted 1,000-event V1 batch, and its entire encoded carrier is at most 16 KiB before allocation. Publication, subscriber and duplicate checks authenticate the committed batch root/certificate and verify only the addressed immutable member's raw event, outbox, sidecars and result binding with that proof; they do not reread every other member on each delivery. A missing member, changed sidecar/result, proof count/index mismatch or uncommitted root holds. An exact append retry still compares the full original batch fingerprint and actor readback, never merely one member. This additive production commitment leaves historical V17/V20/V22/V23 signed fixture literals untouched.

Before parsing, allocation or signature verification, cap the complete signed MembershipClaim carrier (claim, member set, key ID and signature) at **1 MiB encoded**, with at most **4,096** sorted unique logical members and at most **4 KiB encoded per member**. The external route-capability route set is at most **256 KiB** and **1,024** unique type/version/format rows; the complete external manifest plus claim/signature/carrier is at most **2 MiB**, while its dependency closure retains the existing **1 MiB** cap. Length and count prefixes are checked against these caps before copying any nested B value; sorting scratch and duplicate detection are charged. Overflow is typed `ConsumerMembershipFenceUnavailable` or `ExternalCapabilityLimit` and prevents publish/ack, not a truncated set or an inferred handler. A smaller signed closure cannot authorize an overlarge external route set.

The binary handoff manifest's exact bytes are `HX-EV-BINARY-HANDOFF-1\0 || 01 || 0011`, then ascending tags: `01` U MessageId, `02` U tenant, `03` U domain, `04` U aggregate type, `05` U aggregate ID, `06` U component, `07` U topic, `08` U physical subscription ID, `09` N membership revision, `0a` B32 StoredDigest, `0b` B32 DeliveryDigest, `0c` B32 pinned body hash, `0d` B32 pinned attestation hash, `0e` B32 route-set hash, `0f` B route set, `10` U stable delivery OperationId, `11` B32 pinned core/header/transport-rule hash. The route set is `u32 count || U HandlerRouteId` repeated in unsigned UTF-8 sorted unique order; count is at most 4,096 and the complete manifest is at most 1 MiB before allocation. Tag `0e` equals SHA-256 of exactly tag `0f`'s decoded route-set bytes. The durable handoff key is `binary-handoff:` plus lowercase SHA-256 of `"HX-EV-BINARY-HANDOFF-KEY-1\0" || 01 || U component || U topic || U physical subscription ID || U MessageId`; revision, route set and digests are compared as **values** at that one key so a changed delivery cannot create a parallel completed handoff. A route receipt key adds `U HandlerRouteId` under that handoff and retains the complete eight-field `EventEffectKey` (C3); readback verifies every route in tag `0f` before acknowledging one physical message. This manifest is a new production record and does not alter any historical signed fixture.

The public command-outcome record is A8's codec-03 `HX-EV-COMMAND-OUTCOME-1\0 || 03 || 000c` at A8's revision keys. Its tags `0b` and `0c` are authenticated under the same operation fence and compared with tag `09` and actor readback, and a mismatch is no outcome. Revision zero is created after actor commit or no-op readback; one revision never changes its bytes, publication receipt-set hash or state; a `failed` state never changes the actor domain/append result; and the record is bounded by the selected §8 response cap before allocation. The pre-integration codec-01 record and its key are superseded.

The committed per-member proof carrier is `HX-EV-BATCH-MEMBER-PROOF-1\0 || 01 || I index || I memberCount || B(exact ordered MemberLeaf fields from §7) || I depth || depth × B32 sibling`, with no trailing bytes. `index` is zero-based, `memberCount` is 1..1,000, `depth` is the checked `ceil(log2 memberCount)`, siblings are ordered leaf-to-root, and left/right position is derived from each index bit; an odd duplicated right child must equal the current left hash. Compare the reconstructed root to the committed member-root sidecar B32 authenticated by batch-root tag `08` and the actor readback certificate and compare every supplied member field to exact actor-owned readback before effect/publication. A proof over 16 KiB or with a count/depth/index mismatch fails before allocation or hashing. This is a proof of one committed member, never a replacement for full-batch comparison on append retry.

The member-root sidecar is `HX-EV-BATCH-MEMBER-ROOT-1\0 || 01 || 0006` with ordered tags `01` U scoped append OperationId, `02` U actor state key, `03` I member count, `04` B32 final Merkle root, `05` B32 SHA-256 of exact pre-rendered domain/append result bytes, and `06` B32 original AppendOperationFingerprint. Stage it in the same actor save as events, outbox intents, encoding/stored-digest sidecars and operation-result record. The complete ordered bundle hash in `HX-EV-APPEND-BATCH-1` tag `08` and result-record tag `08` includes this exact sidecar after the event members, before final actor readback. Its bytes are precomputed from prepared values and never include the bundle hash or actor ETag, so no hash is circular. Actor commit/reconciliation checks tag `03` against root tag `07`, recomputes every leaf/root once from the full bundle, compares tag `04`, verifies tags `05`/`06` against result/fingerprint and binds the sidecar in `ActorBundleReadbackHash`; only then may the root become Committed. Thereafter a publisher or consumer needs the authenticated committed root, sidecar and addressed member proof, not a repeated full-batch scan. The original batch-root codec, V17 historical fixture and full-batch append-retry comparison remain unchanged.

### C1. Exact publication and transport contract

Import §4's checked big-endian `U`, `B`, `B32`, `N`, `I`, `T`, `Q`, `O(X)` and `M` codecs, strict UTF-8/JSON, no duplicate names in canonical maps or JSON objects, and preallocation bounds. HTTP header multiplicity follows the explicit retained-image rule below; §4 map uniqueness does not discard an admitted non-routing header duplicate. `T` is signed i64 **UTC instant ticks followed by signed i16 original offset minutes** in `[-840,840]`, consistent with DateTimeOffset; `Q` is a UTC instant only. Import §7's exact 37-field `HX-EV-DELIVERY-BODY-1\0 || 01 || 0025 || tags 01..25`: tag `09` stored Timestamp is `T`, tag `21` optional CloudEvent time is `O(T)`. The body has no digest, key ID, signature or attestation field. `DeliveryDigest = SHA256("HX-EV-DELIVERY-1\0" || 01 || B(exact body bytes))`. Its fields are: `01` StoredDigest B32, `02` MessageId U, `03..06` tenant/domain/aggregate ID/type U, `07..08` sequence/global position N, `09` T, `0a` correlation U, `0b..0d` causation/user/DomainServiceVersion O(U), `0e` stored EventTypeName U, `0f` stored MetadataVersion I, `10` stored canonical type O(U), `11` stored payload version O(I), `12` stored format U, `13` readable format U, `14` **original readable** payload B, `15` readable extensions O(M), `16` protection state U, `17` protection metadata version I, `18..1a` scheme/key alias/content hint O(U), `1b` flags O(M), `1c..1f` CloudEvent specversion/id/type/source U, `20` subject O(U), `21` time O(T), `22` content type U, `23..24` component/topic U, `25` six routing headers M. Subscriber compares every consumed metadata field, including original offset, to authenticated source and signed claim. Publisher never upcasts; subscriber creates a current purpose-01 view only after source admission. `ReadableExtensions` and protection flags retain absent/null/empty `O(M)` distinctions; first pin copies the stored extension map and replaces only the exact `eventstore.protection` key with canonical provider-returned unprotect metadata. A case-variant-only historical protection key holds for approved mapping and is never silently normalized. Extension limits are 64 entries, 256 UTF-8 bytes/key, 4,096 bytes/value, 256 KiB canonical map and 512 KiB complete encoded event metadata. Preflight retained history; valid old data beyond a new capability cap holds readiness, while authenticated permanent schema/metadata violation is poison only after AD-31 capture.

At actor commit, A5 **codec-02** intent/receipt and member root bind exact immutable event, encoding/digest sidecars, outbox and **domain/append result payload hash**, including rejection events. The §7 outbox intent `HX-EV-OUTBOX-INTENT-1\0 || 01 || 0012` stages exact source URI, component/topic, routing map/policy, destination configuration digest/bytes or immutable reference, optional subject/time `O(T)` and stored-form core derivation in the same save. Its tag `12` is one `B` containing `00 || inline configuration` or `01 || complete immutable configuration-reference record`, with no nested second `B`; readback resolves and hashes the exact configuration. Mutable publisher options never fill absent intent. An old outbox without authenticated intended-route evidence holds for separately approved migration. Derive the first pin only from authenticated original source/readability and that read-back intent, after A5 complete generation readback and globally Committed batch root. Same-ID append retry compares the **entire** original batch/result/fingerprint; a member proof grants only one already committed member's publication/effect check.

**Canonical destination ID.** It closes the destination-ID ledger item (§11.5). A8's `U destinationId` is exactly `"hxdst1-" || lowercase-hex(SHA256("HX-EV-DESTINATION-ID-1\0" || 01 || U component || U topic || B32 DestinationConfigurationHash))`: 71 ASCII bytes, encoded as `00000047` plus those bytes wherever a `U destinationId` or `U destination ID` appears. `component` and `topic` are the authenticated read-back outbox intent tags `0a` and `0b`, byte-for-byte, each 1..1,024 bytes of strict UTF-8 with no case folding, trimming or Unicode normalization. `DestinationConfigurationHash` is intent tag `0e`, used only after tag `12` resolves to exact configuration bytes whose SHA-256 equals tag `0e`; for the reference variant `01`, the resolved bytes must also match the reference record's own content hash. The storage variant is not identity, so equal resolved bytes give one ID. A missing or unresolved configuration, a length or UTF-8 violation, or any hash mismatch holds before pin, send or evidence write. The ID is derived, never chosen: display names, current or retry configuration, provider aliases and broker-assigned names cannot supply it. Every destination-ID field in this specification carries exactly this value: A8 `ExpectedEntries`, the C2 parent-member row and head, the C3 accepted-delivery log and reverse index **and both of their keys**, and the C5 retry-plan, policy, pre-send, rule, partition-manifest, no-attempt and nonadmissibility records and terminal-row `destinationIdHash` inputs. A verifier recomputes it from the pinned outbox intent; any other bytes are a conflict that holds the record or status that carries them. Before the intent is committed, the admission owner derives the ID for the C5 retry plan and policy from the exact component, topic, tag-`12` and tag-`0e` values it will write into that intent; post-commit readback recomputation must reproduce it, or it conflicts. Known answers (C01c): configuration bytes `{"component":"pubsub","mode":"Binary","topic":"orders","version":1}` (SHA-256 `127208325ff55766b0a9b98a0c8bda6bf499bb5f4e8f15add0e1eb454272c2d2`) with component `pubsub` and topic `orders` give `hxdst1-4b06bdae283a395dcd542ab0c6328ea9403a7914589bc077fb9ca79ec6f0bd63` in both the inline and reference forms. The same configuration under the delimiter-shifted pairs `pubsub.orders`/`events` and `pubsub`/`orders.events` gives `hxdst1-5b1a8f0661e8f66202017982d87a9d73b42b4373c73da7db7951859f866dd1b6` and `hxdst1-f2e0c543f5186d36a46ba2855930203bb3ce9d0eb163094023806f9a454aa169`. Changing only `"version":1` to `"version":2` gives `hxdst1-991eef72e86e51e04f4a233ea44ac7297516469b085d0ec150c7fabf41caa16b`.

The exact global MessageId CAS pin contains decoded body, purpose-02 `HX-EV-ATTEST-1\0 || 01 || 0003` claim/key ID/64-byte P1363 signature, DeliveryDigest, StoredDigest, scope, old approved RegistryFingerprint, signed claim tag-`0a` issuance UTC, routing intent hash, renderer version, the exact accepted membership claim hash/revision, precomputed exact request and predicted accepted outbound bytes, C2 complete ordered request and predicted accepted transport-header images, and their equal six-header signed projection for each authorized mode pair, and exact hashes of the retained body, attestation, mode renderings and complete header images. Key is the **exact MessageId**, never `(MessageId,digest)`; changed body, header, destination, scope or same-mode rendering conflicts. Before any send, the publisher deterministically renders and CAS-pins **both** exact request and predicted accepted body/header images from the immutable destination configuration, accepted membership revision, proposed accepted mode, renderer version and signed routing intent. The broker must attest that its complete accepted image will equal this prediction; no post-acceptance result may choose new bytes for the global pin. An unpredicted broker-added, reordered or normalized header holds before acceptance, while an authorized Binary-to-Structured conversion may change only its predicted mode rendering and its mode-specific complete header image: `Content-Type` and every Binary `ce-*` header (the required `ce-specversion`, `ce-id`, `ce-source` and `ce-type`, the optional `ce-subject` and `ce-time` when present, and `ce-hyevattestation`), all of which the Structured image must omit. The two complete images are independently pinned and compared; decoded body, attestation and all six signed routing headers remain equal. A provider unable to inspect and compare the complete predicted image in its atomic accept path cannot advertise publication readiness. First-pin recovery requires durable no-prior-send proof; ambiguous prior send holds. Pin capacity is charged before send under the publication-retention ceilings below (`PublicationPinCapacityHold`). Its signed historic obligation remains through queue, broker retry, quarantine, rollback and late-delivery obligations. A hash-only tombstone cannot perform C2's required full-byte duplicate comparison. Full pin body, attestation, original/accepted renderings, complete ordered header images, signing evidence and source remain available byte-for-byte throughout every possible late duplicate, retry, route, rollback and incident obligation. Only after authenticated closure proves no future same-MessageId comparison can arise may a CAS tombstone replace these bytes; alternatively a tombstone may name one independently authenticated immutable full-byte comparison source, with exact authority/key/generation/ETag, source bytes and no-expiry obligation read back for the whole enforceable redelivery horizon. On every duplicate, the reader resolves that source and compares all bytes before returning Accepted; missing or expired source holds. No finite broker horizon by itself makes hashes sufficient. Missing historic key/pin/source holds, never permits a new send or false duplicate.

**Publication-retention capacity.** `PublicationPinCapacityHold` reuses B6's per-operation/deployment storage pattern and adds a tenant sublimit. Level one is unchanged: the A3/A8 1 GiB per-operation quota, which already reserves each eventful command's worst-case pins and referenced evidence before A4 Prepared. Level two is the **per-tenant publication-retention ceiling** and level three the **deployment publication-retention ceiling**. Both are exact u64 byte counts pinned in the authenticated deployment capability, for B6's stable `(deployment identity, canonical backend descriptor)` scope applied to the publication-retention backend, with `1 GiB ≤ tenant ceiling ≤ deployment ceiling`. The tenant ceiling is an intersection inside the deployment ceiling, never an extra allowance. Restarts, rolling upgrades, capability changes and namespace renames cannot reset either counter. Three kinds of retained object are charged:
- each global MessageId pin, with every separately stored full-byte rendering, complete header image, attestation, signing evidence and authenticated tombstone comparison source;
- each C4 legacy original or variant side record, with its manifest, attempt, side-link, variant-entry and head records;
