## 9. Consumer and cancellation matrix

| Boundary / condition | Required result and durable progress |
| --- | --- |
| No-op command exact retry or ambiguous save | Resolve by the original command MessageId/OperationId and actor-owned no-event result/checkpoint readback. Exact retry returns the pinned original result bytes; changed input conflicts; ambiguous save holds without domain re-execution or event/outbox creation. |
| Append preparation identity conflict or missing capsule | `AppendPreparationConflict` rejects changed original input under one operation ID. Missing/ambiguous capsule is `AppendPreparationHold` before actor save; exact retry uses its original volatile values and bytes, never generates replacements. |
| No-op capsule retirement or late retry | After no-op result/checkpoint, intent and provider receipt readback and obligation closure, CAS-publish the dedicated compact no-op completion, then reclaim encrypted capsule chunks with authenticated deletion. Ambiguous deletion retains quota. Late retry proves the compact record and returns pinned result without new no-op execution; missing proof is `AppendPreparationHold`. |
| Append capsule or named index limit | `AppendPreparationLimit` rejects an overbound encoded batch before volatile generation or actor save; lost capsule chunks hold without regeneration. `NamedIndexLimit` rejects an overbound row/progress candidate or more than 4,096 changed keys before root publication and preserves last-good state; impossible safe pruning holds readiness. |
| Append malformed pair, unknown alias, bad identity, failed per-output F validation, sequence overflow or limit | Typed rejection before actor staging/reservation; no event mutation. A V1 alias `NoPayloadIdentity` skips only payload-ID extraction, never addressed envelope checks. |
| Raw read corrupt/duplicate names, unknown format, failed protection, missing sequence | Stop at offending sequence with source bytes/protection reason retained. No Apply, checkpoint, `Current` or success response. If parsing prevents StoredDigest, authenticate exact raw actor/provider evidence with addressed key, immutable head/sequence and raw-byte SHA-256; a complete permanent corrupt source is durably AD-31 captured with hash/scope/sequence/reason before ack. Incomplete or untrusted evidence holds/retries without ack; never fabricate StoredDigest. |
| Retained raw-corrupt cutover disposition | An immutable operator-approved `RawCorruptDisposition` may close inventory only for its exact actor/provider-proved key, sequence and raw-byte hash after durable AD-31 evidence. Replay still stops there with typed corruption and last-good prefix; no synthetic digest/origin/route, Apply, checkpoint advance or delivery ack follows from the disposition. Missing decision/evidence holds reader cutover. |
| Raw-source API or provider proof unavailable | `RawSourceUnavailable` holds reader activation or the addressed read before typed materialization; no typed `EventEnvelope` fallback may claim immutable provider bytes, original encoding or a trusted head. |
| Upcast unknown/gapped/ambiguous edge, mismatched result, invalid hop schema/identity, output limit | Startup/corpus mismatch blocks readiness; authenticated deterministic event failure stops prefix. No next hop or partial authoritative state. Unexpected hop failure retries. Input digest mutation or attempted source-owner exposure is `UpcasterContractViolation`, holds the route before next hop/Apply and blocks readiness until code/dependency repair; it is never acknowledged as deterministic source poison. |
| Paged public seam or proof mismatch | External async replay receives public immutable `PagedContext`, opaque authenticated byte[] token and in-process `IPagedReplayStateSession`, then returns public immutable `PagedProgress` naming its CAS-written successor. Gateway validates owner/generation/range/proof and state readback before committing once. Old adapters reject the context and never publish partial state. |
| Incomplete paged result | `InProgress` exposes null final state, final fields and timeline, `ErrorCategory=None`, only the verified page-end sequence and pinned `PagedProgress`; `/replay-state/pages` returns one next token with `isComplete=false`. Old `/replay-state` rejects it. Only complete-prefix proof permits final `Succeeded`. |
| Authorized backup export source mismatch or limit | Stop the bounded export before constructing a downloadable result; report a typed source/identity/protection reason or `ExportLimit` when count/64 MiB encoded bytes exceed the cap under the existing authorization policy. Valid V1 output labels the stored alias and source version, while V2 public identity is canonical with separate stored provenance. No partial content escapes as an ordinary Admin/trace response. |
| Backup export staging or final pointer uncertain | No response bytes, URL or partial success leave the private encrypted stage. Read back the fixed-head staged content/hash and atomically committed completion pointer; changed or missing proof holds for reconciliation, cancellation discards or quarantines uncommitted stage. |
| Oversized proof page | Projection dispatch and ordinary stream, Admin, trace, backup and other authenticated readers premeasure and reduce/re-sign a contiguous page against the fixed source head until both the 64 MiB proof and 128 MiB combined scratch caps fit. One event still over limit returns `ProofLimit` and holds without checkpoint advance, skipped event, partial export or unchanged-page retry. Command pages use the stricter 2 MiB outer cap. |
| Replay/command cancelled or proof/head mismatch | Discard private scratch/timeline/array; preserve last authoritative state. A page is never a complete prefix. Async replay propagates token; bounded sync adapter's limitation is explicit. |
| Live/rebuild projection deterministic bad event | Capture AD-31 where available; stop at event, preserve last contiguous completed checkpoint and mark state non-current. Repair/migration then retries from last good point. Missing sink cannot turn it into success. |
| Subscription bad authenticated permanent source | Durable AD-31 capture or C4 broker full-byte reference, and a C3 `Quarantined` decision for every addressed route, before ack. Addressed no-handler, new capability/proof limit, unavailable key/provider or untrusted ingress hold/retry without ack. Filter ack only for authenticated out-of-scope predicate. |
| Duplicate delivery | Verify global committed ID, canonical decoded body/attestation/core/header pin and same-mode exact outbound bytes first; an allowed mode conversion must strictly decode and canonically re-render to the same pin. Marker/receipt matching returns already-completed without side effect. After pin reclamation, compare the full bytes of the tombstone's authenticated comparison source (C1), the original actor source and the route receipt before the same decision; a hash-only tombstone or missing evidence holds. Conflicting evidence fails closed. |
| Command-state proof absent/mismatch or partial page | `CommandStateUnproven` before admission/processor; perform bounded authenticated source lookup or completed paged replay. Stored `CurrentState.Events` cannot Apply a nonzero-hop source; no command effect or authoritative partial state. |
| Projection checkpoint=head>0 | Verify exact zero-route checkpoint-anchored prefix and fenced durable state/readback; metadata-only completion performs no event read, Apply, handler, state write or checkpoint advance. Wrong snapshot/checkpoint form fails closed. |
| Snapshot source unavailable, unreadable or byte/ETag/batch mismatch | Reject/discard the post-snapshot page before Apply, preserve approved v1 snapshot bytes, request a fresh authenticated page-1 proof from the gateway and start a new operation without snapshot authority; no partial tail Apply. |
| Cross-store checkpoint race or missing shared fence | `CheckpointFenceUnavailable`; immutable prior handler state and its checkpoint pointer remain authoritative. A new immutable state version alone cannot overwrite last good state or sign a mixed pair; ambiguous pointer CAS retains both versions until readback reconciliation. |
| Historical MessageId collision, preparation/batch-root or pin capacity | `HistoricalMessageIdCollision` holds rollout with both original events retained; `AppendPreparationHold` or `ReservationCapacityHold` rejects before actor save; `PublicationPinCapacityHold` retains committed outbox without pin, send or A8 revision zero, and the POST and status answer `CommandOutcomeHold`. No local uniqueness fallback or pin overwrite. |
| Binary membership revision/lease race | `ConsumerMembershipFenceUnavailable` holds publication; acceptance-time broker UTC/revision/fingerprint and all matching lease/probe expiries are checked atomically, including a lease that expired after publisher precheck. Ambiguous acceptance requires durable exact-operation/pin receipt lookup, with unknown outcome holding and no new nonce/send. One global topic pin/send serves all subscribers. |
| Named-projection batch visibility | Shared keys select one route/key-space committed generation root with checked per-source progress; aggregate-only pointers cannot publish them. The complete sparse Merkle row set, source progress, logical concurrency and TTL are verified under the fence, including a final authoritative-UTC expiry check after value readback. Partial shadow rows, failed/ambiguous root CAS or a reader seeing the prior root select only last-good unexpired values; at or after authenticated expiry, `ReadModelExpiryPending`/`ProjectionStateUnproven` holds until a scoped tombstone is certified. Bounded query overflow returns `ReadModelQueryLimit` without partial values. |
| Named read capability or key-space migration | Forged, expired, copied-principal or revoked authority returns `ReadModelAccessDenied` before key/root lookup. Overlapping unmigrated legacy physical keys return `KeySpaceMigrationHold` before guard activation; neither path exposes a partial row set or hidden-key existence. |
| Batch delete readback | Require absent-state readback and durable delete receipt/version under the same fence; absence alone or a present deleted row never advances checkpoint. |
| Legacy ingress or unknown binary consumer | Queued flat JSON resolves the authenticated publication revision and **complete addressed logical route set**, then durably commits/reads back the batch handoff manifest, every route record, one exact shared binary pin and send intent, and acknowledges the physical old copy after D7 exact retained custody, keeping every logical obligation open, or after broker acceptance and every route's terminal decision (C4); partial/ambiguous work remains unacknowledged and reconciles by operation ID. Redelivery compares MessageId/source/full route set/pin; a difference is `LegacyHandoffConflict` with no second effect. Binary publishing remains fenced until every component/topic subscriber proves carrier and duplicate-safe capability. |
| Binary or `data_base64` dead-letter capture | Extract replay-safe identity only after attestation and pinned transport/body/header verification. Capture the admitted body durably with exact hash and actor index readback before HTTP 200; failure returns retryable non-2xx, and malformed identity is safe unidentified evidence, never an identified replay. Valid bytes above the old 1 MiB default are not acknowledged without retention. |
| Verified effect context or dependency route | Both new effect calls receive the additive verified wrapper around the unchanged public `EventStoreDomainEventContext`, with a signed non-null global position where required; mismatched wrapper/legacy members or an effect-capable DI dependency outside the selected write session/exact-key provider holds before invocation or ack. |
| Hopped handler view or production receipt missing | A projection/subscription hop requires verified `VerifiedEffectiveEventView`, a discoverable registered current-type handler and its §5 capability row; `HandlerCapabilityMismatch` blocks handler/effect/checkpoint or ack. A production route without registered `AtomicStore` or `ProviderIdempotency` and queryable receipt returns `HandlerCapabilityHold` before effect or marker. |
| Rollback after V2 persisted | Fence V1-only command/replay/projection/subscription endpoints before routing retained V2 history; `RollbackReaderCapabilityHold` retains work with no Apply/effect when no capable endpoint exists. |
| Snapshot absent/stale/unwitnessed | Preserve bytes; full replay before command. With 6.2 folded runtime, actor stages approved folded snapshot and side witness at `AggregateIdentity.SnapshotKey + ":evolution-witness"` together, saves once, reads both back, then may claim tail cost. Without 6.2 runtime, full replay only. |
| Ambiguous replay blob, ledger or final-result commit | Retain quota, operation ID and token; read back all three under one fence. Return exact pin only when all hashes/proof/transition match, release only after proven no transition, otherwise `ReplayCommitAmbiguous` holds without second Apply. |
| Encoded final response over 128 MiB | `FinalResponseLimit` before authoritative completion; no partial final state. An optional oversized timeline permits a fresh authenticated page-1 state-only replay with `includeTimeline=false`. |
| Exact final retry after token expiry | Within its retained 24-hour pin obligation, return exact bytes without scratch when current key/fingerprint and complete proof verify; expiry forbids fresh Apply or continuation. Invalid final proof restarts authenticated replay. |
| Prior approved delivery pin after registry rotation | Verify old purpose-02 claim only under exact historic obligation, authenticate immutable source and issue current purpose-01 view, compare source identity and pinned bytes; old fingerprint need not equal active fingerprint. Missing evidence holds without ack or effect. |
| Zero-tail completion at `long.MaxValue` | Count-zero start=end=head=target=`long.MaxValue` requires witnessed snapshot for aggregate replay or signed checkpoint/state for projection only; no event page, next token or increment. |

| Cancellation boundary | Required outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Before preparation CAS | Cancel with zero mutation. After a durable preparation capsule but before actor save, cancel with zero **event/actor** mutation; reconcile or release the capsule only with durable no-commit proof. |
| Pending or Ready batch root before save begins | Prove durable no actor commit, then release root and all per-ID references together; Pending partial indexing may resume only from the exact Prepared capsule under the same fence. Ambiguous proof retains the whole batch for bounded reconciliation. |
| No-op actor save begun or result ambiguous | Keep the immutable preparation and no-event result operation ID, then reconcile the actor-owned no-op checkpoint/result CAS by exact input hash, writer mode/fingerprint and result bytes. A proven commit returns pinned result even after cancellation; uncertain evidence holds without re-execution. |
| Save begun or result ambiguous | Preserve the Ready batch root and preparation capsule, read all actor events/metadata/outboxes/encoding and stored-digest sidecars **and pre-rendered operation-result side record** under bounded recovery token and actor fence; decide committed versus uncommitted from their exact durable witness, never caller-token rollback or fabricated failure. |
| After actor commit, before first send | Committed event, purpose-06 sidecar and immutable outbox routing intent remain; a staged exact pin remains if present. Cancellation leaves send pending. A missing first pin is derived once from durable event and readback routing intent only if prior send is disproven; ambiguous prior send holds. |
| Send begun, broker result ambiguous | Retain the same canonical pin and original same-mode outbound bytes; query C2's `GetPublicationReceipt` for the exact attempt key and its complete observation chain before any new nonce/send. Accepted returns the prior receipt, rejected may retry only with a fresh valid fence under the same idempotent operation, and unknown/unavailable holds. No changed bytes under the same MessageId. |
| Subscriber effect committed, ack not durable | Cancellation leaves delivery retryable; retry reads effect receipt. After durable ack, cancellation cannot retract it. |
| Projection checkpoint/notification cleanup | Checkpoint only after durable handler state/effect and fenced readback. Cancel before that keeps old checkpoint. Notifications use durable outbox stable key and exact-byte retry. |

### A9. Failure, cancellation and ordered migration

| Boundary / observation | Deterministic action and durable consequence |
| --- | --- |
| Invalid metadata, identity, alias, version, echo or F output | `MalformedMetadata`, `EventIdentityMismatch`, `UnknownEventContract`, `CapabilityMismatch` or `DownserializeRejected` before reservation/save. Preserve no partial result. Unknown/stale capability holds readiness; it is not proof of poison. |
| Count/encoded size/parser/scratch/sequence overflow | A3 limit or `SequenceExhausted` before the prohibited allocation/staging. Release only uncommitted private buffers/reservations proven safe to release. |
| Caller cancellation before durable preparation/save | Stop work, clear owned scratch/spool and propagate cancellation once no mutation/in-flight commit is proven. If a prepare/save might have begun, reconcile its exact operation instead of asserting no commit. |
| Actor save returns, throws, loses acknowledgement, or caller cancels after start | A5 full authenticated readback. Commit match preserves committed truth; proven no commit permits only fenced same-capsule continuation if its source/version is unchanged, or terminal A5 AbortedStale cleanup if changed; all other states `ActorCommitEvidenceHold` with no duplicate append or ID release. |
| Commit proven but batch-root transition ambiguous | Reconcile one entire root under original fingerprint; no independently committed member, publication or fresh append. Preserve same operation/capsule. |
| Commit proven; publication pending/failed/unknown | Retain append result/outbox. With a proved complete observation, A8 creates revision zero and pins the publication-independent committed POST reply, including when the first observation is failed; later failed observations create private revisions and advance the head normally. Status inspection of private failed follows [I-10] and holds `CommandOutcomeHold` without verified C5 terminal, hold or [I-10] retry-wait evidence; it never claims terminal PublishFailed/stop-polling. Exact retries retain the original pin. An unknown broker send reconciles its receipt before another send; it cannot claim published or undo append. |
| First response or no-op retirement ambiguous | Exact A7/A8 evidence or hold; retain quota until complete readback/absence. No regeneration or reexecution. |
| Permanent corrupt/schema-invalid authenticated historical source | Stop replay/checkpoint; AD-31 capture before subscriber poison acknowledgement. New capability limits, unknown keys, protection unavailability, unexpected exceptions or OOM are hold/retry, never poison acknowledgement. |

Caller cancellation is neither poison nor an instruction to discard committed evidence. Post-start recovery uses a separate bounded token (one 30-second attempt, then durable recovery ownership and hold if unresolved); it never continues unbounded in a disconnected request or uses the cancelled caller token to abandon readback. A lost or cancelled public connection may deliver no response, but cannot change the committed result or first-pin bytes. Cancellation between pin commit and send returns the same first pin on retry. Public diagnostic status is `unknown`/hold when authority is unavailable, not a guessed success/failure.

Reader-first rollout follows §10 with these explicit dependencies:

1. Inventory all retained aliases/versions, measured limits, exact historical encoding/decoder evidence, corrupt items, protection readability and original keys/obligations. Fence every V1 appender at gateway **and actor**, drain uncertain old writes, and complete valid retained branch-02 evidence or A6 corrupt dispositions before evolved-reader activation. Dormant reader deployment alone grants no read capability.
2. Slice 1 includes the minimal **bounded evidence-writing V1 producer**, including A3 ingress/writer and A5 same-save/member-root/receipt probes. New V1 is branch-01, not offline migration. No old endpoint may allocate an unbounded response before a gateway's later check. Retain existing readers until this gate is complete.
3. Dry-run V1/V2 writers and verify exact bytes on the configured production provider plus a second independent provider/conforming harness. The B read and replay sections and the C publication and rollout sections use A5 codec-02 complete sets, A6 source identity, A7 checkpoint and A8 immutable first pin. Global reservations, consumer capability, binary carrier, effect receipts and historic-ID collision/backfill gates remain §10 prerequisites before V2 enablement.
4. After any V2 append, fence V1-only command/replay/projection/rebuild/subscription endpoints in both deployment and rollback before routing work. Returning the **writer** to V1 needs a valid F and cannot downgrade retained V2 read requirements; unavailable capable peers yield `RollbackReaderCapabilityHold`. Rotate verifiers first and retain original keys/evidence through every obligation. Reader/transform changes and writer/trust changes follow A2's distinct compatibility rules.

Nothing here starts these runtime slices; §12 governs approval.

### B9. Failure, cancellation and inspection outcomes

Use §9 plus the explicit B4–B6 bindings. Error results carry safe reason, addressed sequence, bound/count and operation/correlation identifiers only under existing access policy. Do not expose raw/effective/protected payload, identity secrets, CLR assembly identity, provider internals or stacks in ordinary Admin/trace/logs. Authorized backup content remains its distinct existing permission, never inferred from diagnostics permission.

| Trigger | Typed outcome and durable authority |
| --- | --- |
| Authenticated immutable malformed/schema/identity failure | Stop at exact event; `RawEnvelopeCorrupt`, `MalformedMetadata`, `EventSchemaRejected` or identity failure. No following hop, Apply, checkpoint or success. Retain source evidence; AD-31 capture-before-ack remains C3's separate requirement. |
| Missing/untrusted source, capability, proof/key/provider; unexpected upcaster exception | `RawSourceUnavailable`, `ActorCommitEvidenceHold`, `HandlerCapabilityMismatch` or deployment/provider hold; no poison skip or synthetic success. Source mutation/owner escape is `UpcasterContractViolation`, a route-code hold. |
| Preallocation failure | `RawEnvelopeLimit`, `ReadableLimit`, `ProofLimit`, `ScratchLimit`, `LegacyArrayLimit`, `TimelineLimit`, `CheckpointStateLimit`, `FinalResponseLimit`, `ContinuationCapacityHold`, `NamedIndexLimit` or `ReadModelQueryLimit` at the corresponding bound. No unearned transition; newly insufficient capability is a readiness hold. |
| Apply mutates then throws | `ApplyFailed` at that sequence; retain pre-Apply last-good bytes, old committed pointer/checkpoint and no timeline entry for the failed event. Legacy partial diagnostics remain non-authoritative. |
| Cancellation before computation/prepare | Propagate original token, stop bounded read/upcast/Apply loop, discard private uncommitted work and release proven-unneeded quota after safe cleanup. Existing actor events and last-good state remain. |
| Cancellation, timeout or lost acknowledgement after successor/commit begins | `ReplayCommitAmbiguous` and same-operation readback under recovery token; no second Apply or claim of rolled-back state. A proven commit returns pinned committed truth even after caller cancellation; unknown outcome retains quota. |
| Invalid replay scalar/selector/manifest | `ReplayScalarInvalid`, `ReplayTranscriptCapabilityHold`, `TimelineEvidenceHold` or `TimelineProtectionHold` before dependent allocation/Apply or authority release. Retain uncertain prepared objects and quota; unsupported rollback holds. |
| Invalid projection prior descriptor, root/session race | `ProjectionPriorStateHold`, `ProjectionPriorConflict` or `ProjectionPriorSessionClosed` with no mixed-state handler input or checkpoint publication; B7a defines pre-handler retry versus post-handler reconciliation. |
| Diagnostic output/base failure | B2a returns existing safe Problem or sandbox error shape; no fabricated source proof, committed state or partial success. Cancellation propagates. |
| Query code/root-vector failure or retained-cache saturation | `QueryCapabilityChanged`/`ReadModelQueryConsistencyHold` without result for invalid execution authority; capacity of the bypassed cache alone executes uncached and is not a failure. |
| Snapshot rejection or replay restart | Fresh authenticated page 1; no tail Apply under rejected proof, no deletion of old protected snapshot, no reuse of partial timeline across operations. |
| Admin timeline route (blame, bisect, step, diff) whose target exceeds 1,000 events or 64 MiB cumulative state, or with no qualified timeline protection provider | `TimelineLimit` / `TimelineProtectionHold`, with no partial timeline. **Disclosed behavior change:** today these routes replay every event with `includeTimeline: true` whatever the count (`AdminStreamQueryController.cs:484–515`; bisect :155, diff :364, step :818), and `maxEvents` only trims the displayed window. State-only routes (`state`, sandbox) are unaffected. §10.2 classifies it as breaking change BC-04. |
| Query/root race or failed checkpoint proof | `ProjectionStateUnproven`, `CheckpointFenceUnavailable`, `ReadModelExpiryPending` or access-denied outcome; return no mixed generation, expired bytes or partial bulk values. |
| Backup page tamper, cancellation, final fixed-head/proof failure or total output above 64 MiB | `ExportLimit` or typed source/protection failure. Stage authenticated encrypted output privately, validate every bounded page and final fixed-head completion, then commit/read back one completion pointer before any HTTP content chunk/download URL. No partial export escapes. Preserve stored provenance; existing protected/provider-opaque export rejection remains. |

Export staging follows **B6's two storage levels**: the admitted export operation's 1 GiB per-operation quota and the same deployment replay-storage ceiling as replay, in its stable deployment/backend scope. Before the first chunk allocation, atomically reserve the conservative complete encoded output, ciphertext/protection overhead, staging/chunk metadata, completion pointer, recovery evidence and any overlapping copies; the 64 MiB encoded export cap is not an extra storage allowance. Concurrent exports, replay and abandoned/ambiguous export generations share those counters and smaller tenant/store limits; insufficient capacity returns `ContinuationCapacityHold` before allocation, never partial output. Use the existing admitted export operation and exact object-plan reservation/readback under B6’s fence, without another endpoint or codec. Lost completion-pointer acknowledgement reconciles the original exact chunks/hash/pointer before any download; cancellation cannot report an uncertain pointer absent or regenerate an export under the same operation. Pre-completion cancellation leaves private objects invisible and charged until no-future-write evidence and authenticated deletion/key-revocation readback permit cleanup. Completed exports retain exact chunks, metadata, pointer and necessary keys through every active download, retry and backup obligation; recheck existing download authorization and retain charges while readers remain. After all obligations close, fence new readers, reconcile the pointer and in-flight writes, then delete/revoke with authenticated readback before refunding once. Ambiguous deletion or abandoned work retains its reservation for recovery; namespace/revision/operation replacement cannot reset accounting. No partial output becomes visible and completed truth survives caller cancellation.

## 10. Migration and four ordered Story 6.6 slices

Before any reader cutover, inventory each provider's retained V1 aliases, raw/metadata/readable maxima, source versions, current-version reachability, unknown members, queued deliveries, old markers, in-flight writers, protection modes, old keys and snapshot/checkpoint evidence. Fence every V1-capable append path at gateway **and actor admission** before the evolved reader serves the domain: it either uses an upgraded producer that atomically stages and reads back the signed purpose-06 encoding sidecar with each new event, under the measured V1 bounds, or cannot append. Drain/reconcile in-flight old writes under that fence, finish sidecar and original StoredDigest/protection-decoder evidence backfill/readback for every valid retained event, durably classify any independently proven raw-corrupt item under §4 without fabricating a digest, and prove no unfenced binary can append before activating the new reader. V1 emission can continue only through upgraded sidecar-writing producers. A dormant reader may deploy earlier but cannot serve the domain. For each **valid** retained V1 event, separately approved offline work CAS-installs and verifies the purpose-06 encoding sidecar and authenticated original-digest/decoder manifest against immutable raw readback **before slice-1 reader activation/cutover**; missing sidecars block readiness. A new reader binary may be deployed dormant while old readers continue serving, but it cannot serve V1 events or advertise active read capability until this inventory, CAS installation and verification finish. Preflight retained migration source/review/decoder/key availability for the full readable lifetime and open backup/rollback/delivery obligations, protected-snapshot typed readability and raw/folded caps, named-projection shared key-space ownership, route-global row/progress index bounds and every legacy read/write guard. Preflight case-variant protection extension keys and data-dependent F output validation, and prove every subscribed component/topic consumer can decode the binary carrier before publisher cutover. Admit old both-absent V1 exchanges only under exact alias/readiness gate. Reader-first fleet advertises one approved **per-domain** capability; active V1 producers are fenced to measured legacy ceiling and bounded 128 MiB result **before** serving new gateways. An old endpoint that could allocate beyond that bound must be upgraded to bounded writer or have a provider-enforced preallocation bound. Legacy raw storage remains untouched. Unknown reused schema requires separately approved offline evidence migration, not an unimplemented discriminator. Queued V1 delivery lacking attestation obtains authenticated gateway source lookup, durably commits and reads back the §7 batch-wide handoff manifest, every addressed route record, shared send intent and exact attested binary pin, reaches handlers only through that pin, and acknowledges old JSON only after broker acceptance and every route's terminal decision (C4); missing lookup or handoff retries without old-message acknowledgement. Old outbox sends/pins drain or reconcile before stable pinning; old keys remain for every durable pin/queue/quarantine/rollback and encoding-sidecar obligation.

Cutover audits the §4 origin branch for **every valid** V1 event key. Valid historical rows need the independently signed manifest, reviewed docket, source evidence and version-2 digest sidecar; upgraded new V1 appends need their exact actor-save certificate and same-save event/sidecar/result readback. A raw-corrupt item uses only its separate cutover disposition and remains a replay stop. Do not demand an offline manifest for a new writer or accept a retained event under a fabricated new-writer branch. Advertise and compare `MigrationAuthorityDigest` beside the active per-domain RegistryFingerprint on every reader/publisher migration capability; a missing/mismatched signer or reviewer trust map, identity policy or retained old key holds mixed-reader activation. Binary publication readiness includes the §7 all-route physical acknowledgement contract, capped membership/external carrier, provider probe and bounded dead-letter capture. Named-projection readiness includes the callable fenced writer, query-token quota, changed-leaf TTL jobs, bounded ordinal archive and per-member committed-bundle proofs. Each provider probe must inspect durable bytes, route receipts, certified roots, old visible state and actor result/outcome records after injected crash and ambiguous CAS boundaries. Any provider unable to supply those exact capabilities holds the affected domain/route; no fixture is evidence that a production provider supports them.

1. **Reader foundation:** registry/manifest/codecs, bounded raw/protection read, shared evolution pipeline, proofs, corpus probes and additive DTOs. Slice 1 **owns an evidence-capable bounded V1 producer** before either an upgraded V1 writer or evolved reader serves: it premeasures legacy raw/readable/result preallocation ceilings, stages the exact raw event, purpose-06 encoding and version-2 StoredDigest sidecars, branch-01 origin, acyclic pre-save intent certificate, outbox and immutable domain result in one actor save, reads back those staged bytes, then obtains and verifies the separate **post-save** purpose-11 provider receipt under the committed generation. No V1 append is enabled until same-save, bounded-readback, receipt/key and provider capability probes pass. Retained valid V1 receives branch-02 independently reviewed offline manifest/docket/digest evidence before reader cutover; a retained raw-corrupt item may close inventory only through the §4 RawCorruptDisposition and remains unreadable. Fence or upgrade every live V1 appender; V1 admission remains active only for measured bounded evidence-writing producers after this gate. An unready reader binary stays dormant while old readers serve. Slice 1 also carries the additive contracts of §10.3 and activates no §10.2 change. Its producer writes A5 evidence under legacy admission; evidence-required admission activates only at slice 4 ([I-41]).
2. **Writer and transport dry run:** bounded mode-selected V1/V2 writer, raw publisher/ingress, exact pin/protection output, preparation capsules, atomic batch-root reservation, verification of Slice 1 stored-digest/origin/certificate evidence, explicit state-backend identity and provider probes. No V2 writes yet. D9 slice 2 first installs the qualified metadata ledger/shared transactions, registry/onboarding/epoch and all owner/bootstrap charges before any hold producer; then legacy claims and pinned H begin (BC-15). Destination/policy capabilities are stored; V2 remains dormant.
3. **Consumer integration:** command pages/replay, projections/rebuild/checkpoints, subscription effects/markers with verified context and audited effect-dependency graph, named-projection versioned read-model visibility, Admin/trace and all bypass reads through shared route with durable validation. Consumer code may deploy, but production subscriber activation that requires global committed reservations remains fenced until slice 4's complete historical ID backfill and marker reconciliation. Its production activation for a domain also requires the slice-3 rows of §10.2 (BC-02, BC-04, BC-05, BC-13 and BC-14), D5 long-stream inventory/activation and existing reader/capture capability prerequisites. Preparation and qualification of D7 capture in slice 3 grant no captured physical handoff/redrive activation; BC-07/BC-08 replaced D7 behavior waits for slice 4 ([I-41]). Slice 3 activates D5 replay inventory, D3 tenant resume safety route/BC-02 denial, capsule-before-cleanup and exclusive legacy recovery. Wait H and authenticate fenced cutover before slice 4. D8 registry prerequisites already exist from slice 2.
4. **Migration and final gate:** backfill IDs/markers/obligations and **reverify previously installed encoding sidecars** (never first install evidence required by an active slice-1 reader), block on every distinct-event historical MessageId collision until separately approved offline resolution, drain or reconcile old publications and queued legacy JSON, verify cross-instance backend and durable reservation/pin capacity, all serving domain peers' approved registry/trust/handler capability, production state-backend identity and transitive dependency closure, command-state proof and snapshot lookup paths, shared checkpoint fence, **every subscribed consumer's binary-carrier and duplicate-safety lease under a fenced authoritative membership revision**, one global pinned send per shared topic, registered production effect receipts, rollback reader-capability fences, corpus reachability and provider portability vectors; **only then** enable V2 writes. Before V2 writes or binary cutover it also requires the slice-4 rows of §10.2 (BC-01 and BC-01a–BC-01k, BC-03, BC-06–BC-12 and BC-16), including D4 authoritative status and D7 captured physical handoff/redrive and the SemVer-major release carrying all of §10.2, with its API and wire baselines and package-only consumer checks passing ([I-41]). Slice 4 is also where a domain enables evidence-required admission ([I-12], [I-14]).

Mixed-version rollback keeps V1 aliases/readers and old verifier keys while V2 persisted history, queues, pins or rollback targets need them; never emit V1 from a V2 current payload without proven F. Once **any** V2 event is persisted for a domain, every serving command, replay, projection, rebuild and subscription endpoint in both forward deployment and rollback MUST advertise and prove the minimum V2 read/evolution capability covering **all retained source versions** before receiving work. The gateway fences V1-only endpoints from those routes at the membership/load-balancer boundary; if no capable endpoint remains, commands and deliveries hold with `RollbackReaderCapabilityHold` before Apply/effect rather than being routed to a V1-only binary. Returning the writer mode to V1 does not downgrade immutable V2 history. Rollback drills include an old endpoint joining after first V2 append and a previously serving endpoint losing its capability; both are fenced before work can reach them. Advancing current payload version re-runs retained-source ≤16-hop proof. Adding a trust key fences affected-domain V2 writing, installs dual trust/verifier readiness first, attests one matching new RegistryFingerprint, then resumes signing/writes; old obligations remain verifiable under exact prior fingerprint and key interval. Changed `EventTransformHash` or route `HandlerCompatibilityHash` invalidates state witness and forces full replay/rebuild; trust-only change can re-attest a verified checkpoint without state mutation. Provider portability evidence includes exact-byte save/readback, raw ingress/send, bounded protection input/output, CAS/global reservation, effect idempotency and checkpoint fence under at least the configured production provider and a second independent provider or conforming harness.

Before enabling any versioned named-projection key-space prefix guard, inventory **all** physical keys under its exact `(tenant, domain, state store ID, byte prefix)` including old unversioned read-model rows, old shared-projection generation rows and marker keys. Classify each key with authenticated prior batch/marker evidence, not prefix spelling alone. For an overlap, either perform an explicit fenced copy/mapping to new immutable generation keys with exact bytes, owner, logical version, ETag and readback proof, or choose a nonoverlapping declared prefix with a bounded authenticated old-reader adapter. Retain the old keys and ownership evidence through checkpoint, backup, rollback and retry obligations. Fence old writers before the new guard can intercept their keys; until inventory, migration and readback complete, the new route is unready and legacy coordinator reads/writes remain under their old authorized path. An old unversioned key is never reinterpreted as a shadow row, and a guard may not block an active old coordinator without its proven replacement. Prefix collision, missing evidence or incomplete copy returns `KeySpaceMigrationHold`, preserving the last certified root and readable legacy path.

Reader-first activation also needs A3 bounded V1 writer/result ingress, streaming raw provider readback **before typed materialization**, complete valid retained V1 signed manifest/sidecars/branch-02 or independently approved corrupt disposition, historical global MessageId collision inventory and same-backend cross-instance reservation/CAS proof. A5 new V1 branch-01 and V2 complete actor receipt capability precede their reads; a dormant binary advertises no active read capability. Keep old source/wire/DTO constructors and `EventStoreDomainEventContext` binary compatibility through additive optional members; old callers are V1 only under exact alias/capability gate. Public status compatibility: C5's `PublicationRetryExhaustedHold` projects nonterminal `EventsStored` with `Retryable=false`, a `RecoveryReasonCode` and the committed result's metadata, which shipped surfaces contradict. The `CommandStatusRecord` `Retryable` XML doc and the command-status retryability table in `docs/operations/drain-failure-reason-codes.md` define `false` as terminal. The `CommandStatusRecord` class summary gives non-terminal states null terminal-specific fields; its `EventCount` and `TimeoutDuration` parameter docs restrict those fields to `Completed` and `TimedOut`; and the status response-field table in `docs/reference/command-api.md` restricts `eventCount` to `Completed` and `rejectionEventType` to `Rejected` and has no `retryable` or `recoveryReasonCode` row. The `CommandStatusController` status endpoint's OpenAPI remarks, the `CommandStatus.PublishFailed` XML doc, the status sections of `docs/reference/command-api.md`, `docs/concepts/command-lifecycle.md` and the generated `docs/reference/api` pages for `CommandStatus` and `CommandStatusRecord` make a publication failure terminal `PublishFailed`. That guide's `recoveryReasonCode` field also names only values from its reason-code table, which has no `publication_retry_exhausted_hold` row. Story 6.6's compatibility gate verifies every §10.2 amendment (BC-01a–BC-01k) and that table before activation. It must also search the repository for any other shipped XML doc, OpenAPI remark or docs page that defines command terminality, `PublishFailed` or per-status field nullability; this list is the gate's floor, not its limit. Package and consumer manifests pin actual implementation/options/transitive managed/native dependency bytes and backend identity; changed package/handler graph cannot advertise unchanged capability. AOT/trimming is not claimed. A missing provider primitive holds affected domain/route; fixture-only hashes and historical V23 probe do not confer readiness. Epic 8 remains optional.

After reader/consumer, effect provider, capture and broker gates pass, enable binary V2 per domain/component/topic under current signed membership. Migrate queued JSON by C4 and reconcile old markers/outboxes/broker unacked counts before removing old ingress. Once V2 history exists, every serving command, replay, projection, rebuild and subscription endpoint in forward **and rollback** deployment must prove V2 read/evolution capability for all retained versions; returning writer mode to V1 does not erase V2 history. Fence a V1-only endpoint before Apply/effect; no capable endpoint is `RollbackReaderCapabilityHold`. A trust-only rotation refreshes transient proof and preserves compatible state after verification; read/Apply or selected handler semantic change requires authenticated replay/rebuild or approved migration. An unknown external member, lost key, changed route set, expired claim or unsupported rollback holds send/effect without acknowledgement. Every active logical consumer needs its own exact lease/probe, even behind one physical route.

Cancellation before preparation CAS leaves zero mutation. After durable preparation but before actor save, release requires proven no commit; after save begins A5 readback decides truth under one bounded recovery attempt then durable ownership/hold. Before first send, cancellation leaves committed outbox/pin pending; after send begins, broker receipt reconciliation precedes retry. After effect commits but before physical ack, redelivery reads receipt and completes only missing routes; cancellation after ack cannot retract it. Projection checkpoints/notification outboxes advance only after their independent fenced readback, with exact-byte notification retry. No cancellation branch labels a valid addressed event poison or removes a committed pin.

### 10.1 Slice gates for the breaking changes

[I-41] **Ordered activation and release.** D9 fixes the four slices: slice 1 activates no incompatible behavior; slice 2 provider-qualified metadata/registry/epoch/charge prerequisites precede legacy claims and BC-15; slice 3 activates replay inventory, BC-02 safety route/capsules and the slice-3 consumer changes; slice 4 waits H/cutover before evidence-required scopes/status, whole-batch pins/queue/windows, membership restoration and captured physical handoff/redrive. BC-09/BC-10/BC-16 activate slice 4. Readers understand exact schemas before writers; incompatible old readers are fenced. D-RELEASE permits compatible maintenance/security publication through the existing current-main manual workflow when API, wire, package-only consumer and focused inactive-path evidence prove compatibility. Dormant compatible preparation alone is not a shipped breaking change. Genuine breaking commits remain honestly classified under repository commit policy and require SemVer-major. Retain the publication hold whenever compatibility is unproven or incomplete breaking changes reached main; expose the complete approved incompatible set only in the major release. No maintenance lane, version override or CI mutation is created by this specification. Every runtime activation still requires §12 and the separate AD-26 profile/provider gates.

[I-43] Every public, wire and storage change in this document that §10.2 does not list is additive under NFR12 and requires compatible baseline evidence (API and wire baselines plus representative package-only consumers) before release:

Existing constructors, deconstruction, members and defaults are unchanged. - **New interfaces and registrations.** `IEventUpcaster`, `IV1Downserializer`, `IBoundedPayloadWriter`, `IBoundedScratchAllocator`, `IReadOnlyPayload`, `IAuthenticatedRawEventSource`, `IEventEvolutionReader`, `IAuthenticatedSnapshotSource`, `IAsyncAggregateReplay`, `IAsyncDomainProcessor`, `IVerifiedDomainProjectionHandler`, `IVerifiedProjectionPriorReadSession`, `INamedProjectionVersionedReadModelStore`, `IVersionedNamedProjectionBatchWriter`, the transactional and provider-idempotent handler interfaces, `IEventEffectReceiptReader` and the `Add…Handler` registration extensions.

The new `RecoveryReasonCode` values belong to BC-01b and BC-03, not to this list.

Terminal boundary known-answer **field-core** vector (framing, not a standalone signed proof): prefix tags `05..09` for `start=end=head=target=long.MaxValue` and `count=0` are exactly `057fffffffffffffff067fffffffffffffff077fffffffffffffff087fffffffffffffff0900000000` under §4 N/I. It is accepted only with zero route count `00000000`, matching cumulative accumulator and the signed witnessed snapshot (`0d` absent, `0e`/`0f` present) or projection checkpoint (`0d` present with matching container entry and state pointer, `0e`/`0f` absent). The aggregate `/replay-state/pages` endpoint rejects the checkpoint variant. For **this count-zero sentinel**, `count=1` or any route entry fails before Apply; a normal count-one page with a verified route at sequence `long.MaxValue`, prior accumulator through `long.MaxValue-1`, and head/target at max is valid and completes once. Any next token or attempted `long.MaxValue+1` fails before arithmetic. The literal count-zero core above is unchanged. The ordinary k=`long.MaxValue-1` zero-tail still encodes start=`long.MaxValue`, end=`long.MaxValue-1`, count 0. The literal core was generated with Python signed big-endian `to_bytes(8)` and independently recomputed by the embedded Node verifier below.

Rejected: a named progress leaf hashing its own newly signed checkpoint, retrospectively sorting shared-key updates by per-stream sequence/aggregate ID, treating present-key `IdempotentAbsent` delete as conflict, omitting `ValueTypeName` from a logical retry witness, changing key-space ownership without migration, advancing source sequence for TTL expiry, leaving `SharedProjectionEpochCoordinator` on unguarded generic physical-key writes, materializing an unbounded backup export, deriving optional CloudEvent subject/time from mutable current defaults, returning an upcaster-owned output alias from `Complete`, or admitting a zero-row transform primitive as production evidence; volatile append regeneration on exact retry; independent per-ID Committed transitions for one actor batch; recomputing old StoredDigest under a current parser; accepting an old handler whose generic type cannot implement its selected callable effect contract; arbitrary effect-capable DI sinks outside the transaction/provider; counting the 64 MiB page and proof limits as separate additions to the 128 MiB live scratch budget; public replay records that expose internal types or raw mutable scratch; in-place named-projection rows visible before checkpoint pointer commit; friendly state-store name as backend identity; signed timeline chunks without an implemented/proved protocol; mutable publisher configuration as committed route authority; raw event bytes as proof of historic encoding ID; a multi-type handler inferred from its primary type alone; one lease for several logical handlers; partial-batch MessageId retry acceptance; plaintext or unmanaged spool, unzeroed cross-tenant pooled scratch, unprotected/unscoped response blobs, declared-only external dedup provider, precheck-only lease expiry, new nonce after uncertain broker acceptance, cross-mode raw-byte equality requirement, hashing unexpanded option defaults; broker-attempt ID as a stable handoff key; unfenced cross-store generation reads; case-insensitive V2 spelling admission; a final-page-only effective proof for multi-page commands; a caller-controlled consumer lease; unreserved pool rounding; runtime edits in Story 6.5; CLR names as public identity or arbitrary type loading; generic V1 version default; ordinary history rewrite; upcast at publication followed by another at subscription; DTO-only attestation or generic object publication; local/tenant-only MessageId uniqueness; standalone effect reservation; skip/ack past projection poison; unbounded whole-array replay/`GetEventsAsync(0)`; treating a page/token as complete history; trusting a free snapshot object; key expiry as blanket verification permission; AOT/trimming assertion; Epic 8 as prerequisite. **Open decisions: none.** Any newly discovered incompatible historical/provider fact blocks readiness and requires an explicitly approved amendment or offline migration, not ad hoc 6.6 behavior.

Fixed known-answer **codec framing** vectors follow. These small records test
exact bytes and hash framing; zero-field registry, transform and delivery
records are deliberately semantically inadmissible and MUST still fail
production validation. Python `hashlib` and Node.js `crypto` independently
recomputed every SHA-256 value; Python `cryptography` produced the fixed
signature and Node.js `crypto.verify` independently accepted it. Story 6.6
also tests full admitted event fixtures listed above.

Raw `eventstore.protection` selector for JSON string `"a"` and escaped `"\u0061"` is identically `020000000161`; empty string is `0200000000`, null `01`, absent `00`; Unicode normalization is not performed. |

The all-zero bitmap is a framing fixture, not valid event presence. |

### 11.1 Admitted one-event V1 and signed interoperability fixture

Unlike the zero-record framing vectors above, this fixture has a registered V1 alias and an active complete one-event route. The raw V1 source has valid ULID-shaped MessageId, AggregateId and correlation/causation IDs, stored metadata version 1, absent canonical pair and null extensions. The exact raw JSON bytes are V17SourceJsonUtf8Hex below; its payload base64 is e30= (UTF-8 {}), provider encoding ID is json, and raw protection extension is absent. The exact alias is (d, Legacy.Event) -> (evt, source version 1, json), with no payload identity claim under its registered NoPayloadIdentity policy; the addressed envelope still binds tenant t, domain d, aggregate type x and aggregate ID. D current version is 1, so this is a verified zero-hop fixture. Handler route (d, route) consumes evt on d-events and uses AtomicStore. Active RegistryFingerprint is V17RegistryHash. Test key test-key is trusted for purposes 01 through 04 and 06 over UTC ticks 630822816000000000 through 662380416000000000. The key is the fixed P-256 public SPKI already shown above, with fixture private scalar 1 used only to generate signatures. Purpose-02, purpose-04 and purpose-06 claims sign issuance UTC `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z` (Q bytes `08de48c8b4f80000`), within that key interval. The checkpoint uses coordinator `fixture-fence`, generation 1, state operation `op` and state version `etag1` under the shared fence. The source route and prefix fixture does not exercise a command processor, so it has no purpose-07 key or command-state proof. The fixture implementation-file bytes are ASCII fixture-assembly followed by LF; every assembly H below is their SHA-256. The fixture options manifest is the exact sorted UTF-8 JSON represented by V17OptionsTextUtf8Hex, including converter, reader, serializer, signer and validator settings; every options H is the domain-separated hash of V17OptionsCanonical below. Test descriptors D/V/A/S and route R use the exact §5 field tables with those H values and the following IDs: aggregate route r, current CLR type Fixture.Event, Fixture, Apply apply, state schema 1 bytes {}, serializer j, V validator schema, V identity no-payload-identity, A validator alias-schema and decoder noop; S component IDs raw, chain, json, reader, protection, verifier, signer, publisher, reservation, renderer; route handler, effect and readback IDs handler, effect and readback. No E or F row is needed. All raw, manifest, transform and claim encodings are literal, not placeholders.

The fixture proof container is a complete replay from sequence 1 with one route entry, one prefix entry and checkpoint discriminator `00`; its prefix checkpoint-anchor field remains absent. `V17CheckpointAnchorHash` separately exercises the exact checkpoint-entry hash for a later projection tail; this one-event replay does not claim that tail path. The encoding sidecar is signed with purpose 06 and checked against the same raw JSON bytes before the V1 StoredDigest is admitted.

They are the exact inputs for §4–§7 hashing and signing; the byte lengths of RegistryBytes, TransformBytes, RouteClaim, PrefixClaim, CheckpointClaim, DeliveryBody and DeliveryClaim are respectively 1723, 1503, 295, 213, 351, 842 and 223. The batch row witnesses one present (`01`) upsert of canonical readback bytes {} at (store, key), sequence 1, operation op, resulting version etag1. The purpose-06 sidecar binds the exact V1 raw bytes to provider encoding ID json and namespace dapr-state at the actor event key; its key is present in the TrustMapDigest. The checkpoint claim binds its BatchStateReadbackHash, signed issuance UTC and shared fence identity/generation/state operation/version; a missing row or stale fence would reject completion. V1 routing headers derive evt and 1 from the alias while the signed delivery body keeps both stored pair fields absent. Reproduction: decode the SourceJsonUtf8Hex, render and bitmap it under §4, and compare CanonicalRaw and StoredDigest. Decode RegistryBytes, TransformBytes, HandlerRow and the four claims with the fixed field tables; reject wrong counts, tags, order, options or alias. Recompute each listed SHA-256 from its literal input bytes. Parse Spki as P-256 SPKI and verify each signature over the §6 signature input using test-key and purposes route 01, prefix 03, checkpoint 04, delivery 02, encoding evidence 06. Decode ProofContainer under §6 and compute CheckpointAnchorHash from the exact signed checkpoint entry. Check the exact one-event prefix list and accumulator against StoredDigest, the batch row hash against the checkpoint claim, and the decoded Binary attestation against DeliveryClaim and DeliverySignature. Python hashlib/cryptography generated these values; independent Node.js crypto code rerendered SourceJsonUtf8Hex, recomputed StoredDigest and the listed byte hashes, verified all five fixed P1363 signatures and rejected one-byte tampering. Both runs passed for this revision. A production verifier additionally checks the active registry/trust, current key, provider readback, admission limits and route/effect readiness; a framing-only zero-row vector above never passes those checks.

```bash
if(!B(v.transform_bytes).equals(transformExpected)) throw Error('transform row order/bytes');
```

### 11.2 Compact V2, one-hop and protected-source byte vectors

These are additional admitted evidence shapes, derived from the signed V17 fixture under the exact §4/§5/§6 codecs; the one-hop route is a separate registered test manifest and is not signed by V17's zero-hop registry key. `V20V2RawJson` is literal UTF-8 (no final newline); its `eventTypeName=evt`, `metadataVersion=2`, `eventContractType=evt` and `payloadVersion=1` form a valid V2 pair under V17's current-version-1 D/V descriptor. The V2 bitmap covers both value pair members while retaining the absent raw protection position. The one-hop manifest retains V17 A/S/V1 rows, changes D current version to 2, adds the literal V2 row and E row below, and uses zero G rows. E registers deterministic `fixture-default-n` with exact `json` input `{}` and output `{"n":1}`, a version-2 schema accepting that output, and the same explicit `NoPayloadIdentity` policy. The hop's route claim uses V17's immutable V1 StoredDigest/consumed metadata and addressed scope, target `(evt,2,json)`, this manifest fingerprint and SHA-256 of the exact output; `V20OneHopRouteClaimHash` is SHA-256 of its exact §6 claim bytes. A separate dependency-row vector appends one selected G row after the protection adapter, changing the row count from five to six and the transform hash; it exercises the placement rule without altering V17’s signed manifest. These values are independent of the signed V17 route, which correctly remains target version 1.

For protected-source evidence, start from the exact V17 JSON source and replace `extensions:null` with `extensions:{"eventstore.protection":"<scalar>"}` where `<scalar>` is the decoded UTF-8 string given below, serialized as one JSON string member. `V20Protected` uses a test registered bounded `fixture` protection adapter whose readable result is `{}`; the source's original scalar remains unchanged and is included in StoredDigest even after unprotect. `V20ProviderOpaque` uses an unsupported-state scalar; its derived version-1 `ProviderOpaque` record has null scheme/key alias/content hint and flags `reason=unsupported-state`, while the source scalar remains unchanged. ProviderOpaque is source evidence and a typed read hold, never a fabricated readable payload or Apply. Both use V17's exact original raw body fields, provider encoding ID `json`, scope and purpose-06 sidecar binding; only the extension field differs. The expected hashes below use the complete canonical raw renderer, exact decoded protection scalar selector, and derived protection-record hash. The independent verifier checks all bytes and hashes.

### 11.3 Signed broker authority and lifecycle known-answer fixture

This **historical V23 one-member codec fixture** uses domain `d`, component `pub`, topic `d-events`, active consumer `consumer`, revision 7, the current domain RegistryFingerprint below, and one `DurableDedup` provider `dedup` on backend `store-a`. The test probe names a valid ULID-shaped MessageId, records two identical delivery attempts across a simulated restart and one committed effect. The fixture broker authority uses the P-256 test private scalar 2 and `broker-test-key` for purposes 08, 09 and 0a; its SPKI below is distinct from V17's event-trust key. The test authority trusts only purposes 08..0a from `2025-01-01T00:00:00Z` through `2030-01-01T00:00:00Z` and is not revoked. Claim issued UTC ticks are `639028224000000000` and expiry ticks are `639029088000000000`; the fence expires at that earliest lease/membership bound. These are test-only fixed bytes and a V1 probe framing example, not production authority configuration or a production-readiness probe; §7 requires the crash/two-route V3 receipt and independent provider query. Python `cryptography` generated the fixed P1363 signatures; the independent Node verifier below parses every record and carrier, recomputes hashes/linkage, checks scope/fingerprint/expiry and rejects one-byte signed-input tampering. An omitted `converters` field and its explicit `[]` default expand to identical V17 canonical options bytes and the unchanged V17 OptionsHash; the three literal V23 option values below exercise the rule. Run this standalone verifier from the repository root; it reads the literal lines above and checks exact tags, lengths, field order, no trailing bytes, member/config/probe hashes, domain fingerprint, lease/fence expiry, purpose-specific fixed-key signatures and tamper rejection:

```bash
node <<'NODE'
const fs = require('node:fs');
const crypto = require('node:crypto');
const md = fs.readFileSync(process.argv[2] || '_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-event-versioning-upcasting.md', 'utf8');
function literal(name) {
  const hit = md.match(new RegExp('^V23' + name + '=([0-9a-f]+)$', 'm'));
  if (!hit) throw Error('missing literal ' + name);
  return Buffer.from(hit[1], 'hex');
}
function eq(a, b, why) { if (!Buffer.from(a).equals(Buffer.from(b))) throw Error(why); }
function yes(v, why) { if (!v) throw Error(why); }
function sha(x) { return crypto.createHash('sha256').update(x).digest(); }
function u(x) { const b = Buffer.from(x, 'utf8'); const n = Buffer.alloc(4); n.writeUInt32BE(b.length); return Buffer.concat([n,b]); }
function bytes(x) { const n = Buffer.alloc(4); n.writeUInt32BE(x.length); return Buffer.concat([n,x]); }
function parse(buf, separator, types) {
  let pos = 0;
  function take(n) { if (n < 0 || pos + n > buf.length) throw Error('truncated'); const x = buf.subarray(pos,pos+n); pos += n; return x; }
  function value(type) {
    if (type === 'U' || type === 'B') { const n=take(4).readUInt32BE(0); const x=take(n); if(type==='U') { const t=new TextDecoder('utf-8',{fatal:true}).decode(x); eq(Buffer.from(t),x,'noncanonical UTF-8'); return t; } return x; }

    if (type === 'N' || type === 'Q') return take(8).readBigInt64BE(0);
    if (type === 'I') return take(4).readInt32BE(0);
```

The Story 6.6 provider tests additionally exercise a lease expiring after publisher precheck but before broker acceptance, revision/fingerprint change, ambiguous acceptance followed by `GetPublicationReceipt`, changed bytes under one operation ID, same-mode exact retry, and canonical Binary-to-structured conversion. They inspect durable receipt, pin and effect state and assert that an unresolved broker query sends no new nonce or bytes. Scratch, encrypted spool and response-blob cleanup/crash/access tests inspect ownership, readback and deletion without printing payloads.

Review-34 production vectors complete the closure: deliver one authenticated binary body to a physical subscription with two addressed logical HandlerRouteIds, crash after the first route receipt, and prove the broker remains unacknowledged until the second route reaches durable Completed or its authenticated out-of-scope Filtered result. Redeliver after each crash and verify one effect per route, exact manifest/route-set equality and no second effect; change a route ID, pin byte or membership revision and assert conflict without acknowledgement. Exercise `ProjectVerifiedAsync` against Completed with valid/absent state, AlreadyCompleted with present/missing durable receipt, Retryable, Indeterminate, Failed and absent route; assert exactly the §3 response or typed HTTP status and no unearned checkpoint. Drive handler and `SharedProjectionEpochCoordinator` through the same `IVersionedNamedProjectionBatchWriter` with correct and forged capability, wrong key-space, stale root, stale fence and mismatched six-field legacy scope; only a certified pointer exposes rows. Crash after actor save and before publication, then after publication and before public-response acknowledgement; the append result remains byte-identical, a `PublishFailed` public outcome never overwrites it, and exact retry returns only A8's revision-zero first POST pin. Test zero-event no-op under the same boundaries.

For V1, admit a newly written event with branch-01 actor-save certificate and **no** offline manifest, and a retained event with branch-02 independently signed manifest/docket/sidecar; swap branch or event key and assert `LegacyEvidenceConflict` without changing raw bytes. Change one purpose-0d/0e SPKI, interval, revocation or signer/reviewer identity-policy byte and assert `MigrationAuthorityDigest` parity hold while the historical V17 signed claim bytes remain unchanged. At 1,000,000 finite leaves update one key and verify only its expiry job is registered; race stale-root TTL rebase with replacement, saturate 1 GiB job index and 1 GiB hot ordinal log, seal 64 MiB segments and replay across a 64 GiB archive cap with no skipped ordinal or early segment deletion. Issue 100,000 query capabilities and exhaust the 128 MiB tenant index; reject the next issuance, then expire/delete one under ambiguous CAS and prove quota is released only after exact readback. Parse memberships at 1 MiB/1 MiB+1, 4,096/4,097 members and 4 KiB/member; parse external route sets at 256 KiB/256 KiB+1 and 1,024/1,025 rows, and whole carriers at 2 MiB/2 MiB+1 before nested allocation. Commit a multi-event actor batch once, verify every per-member inclusion path against its certified root on publish/duplicate without rereading sibling events, tamper one sidecar/result/sibling/count and assert hold; an exact append retry still requires full-batch equality. Preserve all literal V17/V20/V22/V23 fixture inputs, hashes and signatures ; validate the current §12 owner approval. These vectors inspect durable state, hashes, actor certificates, broker acknowledgements, route receipts and public bytes, not only an HTTP result.

### A10. Dispositions and verification vectors

The BH37 dispositions are recorded once, in the §11.5 register. The vector IDs V01–V24 below are A10's own and unrelated to the signed fixture families V17, V20, V22 and V23 of §11.1–§11.3; this document cites them as A10 V01–V24.

These are future implementation acceptance vectors, not claims that runtime tests were added/run. Each requires authenticated durable state and exact bytes, no second append/domain invocation where forbidden, and allocation counters/provider fault injection where applicable. A status code or mocked call count alone cannot pass.

### 11.6 Integrated child known answers

These literal values fix the codecs that this document adopts from the children. Their exact inputs are defined in the cited models (§11.4); they are local codec answers, not provider or admitted-domain fixtures. C1 carries its four BH37-9 delivery digests and its four `destinationId` known answers inline, and [I-26] carries the integrated capacity known answer. The K02 and K07 fixtures stage marker keys (`batch-member-root:op`, `aggregate-operation-result:op`) that do not follow the A5 and §7 key derivations; they fix framing and hash arithmetic only, and obligation O-01 governs the production keys.

# Story 6.5d obligations and exact wire reference

This file is normative supporting documentation for the compact candidate. Archived reviewed defect evidence is preserved unchanged; replacement targets below describe the new contract, without making archived local model mechanisms binding. All listed local function proofs use fixture authorization/transactions only; production cryptography and provider crash behavior require D9's approved runtime gate. Each row separates the concrete local case from the remaining runtime proof; a function name is not evidence for unmodeled provider behavior.

| E2-38 | replacement; archived D1 plus archived D2–archived D11 give G-B, G-E, and G-I storage, bounds, activation, inventory, owner, and exits. | D1–D8 lifecycle table, one-owner phases and ledger queue; four executed frozen matrix scenario groups, with actual provider proofs retained explicitly in D9 |

## Exact retained binary framing and schemas

All external records use ASCII domain including one final NUL, codec byte 01, big-endian u16 field count, then one-byte tags 01..count ascending and the ordered typed fields below. U is u32 UTF-8 byte count plus exact bytes, B is u32 byte count plus bytes, B32 exactly 32 bytes, N nonnegative checked u64, P u32, I signed i32, Q signed i64 UTC ticks. O(X) is 00 absent or 01 plus X; no null variant. Reject duplicate/missing/extra/reordered tags, invalid UTF-8, negative/overflow/count inconsistency or trailing bytes before allocation. Ordinary identifiers ≤1,024 UTF-8 bytes, Operator subject ≤256. Imported C1/C2/C5 signatures, P-256/P1363 carrier, purpose/issuer/SPKI/time/revocation are unchanged. Purpose 2d is activation, resume/window and redrive only; first-send resolution keeps purpose 2a.

Table field order is exact tag order; types are given in parentheses. The fixture hex is literal in known-answers.json and independently reconstructed without running the archived verifier. Dynamic roots below have semantic definitions; opaque fixture hashes are identified in the descriptors, never claimed provider proofs.

Drain state pending/unknown/failed; resolution outcome resumed/head-advanced/terminal. Member resolution disposition ContinueSamePin/FirstSendMembershipChangedHold. Charge kind pin-batch/side-record/retained-object/oversize-quarantine/resume-window; state staged/active/released. Transferred marker 0 means absent owner, marker 1 means resume-window with present same stable owner in every generation, including released; successor-readback activates stage; the retained predecessor stays charged until fixed-horizon exact artifact deletion/readback, which releases it exactly once. Counter kind tenant/capture-scope/tenant-pool/deployment/unidentified; tenant counter ID may contain `tenant:` plus 1,024 bytes (1,031 maximum), other IDs ≤1,024. Pin-batch state reserved/installed/released; root SHA256(exact uncounted rows), pinCount equals row count and total checked sum. Subscription relation initial/successor (generation 1 initial, later successor), capture mode dead-letter-capture/direct-held-capture; dead-letter topic present only for first mode; source dapr-configuration/broker-api. Quarantine reason invalid-header-value/invalid-carrier/oversize-carrier, disposition terminal-quarantine; backend ≤1,024 and key ≤4,096. Capsule classification success-events/rejection-events, cleanup drain-exhaustion/operator-reconciliation; positive count exactly end-start+1. Signed resume eligibility is exactly retry-exhausted/drain-limit/drain-limit-and-retry-exhausted/legacy-publish-failed. Legacy signed request scope/A8head and window invocation claim hash are zero; no fabricated A8 authority.

Nested exact payloads: activation rows `u32 count ||` sorted `U route || U disposition || N count || N readable || N accounting || O(B32 incrementalCapability)`; hash present exactly for incremental. Pin rows `u32 position || U MessageId || B32 pin || N length || N amount`, counted by pinCount (no inner count). Closure summary `u32 count ||` sorted `u32 position || N finalLocalAttempt || B32 lastDefinitiveResult`. Attempt rows `u32 position || N localOrdinal || N observationOrdinal || U register|unknown|result || B32 parent || B32 sendId || B32 evidence`, counted by evidenceCount; sorted first three fields, every attempt starts registration/0, optional Unknown/1 then definitive result, contiguous attempts/no Accepted successor. Semantic root SHA256(`"HX-EV-WINDOW-ATTEMPTS-2\0" || 01 || U tenant || B32 scope || N window || B32 roster || N count || B rows`). Window unresolved root SHA256(`"HX-EV-PUBLICATION-UNRESOLVED-1\0" || 01 || u32 count ||` sorted `u32 position || U MessageId || B32 committedByteHash`). History successor SHA256(`"HX-EV-PUBLICATION-WINDOW-HISTORY-1\0" || 01 || B32 previous || B exactClosure || B exactBrokerAuthentication`). Neither window nor audit includes successor control hash.

Capsule rows `N sequence || U MessageId || B32 StoredDigest` ascending unique contiguous sequence/MessageId. Chunk root SHA256(`"HX-EV-LEGACY-RESUME-CHUNK-ROWS-1\0" || 01 || B exactRows`). Manifest `u32 chunkCount ||` sorted `N ordinal || N firstSequence || N rowCount || B32 chunkHash || N encodedLength || U chunkAddress`; exact endpoints/count/length and no gaps/overlap/trailing bytes. Event root SHA256(`"HX-EV-LEGACY-RESUME-EVENTS-2\0" || 01 || B(u32 totalCount || all exactRows)`). Quarantine header manifest `u32 count ||` ≤128 rows `U headerName || N valueLength || B32 valueHash`; aggregate names/value lengths ≤64 KiB, exact worst encoded manifest 71,172 bytes, no raw forbidden value. AuthMode exactly SignedCarrier/BackendCas with unchanged C5 authentication framing and source order. C1 destinationId, imported A/B/C public bytes and signature carrier remain byte-identical and are referenced directly in the unchanged 6.5c C1/C2/C5 definitions.

## Evidence and independent checks

Run verify.py directly. Its byte snapshots restart Store from serialized canonical bytes, not returned process dictionaries. Literal frames are reconstructed independently during authoring and match all 23 previously published retained digests (plus newly exposed caller carrier), then checked by the verifier's separate frame implementation. Internal controls have complete literal JSON/hex/digest answers, including the bounded registry header, independently addressed entry/scope header and operations epoch. Every control literal declares its fixed maxBytes; the epoch literal validates exact fields, positive epoch/generation, canonical 26-character ULID ownerFence and the 60-second lease clock. The model does not prove backend lease acquisition, fencing or metric emission. codec_cases checks registry subject decoder/key agreement at 1,024/1,025 UTF-8 bytes, including multibyte values. The shared command-execution-scope exception has its own unframed literal in sharedKeys. All retained key families have exact framed literals, including capacity subject, claim, policy, window, invocation, destination and scope usage/head variants. Fixed maxBytes values are checked against the parsed normative byte ceilings below in both Python and the independent Node constructor, and mutated deep-copy answers run the actual verify_answers check. Corrupted literal digest/framing/cap metadata, exceeded control cap, illegal legacy ordinal transition, bad queue ticket and invalid accepted partition each fail their owning assertion/decoder. These are a bounded owning behavior set, not a per-guard mutation sweep or proof every guard is mutation-covered. Actual mutation of a fixture expected result must fail its scenario assertion; tests do not mirror source text.

Native auth strings beginning fixture-provider-only and fixture-purpose-2d-only establish deterministic test authorization only. Production requires approved profile, actual signatures and separately authenticated provider readback. Protected frozen intent/archive SHA audits and source/path audit belong to the parent acceptance pass. All AD-13/unapproved/source/runtime/test files remain unchanged.


## Focused post-simplification correction evidence

PD1–PD5 and FP1–FP24 (except parent-owned FP19 evidence/trackers) are implemented within the same execution/held owners, registry and queue. The executable groups codec_cases, status_replay_cases, resume_cases, legacy_cases, held_cases and queue_scope_inventory_cases inspect serialized persisted bytes and compute actual persisted owner ordinals/redrive counts and register matrix evidence only after its covering assertions pass. Legacy covers missing capsule, exact same capsule/range/MessageIds, successful-audit ordinal authority, non-failed ordinal preservation, typed evidence repair, later exhaustion, 1,000 maximum-width rows, and capsule cleanup byte restarts before/after original-drain deletion with unchanged refusal on a contradictory source. It also checks live-drain restore byte restarts before/after the external write and after advancement, same-ordinal lost-ack repeats without duplicate advancement, exact original range/MessageIds/classification, wrong owner/ordinal, contradictory readback and altered intent refusal. Resume covers intent recovery after accepted progress, before/after irreversible cancellation/expiry, 64 concurrent outcomes, pending-identity reclamation exclusion and old-charge deletion/refund deadlines. Held covers tenant/deployment account isolation, lost acknowledgement, correctly fixture-signed foreign held-identity refusals at both send and repair with all persisted bytes unchanged, corrupt/absent repair, backoff/count/identity/UTC refusal, observed-route success and distinct delivered versus erasure cleanup. Queue covers tenant blocking, deployment no-bypass, parking after current-overhead rerender, whole net grants, malformed materialization, ticket exhaustion, and unchanged stable arithmetic/evidence refusal. Inventory covers registry capacity, placeholder authority, owner-churn continuation, registry-change conflict, expired/invalid/cross-scope cursors and per-row unavailable evidence.

PD4 defines the adapter/owner-fence/epoch and AD/AD-26 handoff in D1/D8/D9; this is settled policy awaiting an architecture amendment and actual provider gate, not a fixture claim. FW1's automatic CI integration and exact signed/provider authority remain runtime gates. Existing C2 permanent class-02/03 member fences continue to govern drain-only dispatch. Candidate/model storage pressure is reported with actual sizes by parent acceptance; bounds and necessary cases take precedence over the design-pressure target.
